News.title: Lindsay Clancy’s lawsuit against doctors hits roadblock after they make under-the-radar move during her murder trial
News.content:
LINDSAY Clancy’s psychiatrist – who faced a brutal grilling on the stand during her murder trial – is fighting back against a civil lawsuit filed by the mom who killed her three children.

Dr. Jennifer Tufts, who treated Clancy for severe mental health issues before she strangled her kids, is demanding a medical malpractice tribunal to decide whether the negligence case against her stacks up.



The move would see a panel including medical and legal experts scrutinize Tufts’ treatment of Clancy and decide whether there is evidence she failed her patient in the months before the horrific killings.

Documents obtained by The U.S. Sun reveal the legal move was made in Norfolk Superior Court in Massachusetts as Clancy’s blockbuster criminal trial plays out around 40 miles away in Plymouth.



Clancy filed the medical malpractice lawsuit in January 2026, accusing Tufts and other healthcare professionals and organizations involved in her care of failing to properly recognize and treat her deteriorating psychiatric condition before the killings.

Tufts began treating Clancy in September 2022 and saw her 14 times over nearly five months, with her final appointment taking place on January 23, 2023 – the day before the violence.

She never met the mom in person and all of their appointments were conducted virtually.

Clancy is accused of strangling Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan with exercise bands and leaving them in the basement of the family’s Duxbury home.

She then jumped from a second-story window in a failed suicide attempt that left her paralyzed.

The horrific scene was discovered by her husband at the time, Patrick, who had been out running errands.



Clancy’s defense argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors maintain she planned the murders and committed them in cold blood.

Tufts has since emerged as a key figure in the case that has gripped the nation, with her treatment of Clancy coming under intense scrutiny during the trial.

But while attention has been focused on the dramatic scenes unfolding in the courtroom, the psychiatrist has quietly been fighting a parallel legal battle behind the scenes.

If Tufts’ request is granted, the tribunal would bring in experts to look at her treatment of Clancy and decide whether there is enough evidence to back up Clancy’s claims.

Tufts insists there isn’t – and is hitting back hard at the psychiatrist Clancy has brought in to make her case.



Dr. Whaley claims Tufts should have spotted signs that Clancy may have been suffering from bipolar disorder with psychotic features before the killings.

But Tufts’ lawyers argue there were no clear warning signs at the time, pointing out that Clancy repeatedly denied wanting to kill herself or anyone else and said she was not experiencing hallucinations.

They accuse Whaley of looking back at her behavior through the lens of what later happened to the children, dismissing his conclusions as “speculation and retrospective analysis.”



Whaley has also criticized the medication Clancy was given, claiming she should have been treated with a mood stabilizer or antipsychotic.

Tufts’ lawyers hit back that she did prescribe lamotrigine, which is used as a mood stabilizer, and say overlooking that key detail leaves his opinion “fatally flawed.”

The filing comes after defense attorney Kevin Reddington spent hours grilling Tufts at Clancy’s murder trial over many of the same issues now being fought over in civil court.

Tufts had an impressive academic background but was still early in her career as a psychiatrist when Clancy landed in her care.

She studied psychology at Cornell University, went to medical school at the University of Vermont and completed her psychiatry residency at Boston Medical Center.



But she had only finished her residency in July 2022 and was just starting out in private practice when she began treating Clancy – something Reddington seized on during his blistering cross-examination.

He grilled Tufts over her experience with serious postpartum conditions and at one point likened her approach to that of a box-checking “robot.”

Reddington also hammered home that Tufts never once met Clancy face-to-face.



He questioned why she had not obtained complete records from her other doctors and highlighted that the mom had called a suicide hotline twice – something Tufts admitted she did not know.

Reddington then picked apart her prescribing decisions, including increasing Clancy’s Amitriptyline shortly before the killings, suggesting the change had “pushed her over the edge.”

Tufts fired back, “I don’t think so.”

And in another striking exchange, she told the court, “I do not believe that I’ve been negligent.”

The psychiatrist is one of 11 defendants – seven individual medical or mental health professionals and four healthcare organizations – named in Clancy’s civil lawsuit.



Her ex-husband Patrick, who has also taken the stand during her criminal trial, separately filed a wrongful death lawsuit in January on behalf of himself and the estates of their three children.

His case names four defendants – Tufts, nurse practitioner Rebecca Jollotta, Aster Mental Health and South Shore Health System – all of whom also face claims in Lindsay’s case.

Patrick alleges those responsible for Lindsay’s care failed the family through allegedly uncoordinated prescribing and failures to respond appropriately as her mental health deteriorated.

Tufts has also asked a judge to dismiss Patrick’s case, leaving her fighting civil claims from both sides of the shattered Clancy family as the murder trial continues to unfold.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Her requests in both civil cases remain pending.



If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

News.title: Baby hauled alive from rubble & pool cleaner praying for his life… more jaw-dropping footage from Colombia quake emerges
News.content:
A BABY has been pulled alive from the rubble as dramatic new footage emerges of the devastating earthquake in Colombia.

The footage shows rescue workers digging beneath a collapsed building before carefully clearing debris to reveal a man cradling a baby in his arms.



The rescuers painstakingly freed the tiny infant from the man’s grasp and carried him to safety.

Moments earlier, Brian Osorio Zuluaga had left his office in Cali and was making his way home when he was forced to stop near the remains of a five-storey apartment complex.



As he approached the rubble, he heard sounds coming from beneath the wreckage and called out to see if anyone was trapped inside.

“Yes, I’m here. I’m with a baby,” a man replied.



Zuluaga and a group of men immediately began clearing the debris, but their efforts were hampered when they encountered a huge concrete slab.

“On the first attempt, we couldn’t lift it,” he told CNN.



After coordinating their movements, the men managed to clear a safe path to the trapped man and baby.

“You can see the baby’s little head there, which, at the time, looked sort of purplish because he couldn’t breathe,” Osorio said.

“Once we started removing the rubble, the baby began to … breathe, and his colour started to come back.”

The baby boy was quickly handed to a police officer, who whisked him to safety while the rescuers continued working to free the man.

Elsewhere, emergency workers continued searching through the rubble for signs of life.



Fire Chief Camilo Cano said more than 20 people had been rescued from a collapsed apartment complex at Torres del Limonar in the first 12 hours after the quake.

Three more survivors were later pulled from the wreckage, he said, but large crowds of volunteers initially made the search more difficult.

“We cannot concentrate and hear the calls of people under the structure,” Cano said.



Police have since imposed tighter controls, directing volunteers to specific tasks so rescuers can work more effectively.

Among those anxiously waiting for news was Marcela Perez, who said her partner’s 11-year-old daughter was trapped with her grandparents when the building collapsed.

“We have been here since Monday waiting for the girl to be rescued, and for her grandparents too,” Perez said.

“We are just waiting and trusting in God.”

Hundreds of buildings collapsed as the South American country was hit by a huge 7.4-magnitude earthquake on Monday morning – one of its largest in years.



So far, 254 people have been confirmed dead and nearly 2,600 left injured, officials said.

The death toll is likely to rise, with many feared trapped under collapsed buildings.

Striking at a depth of 64 miles in Chocó province, the quake was felt across a huge area – stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia, as far as Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, 750 miles away, and in Ecuador and Panama.



Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella said 1,000 members of the security forces have been deployed to Cali following reports of looting.

The natural disaster is proving to be an early test for the president who was only inaugurated on Friday.

On Tuesday, he flew to Pereira, accompanied by his wife, the first lady Ana Lucía Pineda, to inspect one of the worst-hit areas.

“My commitment is to each and every one of the affected families,” the president wrote on X.

“We remain on the ground, working for our people.”



US secretary of state Marco Rubio said America “stands ready to support” the country.

The US Department of State described the disaster as “devastating” and pledged £11.5million to help provide emergency shelter and supplies.

The EU is also providing funding and supporting rescue operations, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Colombian government announced an immediate emergency rent subsidy for all those who had lost their homes.

The quake follows two back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes in Venezuela in late June.

News.title: Moment huge blaze burns next to rail tracks as trains cancelled and black plume of smoke floats into sky
News.content:
SHOCKING footage shows the moment a huge blaze burned next to a railway station, sparking travel chaos with trains cancelled.

The Royal Berkshire Fire and Rescue service scrambled to the scene on Brunel Way in Slough, and started tackling the blaze just after 4pm today.



Footage from the scene showed thick smoke billowing into the sky with the fire service warning people to avoid the area if possible.

Multiple fire crews swooped on the area to tackle the blaze with eyewitnesses claiming at least twelve fire engines were on the scene.



Trains running to and from Slough and Windsor & Eton Central have been cancelled, sparking rush hour chaos for commuters.

There will be no train services between the stations until approximately 8pm due to the blaze, according to National Rail.

The blaze occurred in an industrial building, said the fire service.

Residents who live nearby were also warned to close doors and windows for their safety by the fire brigade.



Travellers planning a train journey on lines running through Slough have been warned to check for “potential delays”.

Local bus routes can be used instead by train passengers who can show their ticket to the driver.

A GWR spokesperson said: “Due to a fire on property near the railway between Slough and Windsor & Eton Central the line is blocked.

“Disruption is expected until 20:00.”

A spokesperson for Royal Berkshire Fire and Rescue said in a full statement: “At 4:02pm on Wednesday, 12 August, we received reports of a fire on Brunel Way in Slough.



“Royal Berkshire Fire and Rescue Service crews from Slough, Langley, Maidenhead and Windsor fire stations have been sent to the scene.

“A crew from Buckinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service has also been sent to the scene.

“Crews remain at the scene at this time. Please avoid the area while our crews respond to this incident.

“If you live locally, please keep doors and windows closed.”

It comes after a huge fire broke out at an industrial estate sending clouds of black smoke into the sky and causing a major A-road out of London to close.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Around 100 firefighters and 15 fire engines raced to the scene to battle the blaze on Ripple Road, Barking.

A section of the A13 from London to the M25 and Essex was closed following the fire.

News.title: Bus driver, 25, shot dead outside pub is pictured after being in ‘wrong place at wrong time’ as man, 22, arrested
News.content:
A BUS driver who was gunned down outside a London pub had a “gentle heart” and “wouldn’t hurt a soul”, his heartbroken pals said.

Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa, 25, known in the area as “Billy”, was arriving back home from work at Stockwell bus garage before he was killed on Monday night.



Cops and paramedics scrambled to the Landor Pub in Clapham, just before 10pm after receiving reports of gunfire.

Despite paramedics arriving within three minutes, he was pronounced dead at the scene and a 22-year-old was arrested on suspicion of murder.



Auguste was tragically in the “wrong place at the wrong time”, according to friends.

Speaking today at the scene, a close pal who grew up with Auguste said: “He was coming back from work to see his mum.

“He wasn’t dropping off his girlfriend. He lived just opposite with his mum.

“He lived opposite on the estate with her and was just parking up to get home. We think he was either followed or targeted by mistake.



“He was sitting in his car and was just about to get out to walk home.

“It happened right outside where he lives so I immediately messaged him on Snapchat to find out if he was okay.

“He didn’t reply for a few minutes which is unusual and I thought something had happened.

“I fell to my knees when I found out it was him. He didn’t deserve any of this.”

A police forensics tent remained in place across the road yesterday, while several bouquets of flowers were laid and a candle lit outside the pub.



Detective Chief Inspector Claire Guiver, who is leading the investigation, said: “Our thoughts remain with Bile-aka’s family as they come to terms with this tragic incident.

“We continue to appeal for anyone with information to come forward.

“If you were in the area at the time of the shooting, witnessed anything suspicious or have any CCTV, dashcam or doorbell footage that could assist our investigation, we urge you to get in touch.



“Any piece of information could prove vital in helping us piece together the full circumstances.”

Staff from The Landor are understood to have rushed to Auguste’s aid after the shooting.

Auguste’s pal added: “He had an incredibly kind and gentle heart and wouldn’t hurt a soul. He would never hurt anyone.

“He was proud of his job and who he became as a person. He had only started his life. He was an amazing man who was just very hardworking.

“He was always there for his friends and family who always put other first.”



Auguste, from Clapham, South London, had been a bus driver for about a year, friends said.

Today, a forensics team were seen trawling the floor just by the shooting step by step.

The Sun has seen CCTV footage showing a male wearing a moped helmet limping with “blood pouring out his mouth.”



It shows the man walking down a high road about a minute from the scene of the shooting.

A witness said: “The man shouted out: ‘I’ve been shot, I’ve been shot. I’ve been shot.

“He was walking away from the scene with a limp. He was holding his leg and there was blood pouring out his mouth.

“He looked very dazzled and out of it. He was on the phone grunting, calling for his friends to pick him up.”

The man, who did not want to be named, said he saw the man jump into a car which drove away before police arrived.



The male limping is understood to be the 22-year-old male who presented himself to hospital with a gunshot wound.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He was arrested on suspicion of murder.

This man remains in hospital under police guard.

News.title: Labour’s £3bn contract crackdown will hit pubs, care homes and youth jobs, bosses warn
News.content:
LABOUR’S crackdown on zero-hours contracts could cost business up to £3 billion, a damning government assessment reveals.

The party came to power with a pledge to ban “exploitative” zero-hours contracts as part of a new workers’ rights package.



But top bosses last night slammed the rising cost of taking on workers and said it will do further damage to the youth inactivity crisis.

The workers’ rights package has been spearheaded by former deputy PM and now Communities Secretary Angela Rayner.



The impact is set to be most concentrated in industries where demand is more variable including hospitality, the arts along with health and social care, government documents show.

Andrew Griffith, Shadow Business Secretary, said: “Labour’s jobs tax and employment red tape have been so damaging already, but this goes further and once again, it will be young people who will pay the price, during a growing crisis of young Brits out of work.”

Firms have had to deal with hikes to national insurance hikes and minimum wage increases adding to the burden on business since Labour came to power.

Kate Shoesmith, from the British Chamber of Commerce, said: “The increased cost to businesses of the proposed changes to zero hours contracts will be a further hammer blow for many firms struggling to keep their heads above water.

“The government had previously claimed that the cost of the entire Employment Rights Act for business would be £1bn but this research clearly blows that out of the water.

“Businesses have seen their costs due to government policy increase by 70 per cent in the last decade, and their ability to absorb more is extremely limited.



“We are already facing a youth unemployment crisis – now is not the time to make it even more costly for employers to hire.

Kate Nicholls, Chair of UKHospitality, said: “The eyewatering cost of these reforms comes at the worst possible time for hospitality businesses, arriving on the heels of more than £5 billion in additional employment costs in the past two years.

“More than 100,000 jobs have already been lost in hospitality as a result and the extraordinarily high cost of employment continues to restrict job opportunities, particularly for young people.”

Workers on zero-hours and low-hours contracts will get the right to guaranteed working hours from next year if they want them.

The government is consulting on whether to apply the policy to anyone working 48 hours a week, but its preference is for the threshold to be between eight and 20 hours.



Firms will also have to fork out if shifts have been cancelled or moved at short notice in a huge financial blow.

In a worst-case scenario, the right to guaranteed hours could cost firms £450 million.

Then the right to reasonable notice of shifts could cost £1.2 billion and the then £1.3 billion for the right to payments for shifts cancelled or moved.

In a best-case scenario, the overall direct cost to business could be £350 million.

No final decisions on what is deemed an exploitative zero hours contract or what reasonable notice should be given. The consultation runs until next week.



The planned reforms will still “support growth” by improving conditions for workers, an impact assessment said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A government spokesperson last night said: “We are absolutely committed to ending exploitative zero hours contracts, where workers bear all the financial risk when hours, shifts and earnings are unpredictable.

“These reforms will give workers in every postcode greater income security and predictability of hours and while no final decisions have been made, we’re consulting to get the detail right and ensure this works in the real world.”

News.title: What time is the Clacton by-election result? When to expect the winner announcement and full list of candidates
News.content:
CLACTON voters will soon discover who will be their next MP after a record-breaking by-election.

Polling stations open at 7am on Thursday, but the 34-candidate ballot means the count could run later than usual.



What time is the Clacton by-election result?

There is no guaranteed declaration time, but the result is expected before breakfast on Friday.

Reports say the winner should be known in the early hours, while the complicated count could push the announcement back to around 5am.



Once voting ends, ballot boxes from 51 polling stations must reach the count centre.

Officials verify that the number of papers matches the polling-station records before counting all votes.

That job may take longer than normal because Clacton’s ballot paper is almost a metre long.

Acting Returning Officer Ian Davidson said its record size created practical problems, including how staff would spread the sheets out while allowing candidates’ representatives to watch.

He explained: “Administratively, it’s about how we fit this ballot into the envelopes for postal voters, and – when the voters receive their postal votes – how they get it into an envelope and get it back to us because it is that long.

“We also have an issue for the counters, how we’re going to lay it out, how we’re going to ensure that those who are watching can see while at the same time managing these metre long ballot papers.



No exit poll is planned, so voters should not expect a 10pm projection.

When do polls close in Clacton?

Voting runs from 7am until 10pm on August 13.

The contest uses first past the post, so each elector chooses one candidate and the person with the most votes becomes MP – they don’t need to secure more than 50% of the vote.

The by-election was triggered when Nigel Farage resigned as Clacton’s MP on July 8, 2026.

Farage took 21,225 votes at the 2024 general election, finishing 8,405 ahead of Conservative runner-up Giles Watling.



Who are the Clacton by-election candidates?

A record-breaking 34 candidates are standing in a UK parliamentary election, beating the 26 in the Haltemprice and Howden by-election ballot in July 2008.

News.title: How long is the Clacton by-election ballot paper? Why it’s broken records and full list of candidates
News.content:
CLACTON voters face a record-breaking choice when they pick their next MP on Thursday.

The ballot paper for the August 13, 2026 by-election is around 3ft long after an unprecedented 34 candidates entered the race.



How long is the Clacton by-election ballot paper?

The Clacton by-election voting slip measures about 90cm from top to bottom — just short of a metre and longer than many people’s arms.

It includes Nigel Farage, Count Binface and three Official Monster Raving Loony Party hopefuls, as well as independents and smaller-party candidates.



Tendring District Council’s acting returning officer has said it is longer than any previous ballot paper used at a UK parliamentary election.

Its size has created practical problems before a single cross is cast.



Election staff have had to work out how to fold the paper into postal-vote envelopes, how voters will return it and how counters can spread the sheets out while observers can still see what’s going on.

Who are the Clacton by-election candidates?

Tendring District Council says 34 candidates is a UK parliamentary election record, beating the 26 who stood in the Haltemprice and Howden by-election in July 2008.

Why is the Clacton by-election happening?

Labour, the Conservatives, Liberal Democrats and Green Party are not fielding candidates, leaving a crowded mix of independents, minor parties and satirical challengers.

Anyone standing for Parliament must submit valid nomination papers supported by ten registered electors in the constituency and pay a £500 deposit.

The deposit is returned only if the candidate wins more than 5% of all valid votes cast.

News.title: Map reveals parts of UK with ZERO asylum seekers as Andy Burnham vows to send migrants to leafy middle-class suburbs
News.content:
MORE than a dozen local authorities house no taxpayer-backed asylum seekers, analysis shows – after Andy Burnham said more middle-class areas should take in migrants.

Our map reveals migrant hotspots across the country, with Glasgow, Hyndbyrn and Blackburn among the places supporting the most asylum seekers per capita.



Mr Burnham yesterday suggested that wealthier areas should take more people into dispersal accommodation.

He told GB News: “We cannot have a situation where it’s only the poorest communities in the country that receive all of the dispersal of refugees and asylum seekers.”



The PM added: “I do believe all parts of the country need to work, to play their part.”

Mr Burnham was responding to protests in Piddington, Oxfordshire, where the village of 350 people held a mock independence referendum over plans to house 1,000 asylum seekers at a MoD base.

Humans rights groups, the local council and MP Calum Miller have objected to the controversial plans for “Site A”.

The list of 17 areas, first compiled by the Daily Mail, shows posh areas like the Derbyshire Dales, the Isle of Wight and the Cotswolds house zero asylum seekers.

Migrants are more likely to be housed in areas with higher deprivation scores, a Government metric used to track poverty.

Areas with high numbers of asylum seekers and a high deprivation score include Burnley, where there are 455 migrants, or 46 for every 10,000 people.



Similar areas include Middlesborough (43 per 10,000), Blackpool (34) and South Tyneside (42).

The asylum seekers are split between emergency accommodation and dispersal accommodation including hotels and HMO properties, Home Office data shows.

The 17 areas with NO asylum seekers Ceredigion, population 72,599 Cotswold, population 91,661 Derbyshire Dales, population 71,757 East Hertfordshire, population 156,875 Hart, population 103,162 Highland, population 237,290 Isle of Wight, population 141,660 Isles of Scilly, population 2,366 Malvern Hills, population 83,227 Mid and East Antrim, population 139,913 Mid Devon, population 84,993 Mid Ulster, population 152,718 Na h-Eileanan Siar, population 26,020 New Forest, population 176,116 Orkney Islands, population 22,020 Shetland Islands, population 23,190 Tewkesbury, population 101,949

This morning, Anna Turley, the immigration minister, defended Mr Burnham’s remarks.

She said: “I think this is about fairness, and we won’t be asking anyone to take more than they can.

“It’s about their fair share, and we have to look across the country at what is appropriate for areas to take, what is the infrastructure, what is manageable with the local community.



“So this is about fairness.”

And pressed on the Piddington development, Ms Turley said: “The reality is, this is a military base that is outside the village. It’s self-contained.

“People there will be managed and processed properly with the services that they need there on site.

“So we are looking to reduce the impact on local communities.”

But Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “Andy Burnham is planning to dish out another vindictive punishment beating to the UK’s middle classes.



“Labour has hammered hard-working families with punitive tax increases galore, increased regulation and soaring energy bills.

“Now, Burnham plans to deliberately flood more neighbourhoods with thousands of illegal immigrants who he has let into this country, and many of whom will commit serious crimes including rape and murder.”

Mr Burnham, who visited Dover for the first time as PM earlier this month, has already seen 3,000 people cross the Channel since July 20.

More than 15,000 have crossed from France this year, lower than in the same point of the last two years.

The tally includes 230 who arrived in a single “mega-dinghy” in the early hours of Monday morning.



Home Office sources insisted that migrant smugglers had only resorted to larger boats as interceptions were increasing.

A spokesman added: “We’re cracking down on these reckless and dangerous gangs – our work to disrupt their criminal supply chains has led to more than 1,100 small boats and engines seized since the election.

“There are also now more police on French beaches to intercept them before they set off.

“Small boat crossings are significantly down this year with the lowest number recorded for the month of July since 2020.”

News.title: State pensioners left £100s out of pocket trying to claim Attendance Allowance
News.content:
State pensioners left £100s out of pocket trying to claim Attendance Allowance

Martin Lewis' MoneySavingExpert.com website says it has seen examples of “no win, no fee” firms charging hundreds of pounds to submit claims for people

View 2 Images Attendance Allowance is worth up to £114.60 a week (Image: Getty)

A warning has been issued to disabled or ill pensioners who are being urged not to pay for help with applying for benefits.

‌



The issue related to Attendance Allowance, which is awarded to people over state pension age who have a disability, health issue or mental health problems and need extra help.

‌



Martin Lewis' MoneySavingExpert.com website says it has seen examples of “no win, no fee” firms charging hundreds of pounds to submit claims for people - despite there being free services available to help those who are struggling.

‌



One person told the website she had paid £1,033 for a firm to submit her application. MSE says sometimes people have been charged a fixed fee, but in other cases it can be a cut of any benefit you're awarded in the first year.

View 2 Images The warning was issued by Martin Lewis' MoneySavingExpert.com website (Image: ITV)

Instead of paying for help, MSE recommends contacting Age UK (0800 678 1602), Citizens Advice (0800 144 8848), Independent Age (0800 319 6789), Scope (0808 800 3333) or Turn2Us (0808 164 8817).

‌



There are two different rates of Attendance Allowance. The lower rate of £76.70 a week is awarded if you need help during the day, or night. The higher rate is £114.60 a week if you need help both day and night, or are nearing the end of life.

But crucially, you do not actually need to have someone caring for you in order to claim Attendance Allowance - the money can used on things that keep you independent or help you around the house.

For example, it could be used to pay for a cleaner, gardener or taxis. You may qualify for Attendance Allowance if your condition means you have needed help for at least six months.

‌
