We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

The British are famed for making small talk about the weather. Now it’s time for some rather more consequential discussions. Andy Burnham, ever the metro mayor, has called a Cobra meeting to plan for the current emergency and, no doubt, show that he is alive to the public’s concern about the continuing drought.

In fact, the heatwave has been going on for so long, virtually uninterrupted, that it’s easily forgotten that it was the previous prime minister, Sir Keir Starmer, who convened a weather-based Cobra first, when the Met Office issued its first red alerts in late June. Since then, of course, there has been no let-up, and the global consequences of climate change have been brought home with all the power that our damaged ecosystem possesses.

For the long term, everyone realises what needs to be done: achieve net zero emissions of greenhouse gases. In the case of the UK, that has to be on track for 2050, even if other nations, at a different stage of industrial development, take longer. How we get there is also broadly obvious: replace fossil fuels with clean renewables and some nuclear power. Who pays and how for this national and international transition is highly contested, but at least the appropriate measures are clear enough.

We need more electric vehicles, more heat pumps and solar panels for homes and businesses (which can also power air conditioning systems), less meat consumption (livestock farming produces massive greenhouse gas emissions, especially methane from cows and sheep, and requires vast amounts of land that could otherwise be used to store carbon through reforestation) and cutting down on air travel. None of this will be easy to achieve, but there has been progress.

It is also fair to add a more optimistic note: the weight of evidence of climate change is now so painfully apparent that the climate-deniers, the net zero sceptics and the fossil fuel lobby have gone rather quiet lately. The scientific arguments on limiting the increase in the global temperature are being won as never before, and with them the political climate is also usefully changing.

That, however, is not at the top of the Cobra agenda for now. More urgent problems are upon us. Immensely damaging wildfires. Fragile heathlands, for example, are already being destroyed and will take decades to recover. The harm caused to wildlife, biodiversity and, indeed, the danger to human life, buildings, farms and even motorways has also grown more obvious. In this context, the suggested complete ban on disposable BBQs is a step that should have been taken before, and the penalties for their improper use must act as a deterrent.

Public education is also a perennial issue. The fire service is right to ask for more resources – such as helicopters with which to douse the flames. The NHS and care homes also need backing to cope with the extra demands; some smart “nudge” is needed to encourage the public to put their sun cream on.

With most of England now officially in drought conditions, water has to be preserved. As with most commodities, the surest way to do so normally would be by price – increase its cost and expand the coverage of water meters. However, for obvious reasons of health and sanitation, let alone the cost of living crisis, this is a difficult remedy to implement. Resorting to moral persuasion, as with a hosepipe ban, is always an uncertain solution.

As a practical imperative for the southern counties, and as a necessary precaution elsewhere, statutory drought orders should be issued, at least across England, imposing restrictions on swimming pools, hosepipes, car washes and the like. That would forestall or, preferably, avoid physical rationing – street standpipes, mobile water tanks or bottled water deliveries.

The biggest economic and human impact of the drought will be on farmers, and for some another year of failed harvest will push them to the wall. Since Brexit, agricultural businesses have been deprived of the financial support available from the European Union that offered them more resilience in difficult years. Food prices are certain to rise and the UK will inevitably have to import more foodstuffs as autumn approaches.

There will be demands on the Treasury for financial support. At a time when the public finances remain under strain, it will be difficult to offer all the financial assistance required. Mr Burnham and his ministers will need to revisit the present system of farm subsidies, biased as they are towards environmental rather than production objectives, with the very real risk that many otherwise profitable farms will go under. If these drought conditions become more normal, they face an extremely uncertain future.

One option would be to partner with rural businesses and take an equity stake or lend them the funds so that they can adapt to more drought-resistant crops (for example chickpeas), or else diversify. That would be an investment that the government should consider in the national interest. But if climate change is giving Britain wetter winters and long, hot and dry summers, then an even more difficult national conversation about the future will need to be had. For now, the nation’s lawns and parks will just have to stay parched.

News.title: Man kills partner and child at their Minnesota home daycare with six other kids present: police
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A father killed his partner and their child inside a Minnesota home daycare before taking his own life, according to police.

Six other children who were inside the home at the time of the murders were not injured and have all been reunited with their parents, Hopkins Police Chief Brent Johnson said during a press conference.

They were all "very, very young" children, Johnson said.

A parent arrived to drop a child off at Brown Bear Childcare when the attack is believed to have begun unfolding; they then alerted the police, according to Johnson.

“There’s no worse scenario than this, where you drop off your child somewhere you think is safe, and you get that phone call,” Johnson said at a news conference.

Johnson said he didn’t know what the relationship between the two adults who owned the daycare was, but did believe the child who died was theirs.

The police chief declined to release the victims’ identities and didn’t elaborate on how they died.

open image in gallery ( AP Photo/Carly Danek )

Records show the daycare has been licensed by the state since 2019 and has a capacity of 10 children. It was found to be in compliance during visits in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

The home daycare was located in Hopkins, a small suburb about 10 miles southwest of Minneapolis.

Johnson said the scene was a “rarity” in Hopkins and that his officers were shaken by the killings after arriving at the home.

“I could see on the look on their faces that this was one of those ones that you’ll remember for your entire career, if not life,” Johnson said.

open image in gallery ( AP Photo/Carly Danek )

Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey acknowledged at the start of his 2027 budget address Wednesday morning that a "critical incident" had occurred in Hopkins.

"I know that our hearts and our prayers are with the people of Hopkins and any families that have been impacted," Frey said. "I have already touched base directly with Mayor Hanlon, offered any assistance that we possibly can provide."

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games.



What counts as a Save?

A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

For an exhaustive list of how to score Telegraph Fantasy Football points, take a look at our Game Guidelines.

Sports.title: Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'
Sports.content:
Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'

Manchester United have been linked with Leicester City's Louis Page but Russell Martin has made it clear the teenager is not for sale

View 2 Images Man Utd are eyeing up a move for Leicester's Louis Page (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Leicester boss Russell Martin admits he'd tell Manchester United chief Jason Wilcox "to go away" if he made attempts to sign teenager Louis Page.

‌



The 18-year-old was named the EFL Apprentice of the Year last season and is seen as one of the most exciting talents in the Football League - attracting attention from the Red Devils.

‌



Page would reportedly be keen on moving to Old Trafford if the opportunity arose, but Leicester are determined to keep hold of their academy graduate. The England U20 international has already made 21 senior appearances for the Foxes - including five starts last season. He played in their Carabao Cup win over Northampton on Saturday.

‌



Martin has been appointed as the Foxes new boss following their relegation to League One and he previously worked at Southampton with Wilcox, who is now the director of football at United. He admits, despite their history, he'd tell him to look elsewhere if they came looking for Page.

Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message READ MORE :

Youri Tielemans sends clear Marcus Rashford message to Michael Carrick after Man Utd reunion READ MORE :

He jokingly told Sky Sports: "Louis is a really fantastic young player. Obviously, I know the director of football at Manchester United very well after spending some time with Southampton. So we haven't actually spoken with Louis because he probably knows what I'd say to him and tell him to go away.

"But no, until something comes in that is really brilliant for the club, the player, and everyone is happy, then Louis stays, and he's in the squad. I'm really enjoying working with him. He's a fantastic young player."

‌



View 2 Images Leicester's teenage star recently signed a professional deal

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also shown an interest in Page. Leicester have already lost one of their leading young prospects this summer after seeing forward Jeremy Monga, 17, join Manchester City, and they will be loathed to see another leave the King Power Stadium.

Page signed professional terms with the Foxes in September last year, which means United would need to agree a transfer fee if they wanted to secure his services.

Article continues below

Leicester said after he penned his deal: "After joining us at Under-9s, Louis has progressed through our Academy ranks and developed within the LCFC pathway into one of the brightest talents in our system".

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho hits new low as club reject free transfer for Man Utd flop
Sports.content:
Jadon Sancho hits new low as club reject free transfer for Man Utd flop

Jadon Sancho is still without a club following his Manchester United exit earlier this summer

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho is still a free agent after leaving Manchester United earlier this summer. (Image: (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images))

Serie A side Fiorentina have reportedly turned down the chance to sign former Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho as his search for a new club drags on. The 26-year-old is still without a new club after leaving Old Trafford earlier this summer, with the new season edging closer.

‌



Reports emerging from Italy state that Fiorentina have passed up the opportunity to bring in the ex-United winger, who spent last season on loan at Aston Villa. Sancho featured 39 times for Villa across all competitions, as Unai Emery's side secured fourth place in the league and lifted the Europa League trophy.

‌



Yet despite that triumph at Villa, he hasn't found a new club yet. Alfredo Pedulla claims Sancho was proposed to Fiorentina a fortnight ago, but the Serie A outfit had reservations about signing him given his performances in recent years.

‌



Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

This isn't the first occasion that Sancho has seen a potential move to Italy collapse, with AS Roma showing interest in acquiring the England international during the summer of 2025.

‌



It was claimed his representatives' fees derailed that transfer to the Italian heavyweights, and negotiations this summer have encountered fresh complications.

Non-league outfit Flixton were compelled to issue a statement earlier this summer after Sancho was seen training at the club's ground.

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho was last with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Club owner Christopher Garcia denied that Sancho had been on trial and clarified: "Over the past few days, we've seen a number of posts and comments circulating regarding Jadon Sancho's visit to Flixton FC.

"To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions. He simply used our facilities for a private training session to maintain his fitness while preparing for the next chapter of his career.

"We're proud that the quality of our pitch and facilities made Flixton a place where a player of his calibre felt comfortable training, and he is welcome to train at Flixton FC whenever he wishes.

‌



"During his visit, Jadon was nothing but professional, humble, and generous with his time. After completing his session, he happily met with young supporters, posed for photos, signed autographs, and left a lasting impression on everyone who had the pleasure of meeting him.

"Jadon is a world-class footballer who has achieved more in the game than most players could ever dream of. He deserves respect for both his accomplishments and the way he conducted himself during his visit, not the unwarranted criticism that has followed.

"We thank Jadon for choosing Flixton FC as a place to train and wish him every success in the next stage of his career, which will undoubtedly be at a level far above where we currently compete. Our doors will always be open to him."

Sports.title: Kyle Walker lined up for immediate Premier League return after Burnley relegation
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker lined up for immediate Premier League return after Burnley relegation

Kyle Walker suffered relegation with Burnley last season but has remained with them in the Championship, however he could received an offer to make a Premier League return

View 2 Images Kyle Walker could make a Premier League return before the transfer window closes

Kyle Walker could be handed a route back into the Premier League with Everton keen on signing the veteran right-back.

‌



The ex-Manchester City star suffered relegation with the Clarets in his first season at Turf Moor and is now tasked with getting them out of the Championship, but the Toffees could finally land the Englishman.

‌



Twice in the past they've missed out on Walker. They were in for him before he moved to Burnley 12 months ago and back when Walker was a teenager they also tried to sign him, but he made the move to Tottenham.

‌



Everton could be successful with their third try, according to The Sun, as David Moyes looks to add more experience and quality to his squad on Merseyside.

Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message READ MORE :

Everton player charged with 61 breaches of FA betting rules as statement released READ MORE :

The Toffees have already signed the likes Brennan Johnson, Christian Norgaard and Tyrique George this summer. Johnson became their latest addition this week as he was involved in a swap deal that saw Dwight McNeil head to Crystal Palace.

Walker, now 36, made 35 starts for Burnley in the Premier League last season, highlighting his durability despite his age. He's chosen to remain with the club and scored the winning penalty in their spot-kick Carabao Cup victory over Notts County on Saturday.

‌



The ex-international can boast a CV that includes six Premier League titles and the Champions League but maintained that he's relishing the challenge of the Championship once again. He's previously played in the second tier with Sheffield United and QPR.

View 2 Images David Moyes is eyeing a move for the veteran right-back (Image: Getty Images)

Whilst at Loftus Road he was part of a team that would claim the title and believes that Burnley have all the tools to make an immediate return to the top flight.

‌



"Things aren’t always going to go as planned," he said. "This season might not go as planned. It might not be as plain sailing as we all want it to be. But I feel with the quality, what we have in the dressing room, that’s what we should be doing: getting promoted and going back to the Premier League."

Since 2013 Burnley have won promotion from the Championship on four occasions - but been relegated as many times. This is their sixth straight year playing in a different tier following a period of ups and downs.

Sports.title: Luis Enrique's daughter tragedy which helped shape PSG manager's new determination
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique's daughter tragedy which helped shape PSG manager's new determination

Luis Enrique has an emotional connection to European competitions as his Paris Saint-Germain side gear up for a Super Cup clash against Aston Villa

View 3 Images PSG manager Luis Enrique's daughter Xana Martinez sadly died in 2019 (Image: Getty)

Luis Enrique will look to add another European trophy to his already glittering cabinet on Wednesday night as PSG take on Aston Villa in the Super Cup. The Spaniard guided his team to their second-ever Champions League success in May and is still inspired by the tragic death of his daughter Xana.

‌



After the Parisian side beat Inter Milan 5-0 in 2025 to win the competition for the first time, they went on to claim consecutive titles, defeating Arsenal on penalties three months ago. Becoming European champions means PSG will once more play in the Super Cup against the Europa League winners, Villa.

‌



They came back in dramatic fashion to secure a shootout win over Tottenham in last year's edition. For this renewal, PSG are favourites to once again lift the trophy. All eyes will be on Enrique as he looks to tactically outwit his compatriot and former PSG manager Unai Emery in the opposition dugout.

‌



Enrique was hugely successful even before taking the reins in Paris, having won the Champions League and Super Cup with Barcelona in 2015. But behind his intense and fiercely competitive demeanour on the touchline lies a tragic story that shook the footballing world several years ago.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Aston Villa linked with bargain Real Madrid transfer to replace Morgan Rogers READ MORE :

In June 2019, Enrique suddenly stepped down from his role as manager of Spain's national team. The Spanish Football Federation cited "urgent personal matters" and Enrique revealed two months later that his youngest daughter, Xana, had tragically passed away at just nine years of age.

‌



View 3 Images Ex-Barcelona coach Enrique was joined by his daughter Xana after the 2015 Champions League final (Image: Getty )

Xana had spent five months fighting osteosarcoma, a rare and highly aggressive form of bone cancer that primarily affects children, teenagers and young adults.

Enrique said at the time: "We will miss you a lot but we will remember you every day of our lives with the hope that one day in the future we will meet again. You will be the star that guides our family. Rest in peace, Xanita."

‌



There was an immediate outpouring of support as Enrique was lauded for his positive and brave outlook despite the tragedy. He went on to share his inspiring perspective on the nine years he spent with Xana in a multi-part documentary about his life and career.

"My daughter came to live with us for nine wonderful years," he said. "We have a thousand memories of her. You may ask whether I consider myself fortunate or unfortunate. I consider myself to have been fortunate. Very fortunate."

Following his first Champions League success as a manager with his beloved Barcelona, Enrique celebrated on the pitch with the youngest of his three children, Xana, who carried and waved a huge flag.

‌



View 3 Images PSG supporters unveiled a tribute to their manager's late daughter (Image: TNT Sports)

He delivered a touching tribute a decade later following his first historic Champions League triumph with PSG, dedicating the victory to his late daughter and stating she was with him "spiritually." After the French side defeated Inter 5-0, PSG fans celebrated their manager by unfurling a huge tifo inside the stadium that also featured Xana.

Enrique was clearly left emotional by the gesture and responded: "I'm very happy. It was very emotional at the end with the banner from the fans for my family. But I always think about my daughter. It means a lot. It's so nice, but I don't need to win the Champions League to remember my daughter. My daughter is always with us."

Sports.title: Birmingham Phoenix win battle to avoid Hundred wooden spoon vs MI London
Sports.content:
Birmingham Phoenix prevailed in the battle to avoid the wooden spoon in The Hundred women's competition as Ellyse Perry's composed half-century condemned MI London to a sixth defeat of a chastening campaign.

Both teams had managed a solitary victory heading into this fixture but a fifth-wicket stand of 66 between Perry (62no from 39) and Pakistan skipper Fatima Sana (36 from 32) ensured Phoenix halted a three-match losing streak to end with a consolation win and finish seventh in the table.

Set a modest target of 122, the hosts were wobbling at 48-4 after Jemima Spence and Davina Perrin fell in the powerplay and England duo Alice Capsey and Emma Lamb were dismissed cheaply, with Kirstie Gordon (2-20) making early inroads with her left-arm spin.

But Perry found a willing partner in Sana, who eventually fell to Nicola Carey when just seven runs were required, and the Aussie superstar secured the win with six balls to spare.

Sports.title: Fery feels 'no added pressure' despite being British No 1 as he returns
Sports.content:
Arthur Fery insists he feels “no added pressure” as the new British No 1 prepares to return to action this weekend for the first time since his memorable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals.

Fery became only the fifth British player to make the last four of the men's singles at Wimbledon in the Open era and has surged into the top 40 in the ATP rankings, have been ended 2025 in 198th.

The 23-year-old skipped the Canadian Open to ensure he is rested but will be back this weekend at the ATP 1000 event in Cincinnati, live on Sky Sports Tennis.

"It's obviously a privilege to be to No 1 in in Britain. I'm not gonna put any added pressure on myself," Fery told Sky Sports.

"I'm just going to take every match as it comes, keep working hard day in, day out, both in practice and at tournaments, and see where that takes me. That's what I've been doing this year and it's worked well so far, so I'm just going to keep going in the same direction."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery says it was 'incredible' to reach the Wimbledon semi-finals and vows to keep the British No 1 spot

Fery will look to ensure he is seeded at the last Grand Slam of the year, the US Open, which begins on August 30, by having a strong run in Cincinnati.

He has been training in London since Wimbledon but flew to Ohio earlier this week to acclimatise to the conditions, with Fery also saying fellow players have been welcoming as he adjusts to his sudden rise.

"All the way through the fortnight, it was just incredible to have so much support. I'd never had that amount of people and fans behind me, so that was really special," he said.

"Now here in in Cincinnati, playing my second Masters 1000 main draw, I'm really looking forward to playing all these tough events this year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky's Jacquie Beltrao looks ahead to a bright future for Arthur Fery after his semi-final exit to Alexander Zverev at Wimbledon

Draper could meet Djokovic in Cincinnati

Jack Draper has been given a wild card for the Cincinnati Open and could meet Novak Djokovic in the third round of the tournament.

Draper will play rising Spanish star Martin Landeluce in the first round before facing Italy's Matteo Arnaldi. Should Draper win those two matches, he could meet Djokovic next week.

However, the 24-year-old will likely simply hope he is fit for multiple matches after he was in tears during his defeat last week to Terence Atmane in the first round of the Canadian Open. It was unclear whether that was related to his recent arm injury recurring.

Cameron Norrie will face Croatia's Dino Prizmic while Jan Choinski goes up against Argentina's Thiago Agustin Tirante and Fery has a bye to the second round since he is seeded.

Katie Boulter is the only Brit in the women's draw and she will play USA's Katie Volynets.

Sports.title: McIlroy keen to asses his game during first FedExCup Playoffs event
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy believes this week's FedEx St. Jude Championship will be a good chance for him to assess the current standard of his game, as the Northern Irishman returns to PGA Tour action for the first time since The Open.

The two-time Masters champion heads into the first of three FedExCup Playoffs events at TPC Southwind in Memphis refreshed after four weeks away from the course, which included holidays to Greece and Ibiza.

McIlroy, who is ranked 12th in the FedExCup standings, can also wrap up his 2026 PGA Tour season on a high note, as he bids to win a record-extending fourth FedExCup title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Northern Irishman is looking to clinch his fourth FedExCup title

The 37-year-old chose to skip last year's FedEx St. Jude Championship and instead took a four-week break following his tied-seventh finish at The Open before returning for the BMW Championship.

But ahead of this week's event, the Northern Irishman explained he was excited to tee up as one of 69 players in the field at TPC Southwind, adding he felt it was "important" to feature in the opening Playoffs event.

"A few different things went into that decision," McIlroy said.

"Having four weeks off going into the last two events of the year [2025] was probably going to be a little too much for me in terms of wanting to be competitive.

FedExCup Playoffs schedule All tournaments live on Sky Sports August 13-16: FedEx St. Jude Championship (TPC Southwind, Memphis, Tennessee) August 20-23: BMW Championship, (Bellerive Country Club, St. Louis, Missouri) August 27-30: Tour Championship (East Lake Golf Club, Atlanta, Georgia)

"Obviously, I want to play well, but it's also a good week to see where my game is, do a lot of practise, or as much as I can in the heat.

"I think it's important to be here. It's the FedExCup Playoffs. I think it's important for all the players to be here.

"I've had some good conversations with (PGA Tour CEO) Brian Rolapp over the last couple of weeks. It's important for me to be here and show support. I'm looking forward to teeing it up."

McIlroy has been open about his desire to reduce his schedule, and on the course he has enjoyed a solid 2026, successfully defending his Green Jacket, while finishing inside the top 10 in four of his 11 PGA Tour starts.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy says he is interested in assessing his game during this week's event

After the FedExCup Playoffs, McIlroy will look to defend his Irish Open title in September, before heading to Wentworth to tee up at the BMW PGA Championship.

But before then, he faces the challenge of outlasting some of the best players on the PGA Tour across three events in the blistering heat of the American south.

McIlroy, who has a great record in the PGA Tour's season-ending events, explained his game plan for the three-week stretch, saying he sees the Playoffs as "one long golf event".

"I almost try to view the Playoffs as one big, long tournament, like a 12-round event," McIlroy said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy added he felt it was important to play at the FedEx St. Jude after skipping the event in 2025

"You've got to pace yourself. It's three long weeks. We're going from here to St Louis to Atlanta. Every week is going to feel a bit like this. It's going to be hot and sweaty. So you want to be able to conserve energy as well.

"I've always tried to treat it like one big, long golf tournament and get into the rhythm of it and go from there.

"I've been lucky enough to do pretty well on these things over the years. So I'll try to add another one to the list."

The PGA Tour's FedExCup Playoffs begin on Thursday with the FedEx St. Jude Championship. Watch live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event from 7pm or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: Cadillac sack team principal Lowdon as Budkowski takes charge
Sports.content:
Cadillac have sacked team principal Graeme Lowdon and replaced him with Marcin Budkowski in what Formula 1's 2026 newcomers claim is a "planned leadership transition".

Budkowski, whose most recent role in F1 ended when he left his position as Alpine executive director in 2022, takes over with Cadillac as the only team yet to have scored a point during the first 11 rounds of the 2026 season.

The 49-year-old Polish-French engineer's first race in charge will be the Dutch Grand Prix, which sees the season resume from August 21-23 after the sport's four-week summer break.

Lowdon was appointed team principal of the Cadillac project in December 2024 and had overseen the American-owned outift's preparations for and arrival on the F1 grid, for which they assembled a driver pairing of Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Valtteri Bottas was told to immediately stop on track due to a technical issue at the Australian Grand Prix

Cadillac F1 team chief executive Dan Towriss said: "Marcin's appointment marks another important step in the continued evolution of the Cadillac Formula 1 Team.

"From the beginning, our goal has not been simply to participate in Formula 1, but to build a next-generation team capable of competing at the very front.

"As we enter this new era for the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, Marcin brings exceptional F1 experience, technical expertise and strategic leadership that will strengthen our organisation and help us develop the winning mindset, tools and processes required for long-term success."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cadillac's Sergio Perez made a swift escape from his car after his brakes went on fire at the end of P2 at the Monaco Grand Prix

While a team statement said that the change "follows a planned leadership transition", there had been no previous indication that Lowdon would not remain in place for at least Cadillac's first season on the grid.

It is not a major surprise that Cadillac - as a new team - have not scored any points, although it is possible there was disappointment from above Lowdon at the technical issues that have resulted in nine grand prix retirements between Perez and Bottas across the first 11 rounds.

Cadillac's reliability has actually worsened as the season has gone on, with the team having managed to get both cars to the chequered flag at only one of the last seven races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bottas crawls back into the pits after the front bib of his Cadillac catches fire due to heat

Towriss added: "We're grateful to Graeme Lowdon for his leadership and the role he played in forming the Cadillac Formula 1 Team from the ground up.

"His contributions helped establish a strong foundation in our build-up phase, and we thank him for his commitment and wish him well."

Lowdon informed of sacking on morning of announcement

Speaking in a virtual press conference later on Wednesday, Towriss confirmed he had decided to dismiss Lowdon, and that the Briton had only been informed of the decision a matter of hours before Cadillac's announcement.

"It was my decision, it wasn't a mutual decision," Towriss said. "The process started a few months ago to explore really thinking about what the next phase for Cadillac F1 looks like, what's the right timing? How would that look?

"And then the capabilities of the various folks out there, and obviously we were delighted in the conversation with Marcin and how that relationship evolved.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sergio Perez stops on track during P3 of the Hungarian Grand Prix

"Graeme and I spoke this morning. It is a very recent conversation from that perspective. There's no easy way to make this transition within Formula 1. Can you imagine the press if Marcin was strolling through for a tour of the factory, or having these conversations?

"It becomes destabilising at that point. It's important to respect the leadership that's in place at that time, so it does compress the timeline in how these things come together. It makes it feel more abrupt than it would be otherwise. But it's the nature of F1 and it's the way it had to happen."

Budkowski worked at Prost, Ferrari, McLaren and the FIA before joining Renault/Alpine, where he spent four years before leaving in 2022.

Sports.title: European Super Cup: Paris Saint-Germain v Aston Villa – live
Sports.content:
PSG also have a shiny new thing in their starting line-up: Maghnes Akliouche, a £43m buy from Monaco, prepares to cause havoc on the right wing. Lucas Digne, freshly arrived from Villa, sits in the dugout awaiting his debut. Bradley Barcola, coveted by both Liverpool and Arsenal, is also on the bench.

Aston Villa name two debutants in their XI. João Gomes, their £38m purchase from Wolves, starts in the centre of midfield, while 17-year-old Brian Madjo – at six feet four, officially a big unit – leads the line.

Aston Villa already have the Super Cup on their roll of honour, of course. Gather round, dear children, and hear tell of a time in which FC Barcelona were less renowned for their Cruyffian devotion to the beautiful game, more interested in toe-punting whoever so much as looked at them all around the shop with great vim and vigour.

The modern-day artistes of Paris Saint-Germain are unlikely to resort to such base hoodlummery this evening. That said, they’ve already thrown a toddler’s tanty over the size of their dressing room, so let’s rule nothing out. Will the European champions put Villa to the sword, just as they did Spurs this time last year? Or will Unai Emery fill an odd gap on his personal resumé, finally converting Europa League glory into Super Cup success at the nth time of asking? We find out soon! Kick-off in Salzburg is at 8pm BST. It’s on!

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 6: Chelsea
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 3rd (NB: this is not necessarily Billy Munday’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

After a season of struggle and regression, with two head coaches and two spells under a caretaker, there is cautious optimism that this campaign will bring something like stability. Much of that optimism centres around the appointment of Xabi Alonso, an elite manager with something to prove. There is also an expectation that the young players brought in as part of BlueCo’s £1.8bn splurge in recent years are beginning to come into their best years. There is no European football to complicate the schedule and a return to the Champions League by finishing in the top four or five would suffice for now. More importance will be placed on the domestic cups after a season without trophies.

Alonso’s squad is more rounded than what Enzo Maresca or Liam Rosenior had at their disposal. Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers bring quality to positions where Chelsea were lacking it – at centre-back and out wide. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson – the “uncs” as Tosin Adarabioyo has called them – will contribute as much off the pitch as on it. The signing of Marco Palestra, a specialist wing-back, suggests Alonso wants to be tactically flexible. He has used a back four and a back three in pre-season.

What about Cole Palmer? For so much of his time at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea’s form has been tied to his. When he has struggled to be 100% fit, the team have suffered too. After being omitted from England’s World Cup squad, Palmer had a seven-week break and sought advice from a specialist on the groin injury that hampered him last season. “I got bored after six weeks,” Palmer said after returning for pre-season. “I was sat in Marbella thinking: ‘I want to go back in.’” With the prospect of linking up with Rogers and João Pedro, who has also had a good rest, Palmer has plenty of reasons to be excited.

Off-field picture

July ended with Chelsea being fined £10m and receiving a suspended transfer ban over multiple violations of transfer rules under the ownership of Roman Abramovich. An appeal from the club saved them from a six-point deduction. Chelsea were deemed compliant with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules for the three-year period ending in 2025 despite posting an English record £262.4m pre-tax loss for the 2024-25 season. They have not been cowed by failure to qualify for Europe and have spent over £300m on new signings. For the fourth year in a row, Chelsea look likely to start the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Supporter protests against the ownership of Todd Boehly’s BlueCo have been a frequent sight on matchdays, including before May’s FA Cup final defeat by Manchester City. There have been reservations about the club’s youth-oriented transfer policy from the start and last season’s failings prompted the co-owner Behdad Eghbali to admit the need “to add more ready-made players” to the squad. Whether fans were expecting the arrivals of Welbeck and Henderson is another question. The introduction of a ticket ballot system for home games has also been unpopular with regular match-going supporters.

The manager

It was a bit of a coup for Chelsea to secure Alonso’s services this summer, especially given the Liverpool job was available. The Spaniard has a reputation to rebuild after his dream job at Real Madrid ended in the sack after six months. “I got a scar, now it is healed,” he said. Alonso’s record of developing young players, such as Florian Wirtz, at Bayer Leverkusen while simultaneously delivering silverware is a match made in heaven for the Chelsea hierarchy. One detail to note: Alonso has been appointed as manager, rather than head coach like his predecessors. He has also brought in Austin MacPhee, Aston Villa’s set-piece guru.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Chelsea broke the British transfer record to pry Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea went one better than Manchester City’s £116m signing of Elliot Anderson by bringing in Rogers, who had been linked with Arsenal, for a new British record fee of £117m. Although he started England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina on the right wing, Rogers has thrived for Aston Villa playing largely off the left and should slot in there nicely at Chelsea. The 24-year-old has proved himself in the Premier League and his best-buddy relationship with his former Manchester City youth teammate Palmer is a major plus. “I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said.

Stat attack

Has anyone checked Chelsea haven’t built a squad of Benjamin Buttons? The average age of their starting XI has decreased over the past three seasons when they were already the youngest team in Premier League history. You can see why they signed Henderson and Welbeck.

Set for a breakthrough

Robert Sánchez is still Chelsea’s No 1 but he may face serious competition this season from the 21-year-old Mike Penders. The goalkeeper, who was third-choice for Belgium at the World Cup, was signed from Genk in 2024 and spent last season on loan at Strasbourg in Ligue 1. The comparisons with Thibaut Courtois, who Chelsea signed from Genk at a similar age, are obvious. Like Courtois, Penders is 6ft 7in and therefore has a massive reach, but he also earns plaudits for his passing. Chances will come in cup competitions, but the clamour for Penders to be first choice might become hard to ignore.

World Cup impact

Enzo Fernández had a rollercoaster of a World Cup. Chelsea’s vice-captain popped up with crucial late goals for Argentina in the knockout stages, including a winning header against Egypt and the equaliser against England. But the abiding memory was his part in Argentina’s unsavoury approach in the final against Spain, where he received one yellow card for dissent and another for sending Pau Cubarsí flying. Real Madrid said in July they had “no intention” of pursuing a move that Fernández seemed to covet earlier this year when he said he would “love” to live in Madrid – comments that earned him a two-game ban under Rosenior. How about living in Manchester? City have been linked.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father.

Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

In a tribute on Instagram on Wednesday, Messi wrote: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you. I don’t know how ​to move forward. I only played football and now I have quite a few doubts about whether I’m going to keep doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the tournament, where Argentina were beaten in the final by Spain, before rejoining his club side, Inter Miami, making his Major League Soccer return against Columbus at the start of this month.

Jorge had been a constant presence during his son’s career from his earliest days at Barcelona, with the World Cup the first time he had been absent from a major tournament. Messi revealed that his father, despite his deteriorating condition, had urged him to play for La Albiceleste in their ultimately unsuccessful attempt to defend their title.

“You always asked me to play in the last World Cup and a few days before it started was when you got worse,” he wrote. “It was the first time you weren’t going to be at a tournament … Every time a match ended, I would ‌wait and hope for your message. That’s when I realised how real the situation was.”

After tearfully celebrating the opening goal of his hat-trick against Algeria in the group stage, Messi had explained he was going through “a few difficult, complicated days” because of “something unrelated to football”. he said he ran out of energy in final.

“My legs couldn’t go on any more,” he wrote. “This time I tried to push myself beyond my ​physical limits, but I couldn’t. ​I never felt well … We weren’t champions, ​but you don’t know how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were ​right: I had to ‌be there and play ​it.”

Messi has earned 207 caps for Argentina since making his debut for his country in August 2005. He captained the side to World Cup glory in 2022, matching the achievement of Diego Maradona in 1986, though like Maradona he fell at the final hurdle when attempting to win back-to-back titles.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Messi did, though, break the record for total World Cup goals, with his strike against Egypt in the last 16 his 21st at the tournament and his 125th in all for Argentina. His World Cup tally was later surpassed by France’s Kylian Mbappé in the third-place playoff.

With his future uncertain it remains to be seen whether he will add to his remarkable CV of honours, which includes 10 La Liga titles, four Champions Leagues and eight Ballons d’Or in addition to that World Cup triumph in Qatar.

But he promised to honour his father’s memory through his own children: “I’m going to miss you so much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I will teach them and raise them the way you raised me.”

Sports.title: ‘It’s a nice hobby’: Manchester United’s Janina Leitzig on goalkeeping and gardening
Sports.content:
With some parts of England gearing up for a fifth heatwave of 2026 the new Manchester United goalkeeper Janina Leitzig, a keen gardener, is sympathetic to the precarious health of this reporter’s tomato plants. “You’re not used to so little rain, are you?” she observes. For the time being, after her summer move to Manchester, the former Germany youth international does not have a garden of her own but she reveals that, during her three-and-a-half-year spell at her former club Leicester, homegrown vegetables were her pride and joy.

“I love to do some gardening. Back home, everyone has their own vegetables and it’s just better, it tastes better,” she tells the Guardian. “Being away from home and away from family, of course you have your football friends, but still it can be quite lonely sometimes if you come home from training, so it was really nice to have a garden and to spend time outside. It’s not too much effort, it’s just a nice hobby.”

The 27-year-old got her outdoor fix with a spot of surfing in Cornwall this summer during the off-season, but now the serious business of pre-season is well under way. Her new club Manchester United are heading to La Manga for a training camp between 14 and 19 August, where the focus will have to be less on runner beans and more on running drills.

Leitzig, the former Bayern Munich and Hoffenheim keeper, was sitting down for an interview before it was known that the Spanish coach Eva Olid was to become United’s new manager, but explained why swapping Leicester for United was appealing to her. “It’s such a big club and it’s such a big honour to be here,” Leitzig says.

“I think, for every player, it’s really interesting if you have an offer from Manchester United. First of all, the team is so nice. The characters in here – you can tell it’s a really good and strong team. The training quality is really high. The building and the facilities [at Carrington] are really good; it’s really professional here. [When] the conversations were going on [with United], they just gave me a really good feeling.”

View image in fullscreen Janina Leitzig during a training session at Carrington. Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Getty Images

Leitzig has signed a contract with United until 2029, after the disappointment of relegation with Leicester last season, but says she has nothing but fond feelings about her former club, who she initially joined on loan in January 2023 before signing permanently that summer.

Looking back at what she learned in the East Midlands, she says: “It was such a special time for me. It was supposed to be only half a year and then it ended up being three-and-a-half. I think that says a lot about how much I liked it there. The people are great and the club is great.

“Obviously we had some tough times and unfortunately the relegation last season was really, really tough and it really hurt, because the club deserves to be in a better position, but I really hope that the girls will do well and I see them soon back in the WSL. It would be great if they could come back up quickly.”

During her time in England, Leitzig has observed an evolution in goalkeeping styles, and she is in a thoughtful mood when discussing what the future might look like for keepers, tactically. On the modern trend of keepers playing out from the back, she says: “To be fair, there was one phase where everyone wanted goalkeepers to play with the feet and I think it’s still really important, but I think there was a phase where it was too much. I think it was a bit overexaggerated at times, so I think it’s coming back now to be more about the basic stuff.

“Obviously you have to switch play and you have to be good with your feet under pressure, but I think the game is going to be more [about] trying to get the ball as quick as possible in the opposite half to then keep the pressure up there and not to try to take such a high risk. It’s going to be interesting.

“I think, because I’m German and Manuel Neuer [her idol] is German, I learned quite early to play with both feet and I was an outfield player initially, so I’m feeling confident about playing with the ball. But saving shots is the best part of goalkeeping.”

The USA keeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce played in 21 of United’s 22 matches in the Women’s Super League last season and Leitzig says they will enjoy working together and helping each other. “They [United] said it’s like a competition [to start in goal]. Obviously it’s really important to have strong goalkeepers, because you never know what happens in the season.

“I will just give my best, I’ll try to bring quality, and then it’s the manager’s decision to decide who’s going to play. But it’s really important that we are a good goalkeeper team, that we support each other and push each other because then everyone can get better.”

United, who finished fourth last season, will get the new WSL season under way on the opening night, at London City Lionesses on 4 September. Leizig concludes by looking ahead to that showdown and says, with fire in her eyes: “To have the first game of the season Friday evening, 7pm, floodlights, it’s just something you’re really excited for. Working in the pre-season you think: ‘When can the [games] finally start,’ so I’m really excited for that game.”

Sports.title: Barcelona make improved £51m bid for Rodri as Manchester City target Fernández
Sports.content:
Barcelona have made an improved bid to Manchester City of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri. This follows Barça’s initial offer of €45m that was rejected out of hand by City.

The Spanish club’s new offer – which may include add-ons – is close to City’s valuation for the 30-year-old who captained Spain to the World Cup and won the Ballon d’Or in 2024.

As the midfielder has declared a preference for Barcelona it seems it is inevitable he will leave. In preparation City are targeting Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández as a potential signing though the west London club’s valuation of around £120m may be too high.

Chelsea are understood to be intent on that price for the attacking midfielder so any transfer may include add-ons. Enzo Maresca is keen on Fernández after working with him for a season-and-a-half at Chelsea before his tenure ended in January.

The 25-year-old was a key member of Maresca’s team that finished fourth and won the Europa Conference in 2024-25 and the Fifa Club World Cup last summer.

If City were to sign Fernández, a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022, another midfielder could be offloaded, with Tijjani Reijnders a possible candidate to depart.

As Rodri is intent on a move to Barcelona the arrival of Fernández, Chelsea’s captain, would add seniority and leadership to Maresca’s squad and a player whose combative style would offer an edge to City’s play.

City have so far recruited Elliott Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest and are close to the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi for around £85m from Lille.

Chelsea are thought to have enquired about Bournemouth’s Alex Scott as a replacement for Fernández should he leave.

City announced on Wednesday the signing of Gerónimo Rulli on a two-year deal following James Trafford’s move to Leeds. The Argentina goalkeeper was previously at the club in 2016-17.

The 34-year-old said: “My job now is to train hard, get to know the players and staff and do everything I can.”
