Newly-promoted Hull have broken their transfer record to sign Senegal defender Nobel Mendy from Spanish side Rayo Vallecano.

The Tigers have not disclosed the fee for the 21-year-old but it exceeds the reported £20m they paid for Greece goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis last week.

Mendy, who has one international cap and previously played for Paris FC and Real Betis, has signed a five-year deal, with an option for a further 12 months.

He finished his only season with Rayo Vallecano with an appearance in May’s Conference League final loss to Crystal Palace.

“I have wanted to play in the Premier League since I was little, so it’s a great challenge to face and I am ready for it,” Mendy told Hull’s website.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s ‘rock star’ plays the hits but will he find it hard to stay in Toon?
Sports.content:
IN A BLACK AND WHITE TOWN

As rallying cries for the dawn of a golden era go, “I am quite optimistic” is not “ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country”. It did not fit the “I think I am a special one” template set 22 years ago by Netflix’s latest documentary subject. Nor did Matthias Jaissle’s unveiling as Newcastle manager meet the pre-match billing of “fire” and “a rock star” that the club’s chief suit had promised the journalists in attendance. Though, considering the summer of tumult on Tyneside, it was a sensible path to take. Expectations among the Toon Army have certainly lowered since Geordies sunk Tin and donned tea-towel headdresses in celebration of Mike Ashley’s departure and the arrival of a consortium underpinned by the petrodollars of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. As it turned out, Lionel Messi neither ended up mowing the pitch nor selling the pies.

Depending on your perspective, that Newcastle have not yet been crowned Premier League and Bigger Cup champions is down to the servile football authorities bowing down to the hated red cartel or that day of wild celebration being one of false hope. The truth lies probably somewhere in between. A number of missteps pockmarked the last season of Eddie Howe’s reign. The “here we go” arrivals were nowhere near up to snuff. It should, though, be readily accepted that Newcastle enjoyed a good run under Howe, including an actual trophy and two rides on the Bigger Cup fun bus.

The Saudi connection has not paved St James’ Park with black gold (or Texas tea as the Beverly Hillbillies once had it). A pitfall of becoming the plaything of a top-level geopolitical operator is that those geopolitics may get in the way. Gulf states have a few things on their plates at the moment, and the interests of that investment fund stretch beyond a football club 3,000 miles from Riyadh. A new phase is entered; Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães are gone. Some might say the Saudis have lost interest, though Jaissle’s arrival from Al-Ahli, another club in the Pif portfolio, suggests hands are still on the tiller.

As for the new manager, the verdict was that he spoke very well at his premiere. “We were looking at each other with smiles and goosebumps,” he cooed, in describing his and his assistants’ first look at the stadium. Realism was offered in admitting a “vacuum” now those assets have been flogged off but there was no preview of the touchline histrionics various profiles have promised. Jaissle also followed the recent but now ingrained tradition of shaking each of his future interrogators’ hands. A classy gesture? A power move? Take your pick. Howe’s departure, and the loss of those big names, has returned Newcastle to the state of flux that was long their usual state of existence. How long can Jaissle’s calm and collected deportment last? How long can measured optimism sustain?

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray at 8pm BST for live updates on PSG 3-1 Aston Villa in the Uefa Super (Duper) Cup final.

Sports.title: Championship angst: why the sense of rejuvenation in EFL is not universal
Sports.content:
A new season is supposed to be about renewed hope and optimism, a fresh campaign opening up a world of possibilities, a clean slate. But with the English Football League due to kick off on Friday night when Wolves host Blackburn in the Championship, the sense of rejuvenation is not universal.

The lineup of Championship teams this season is fearsome. Wolves and West Ham, hitherto established Premier League clubs, have dropped into the second tier. Others such as Burnley, Middlesbrough and Southampton anticipate a promotion push. So perhaps supporters of those who are not enjoying parachute payment riches and squads still packed with top-flight talent are wise to feel cautious. Some fear a long slog of a season to come.

Blackburn fans, for example, saw their side scrape to the safety of a 20th-place finish last season, therefore would be forgiven for tempering their expectations before the trip to Molineux. Tony Mowbray has been brought back to Ewood Park as an experienced guiding hand, but the 62-year-old has a huge task to avoid a relegation battle.

Fans believe the Rovers owners and the club’s head of football operations, Rudy Gestede, have sold Mowbray short on players heading into the season, particularly in midfield. The 34-year-old Sam Morsy – described by Mowbray as “a real man, a soldier” – has added steel to that area of the pitch with his free transfer, but after Moussa Baradji and Jayden Fevrier he is only the third addition at Blackburn this summer. Mowbray wants and needs more.

“I’m a bit greedy for good players,” he said. “I keep saying to Rudy: ‘I just want good players, doesn’t really matter where they come from, what age they are.’ I want to see personality on the pitch, players who are desperate to win.”

Blackburn edged past Burton 2-1 in the Carabao Cup first round last week, though they required late goals from Andri Gudjohnsen and Fevrier, who Mowbray believes can bring “magic” on the right wing after signing from Stockport.

View image in fullscreen Bolton Wanderers celebrated victory in the League One playoff final but a tricky season lies ahead. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Down the road, there are two other Championship clubs feeling a similar sense of trepidation before the new campaign, and they meet at the Toughsheet Stadium on Saturday lunchtime, a game that could set the tone for their seasons. Bolton should still be on cloud nine; they finished last season with a 4-1 demolition of Stockport in the League One playoff final. Yet as the football world has witnessed this summer at York – where the manager, Stuart Maynard, was sacked and replaced by Scott Lindsey, despite winning the National League with 108 points – the afterglow of promotion can be short-lived. Reality bites quick.

And such is the chasm between the second and third tiers nowadays, the need for Steven Schumacher’s side to strengthen fast became paramount after that glorious day at Wembley. David Watson, Ben Davies, Akin Famewo, Luca Stephenson, Kyliane Dong and Gaizka Larrazabal have all arrived, but there is a feeling among the fanbase that a marquee addition is needed, especially in attack where they risk asking too much of the striker Sam Dalby. Schumacher’s admission last week that Bolton “can’t afford to waste money” rang alarm bells with the fanbase. There is not an embarrassment of riches in the pot but forward players must be signed.

“We know we’re short, especially at the top end of the pitch,” Schumacher said. “Our budget isn’t massive so we need to make sure we get the right players in, rather than just signing anybody to fill numbers. We need to try and consolidate this year, rebuild, get some more finances behind us, bring in a better squad that can keep us at this level, and then kick on.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Schumacher said that “this part of the journey is an exciting one” but it seems negativity among some fans has kicked in before a Championship ball has been kicked. A 1-0 defeat against Sheffield Wednesday in the Carabao Cup reinforced concerns around goalscoring, or the lack of it. Max Dean of Gent is coveted, but the striker is just 22 and his English football experience is limited to a short spell at MK Dons.

Preston will hope to take advantage of the uncertainty around Bolton on Saturday, but Paul Heckingbottom has endured his own problems in the transfer market this summer. A public spat with Ben Whiteman over the midfielder’s desire to join Wrexham left a cloud hanging above the club and saw the Lilywhites lose their club captain. Heckingbottom said Whiteman “crossed a line” and was frustrated by the saga.

Money has been spent at Deepdale this summer with Alfie Devine brought in from Tottenham for a fee in the region of £6m, while Callum Lang “feels like a new signing” according to Heckingbottom, having arrived in January for around £2m before getting injured. So the pressure is on Heckingbottom perhaps like never before. A run of just four wins from their final 20 matches of last season prompted a few fan murmurs of discontent towards the manager. With Preston almost investing £1.5m to install a modern hybrid pitch at Deepdale, the club expect better than last season’s 14th-place finish, but expectations can weigh heavy.

Sports.title: ‘It is just smelling football’: Tielemans says adjusting to life at United has come naturally
Sports.content:
Youri Tielemans has stated that adjusting to Michael Carrick’s vision for Manchester United has been as easy as “smelling football” for the vastly experienced £35m midfield signing.

The 29-year-old, who joined from Aston Villa last month, made his debut for Anderlecht at the age of 16. He has been integrating with the United squad during the past 10 days of the club’s pre-season tour, making his first appearance in the 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on Saturday.

Tielemans left Belgium for Monaco in 2017 and joined Leicester in 2019, before signing for Villa four years later and has 579 career appearances, so any demands from Carrick do not faze him.

Tielemans said: “He has got his structure. He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways, you know. It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht.

“So for me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together. Then when you follow those principles, then you can add your offensive qualities, especially in the last third where everything is a bit more in freedom, without obviously overcommitting and keeping the defensive line in place, then I think we can do good things.”

Tielemans was limited to only 25 starts in the Premier League last season because of injury and also sustained a hamstring problem in the warm-up before Belgium’s World Cup quarter-final against Spain in July. Yet despite this and having already played for 13 years in midfield, Tielemans denied that Carrick will need to rest him on occasion.

He said: “Not really. The thing is, at the World Cup, I think we played 120 minutes against Senegal [before Spain], and from there we had less time in between games. So we played the US I think three or four days later [actually five days] and then three days later we played against Spain. In the warm-up, my body just switched off for some reason. Now, I do not think I am a player that I absolutely need a rest. Obviously, there are a lot of games and the manager needs to manage the team, but when I am good I am good, you know.

“Unfortunately, my body is … when it does not go well, then I will know straight away and I will alert the manager, but it does not happen often.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United previously showed interest in signing the Belgium captain, reportedly in 2019 and 2022. “There has been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve to anything, so I was just very calm about it. It was way after Anderlecht,” Tielemans said.

United, who triggered his release clause, did not face any competition to sign the player. “Not that I am aware of, no,” Tielemans said.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold told why Real Madrid career is not over despite Denzel Dumfries transfer
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold told why Real Madrid career is not over despite Denzel Dumfries transfer

Denzel Dumfries' arrival doesn't mean the end of Trent Alexander Arnold's Real Madrid career.

That's the view of Real Madrid writer for The Athletic Mario Cortagena, who suggested the former Liverpool star will be Jose Mourinho's initial first choice at right-back this season.



2 Alexander-Arnold faces right-back competition from Dumfries (pictured) Credit: Getty

It's been a summer of changes at the Bernabeu, with Jose Mourinho returning as head coach and Dumfries among a raft of new signings.

But the Netherlands right-back won't automatically take Alexander-Arnold's place in the team, believes Cortagena.

Asked by talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor if he worries about Alexander-Arnold's game time for the upcoming season, he said: "Not really, because obviously he will have to deliver.



"But if you remember the first reports from early May, when Mourinho had spoken to the club to making plans about the transfer market, it was clear that he wanted a back-up for the right-back position, while for the left-back position, since the beginning, he wanted potentially a starter left-back.

"So, his starter right-back is expected to be Trent Alexander-Arnold. He's happy with him, but again, obviously this is football and Dumfries is understood to be a strong competitor for Trent and he should deliver to keep his spot in the starting line-up."



Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid from Liverpool last summer and made 30 appearances in all competitions in his first campaign with the 15-time European champions.

However, the 27-year-old has found it tough going adapting to his new club, enduring an injury-disrupted season which ended with him being left out of England's squad for the 2026 World Cup.



And with Mourinho's return to the Bernabeu and his reputation for defensive football, doubts had been raised over Alexander-Arnold's future in the Spanish capital.

Indeed, talkSPORT's Angelina Kelly said earlier this month that Liverpool should be open to re-signing their academy graduate, whose departure from Anfield sparked an angry reaction from fans.

"I’m not saying you’ve got to sign him immediately – let’s just explore this. Because Real Madrid have signed another right-back in Denzel Dumfries – that is not good news for Trent," she explained.

2 Alexander-Arnold has been reunited with Ibrahima Konate at Real Madrid Credit: Getty



Dumfries is one of six signings Real Madrid have made in the current transfer window.

Among them is Alexander-Arnold's former Liverpool defensive teammate Ibrahima Konate.

He's joined by another defender, Spain World Cup winner Marc Cucurella, who has moved from Chelsea.

And Bernardo Silva, Carlos Espi and Yan Diomande have also made the switch to the Bernabeu.



Real Madrid kick off the new LaLiga campaign away to Espanyol on Saturday, August 22.

Before then, they have two more pre-season friendlies against Deportivo A Coruna and Schalke.

Sports.title: ‘That is the problem’ – Arsenal and Man United scouts urged to wait for Brazilian talent
Sports.content:
‘That is the problem’ – Arsenal and Man United scouts urged to wait for Brazilian talent

Manchester United and Arsenal target Kaua Elias' movement is terrific - he can go a long way.

That is the verdict of European football expert Andy Brassell, who hailed the Shakhtar Donetsk striker for his start to the season.

3 Manchester United and Arsenal have been linked with a move for Shakhtar Donetsk sensation Kaua Elias Credit: Getty

Man United and Arsenal scouts were reportedly in attendance to watch Elias score a 'perfect' hat-trick at the start of last week.

Representatives for the two Premier League giants were in the stands for Shakhtar's first league game against Kudrivka.

Man United and Arsenal scouts watch summer target Kaua Elias

Elias, who is said to be valued at £30million and is also being eyed by Serie A giants AC Milan, took home the matchball in a 5-1 demolition.

However, Brassell wants to see the 20-year-old cut his teeth in the Champions League first instead of making the move this summer.

Shakhtar punched their ticket automatically for the league phase due to having the highest coefficient of all the clubs currently top of their domestic leagues from associations 11–55, since last season's finalists Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal have already qualified via their domestic league position.

It will be Elias' first appearance in the Champions League, having only arrived at Hirnyky (The Pitmen) in February 2025 from Fluminense.

On the small sample size involved, Brassell exclusively told talkSPORT: "I think that is the problem.

"Like when you look at Shakhtar's golden era - going back into the Mircea Lucescu years, when they were still in Donetsk.

"Then it was different because Shakhtar were a genuinely huge club that was on its way to becoming a European superpower, and I think you knew from the quality, not just the quality of the Ukrainian league then but the quality of their performances in the Champions League, that you were getting guys that were ready to go.

3 Shakhtar reached the semi-finals of last season's Conference League Credit: Getty

"So when you bought a Fernandinho, [or] Willian - they were like ready now," Brassell continued to talkSPORT.com.

"It's so hard to judge the level effectively of Ukrainian domestic football now through no fault of Ukraine's own or through no fault Shakhtar's obviously but that they are really living in extraordinary times and very difficult conditions and Shakhtar in a league with a lot of teams that would not be anywhere near the Premier League, if we were comparing it, which I'm always bit loathe to do.

"But the reality is Ukraine is not one of the top leagues at the moment, so I think you need to see them a little bit more in European competition.

"That's certainly the case with Kaua Elias.

"His movements terrific. I really like what I've seen of him, but again, I want to see him in the Champions League first."

Elias scored twice in five Europa League qualifying appearances last term, before finding the net the same number of times in Shakhtar's run to the Conference League semi-finals.

3 Shakhtar have been forced to play their European 'home' matches in Poland last season Credit: Getty

The Brazil Under-17 international registered an assist in the 3-1 home defeat to eventual tournament winners Crystal Palace in April.

But on Shakhtar's return to the Champions League, Brassell added: "To see them in that sort of context would be really important.

"Now bear in mind, say when Kevin came over to Fulham, and that's Fulham, not Arsenal or United, we'd seen some of him in European competition.

"So you knew that not only what he was able to do in there in the Ukrainian Premier League, but you'd seen a bit of him in Europe and you thought okay, this is something we can work with here.

"But this is Shakhtar's model now, to go out and buy really young players from Brazil, so a sort of accelerated version of the model that they used to do when they were in Donetsk and be able to inflate them into players that they can sell for three/four times that sort of money.

"Of course, they need to sell to survive, whereas before it was about selling to satisfy the dreams of those players and go and buy the next lot of players.

"It wasn't such a financial imperative because they were in a better financial position. The owner, Rinat Akhmetov, was in a better financial position.

"The country was in a better financial position, and the league was in a better financial position.

"But a great start to the season for Kaua; I think he can go a long way, but yeah, I need to see him in the Champions League first."

Sports.title: Leeds handed warning over signing one of the best free agents around
Sports.content:
Leeds handed warning over signing one of the best free agents around

Leeds United have been told not to expect too much too soon if they manage to sign defender Diogo Leite.

The Whites have been linked with a move for the centre-back, who is available to pick up on a free transfer after his Union Berlin exit.



2 Leite is one of the most highly coveted free agents still available on the market right now Credit: Getty

Leeds' German boss Daniel Farke will be more than aware of the 27-year-old, who made 23 Bundesliga appearances last season.

Leite started his career in his native Portugal at Porto, before being loaned out to Braga and Union Berlin - with the latter signing him on a permanent deal in 2023.

The Portuguese Under-21 international helped the club secure Champions League qualification for the first time in its history.



He became a free agent at the end of his Union Berlin contract in June, and Leeds have been touted as among his potential suitors.

European football expert Andy Brassell believes Leite is 'one of the better free agents out there', but it won't be until the September international break when Leeds can start to reap the benefits.



"He's been so solid in the Bundesliga over the last couple of years now," Brassell exclusively told talkSPORT.com.

"I think it's hard to leave a big club like Porto and to really knuckle down and make a good career at not one of the biggest clubs in another league, which is what he's done at Union Berlin.



"He's been ultra reliable. He's strong. I think he could deal with the tempo of the Premier League.

"The Bundesliga is quite good prep for that as well. I think it'll be hard for him having not had a proper preseason.

"So if they're gonna sign Leite, I would have thought it would be like sort of mid-September, until we see the best of him, but he's definitely one of the better free agents out there."

2 Leite has made over 100 Bundesliga appearances but will be severely lacking match sharpness Credit: Getty



Leeds transfer news

Farke has been active in the market this summer, with Tarik Muharemovic coming in to replace Pascal Struijk.

James Trafford has completed a club-record £40million switch from Manchester City a year on from rejoining the Etihad set-up.

Leeds also beat out plenty of Premier League competition to pick up Harry Wilson following his release from domestic rivals Fulham.

The Welsh international was one of the standout figures in the top-flight last term, scoring 10 goals and assisting seven more.



However, Leeds passed on the opportunity to sign AC Milan's Rafael Leao, who was offered to the Elland Road club earlier this month.

Sports.title: Michail Antonio trains with EFL club as he looks to make return to English football
Sports.content:
Michail Antonio trains with EFL club as he looks to make return to English football

Add us as preferred source

Michail Antonio is training with Watford in a bid to earn a permanent deal with the club.

The 36-year-old is a free agent after leaving Qatari outfit Al Sailiya earlier this year.

3 Antonio is training with Watford as he looks to earn a permanent deal Credit: Getty

Antonio joined the club in February on a short-term deal, which expired at the end of the season.

After four appearances for Al Sailiya, he is now looking to secure a return to English football.

Antonio trains with Watford

Antonio is currently training with the Hornets, having been pictured at their Hertfordshire base.

The Jamaica striker could be handed a deal by the Championship side if he impresses manager Alessio Dionisi.

It comes after sporting director Luke Dowling revealed last week that the club need to sign a new striker.

Dionisi currently has three senior centre-forwards at his disposal in the form of Luca Kjerrumgaard, Mamadou Doumbia and Iker Bravo.

However, the trio are all aged 23 or under, with experience needed ahead of the new campaign.

Antonio has 142 Championship appearances to his name across spells with Sheffield Wednesday, Nottingham Forest and Reading.

Those matches saw the forward score a total of 28 goals in the division.

Meanwhile, he is West Ham's all-time leading scorer in Premier League history with 68 strikes in 268 outings.

3 Watford sporting director Dowling has revealed the club need a new striker Credit: Rex Features

Antonio has not played in England since leaving the Hammers last summer.

His departure came seven months after he suffered a lower limb fracture following a car crash in December 2024.

He previously held talks with Charlton Athletic over a move before signing for Al Sailiya.

It came after a proposed deal with Leicester City fell through due to a training ground injury.

Since leaving his last club, Antonio has also been in negotiations with multiple EFL sides this summer.

His latest suitors Watford are set to begin their Championship campaign this weekend.

3 Antonio has been a free agent since leaving Al Sailiya at the end of June Credit: Getty

The Hornets host Southampton at Vicarage Road on Sunday, with kick-off at 1.30pm live on talkSPORT 2.

It follows their Carabao Cup first round victory over Crawley on Saturday.

This season marks the club's fifth consecutive campaign in the second-tier following relegation in 2022.

Sports.title: Liverpool handed huge boost in Bradley Barcola pursuit but Premier League rivals urged to hijack move
Sports.content:
Liverpool are in pole position to sign Bradley Barcola but Andy Brassell thinks Arsenal should hijack the move.

talkSPORT understands that the French international is a top target for the Reds, and he is expected to depart Paris Saint-Germain before the close of the transfer window.

3 Barcola is a lightning fast and direct forward Credit: AFP

However, after missing out on Vinicius Junior, the Gunners need another left-sided forward.

Arsenal had the capacity to make a move for the Brazilian, although this was never formalised, but he signed a new six-year deal at the Bernabeu instead.

But with Liverpool hesitating over PSG's asking price of between £130m and £140million, Brassell thinks Mikel Arteta's side should be all over it.

Speaking on The Transfer Insiders with Ben Fletcher and Jacob Hawley, Brassell said: "I know Liverpool seem to be in front for him, but if I am Arsenal, I chuck everything at him because he is the player out there who can really elevate them in a position they've needed to improve for a long time.

"He would take them up a level, and when you are in Arsenal's position of being one of the best teams in Europe, it is so difficult to get players who can actually make you better.

"I am not even sure that Bruno Guimaraes does that, but Barcola definitely would."

Comedian and huge Arsenal fan Hawley then wanted to know if Barcola is suited for the Premier League.

Brassell responded: "We have seen with France that he is able to deal with deep back lines, and that is what he has been doing with PSG every week in Ligue 1.

"So, he is useful against half-dead defenders on the counter-attack, but there is a lot more to his game as well.

"He's been playing for teams that are expected to win very week since the beginning of his career.

3 Barcola has Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ahead of him in the pecking order at PSG Credit: Getty

"I honestly think Barcola is more suited to what Arsenal are trying to do than Vinicius Junior.

"Vini needs a team built around him, Barcola, not so much. I think he fits what Arsenal are doing very nicely."

Outrageous fee?

Liverpool have spent huge money over the past 12 months with moves worth over £100million for Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz.

The Reds are hoping to reach a compromise with PSG, but if they don't, Brassell thinks the fee is more than fair.

"I think that's fair enough because you are looking at a guy who already produces at a very high level," he added.

"He's 24 and the ceiling is pretty high - he can get loads better.

3 Barcola has won back-to-back Champions League titles and has torn teams all over Europe apart Credit: Getty

"Goalscoring is not the main string to his bow, but he gets in double figures every season, but he can stretch the game, go both ways, beat a full-back and deliver the right ball.

"The coaching staff at PSG think that with the right work, they can turn him into a 30 goals a season guy, but he'll never get that chance at PSG.

"They have Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who is pretty close to being the best player in the world, so he can't complain about being behind him.

"But it has really stunted Barcola's development. He is not a better player than he was two years ago.

"What we have found is he has more ways to influence the game off the bench like he did with France during the World Cup."

Definitely moving

Barcola will be leaving the French capital this summer with PSG set to bring in two attacking options.

A deal between Barcelona and the champions of Europe is close to being concluded for Ferran Torres.

They've already signed Maghnes Akliouche as well, suggesting one of their forward players will have to depart.

Desire Doue starts more than Barcola, so it makes it likely to be the 23-year-old to be the one allowed to leave.

Sports.title: Six EFL games forced into late schedule change because of Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Six EFL games forced into late schedule change because of Carabao Cup

Chelsea and Fulham's Premier League clash has forced six EFL fixtures to change their dates.

The two top-flight clubs face each other on Monday, August 24, which forces both of their Carabao Cup second-round ties to be played on Thursday.



3 Fulham's opening Premier League game will be televised on Monday night

Following the second round draw on Monday night, it was revealed that Chelsea will play Luton at Stamford Bridge, while Fulham will go head-to-head against AFC Wimbledon at Craven Cottage.

Despite the fixture dates for the cup games being locked in two weeks ago, the Premier League fixture schedule has taken precedence and forced six League One matches to be changed.

With mid-week games in the lower league scheduled for the following week, it has left little room for fixture organisers.



The date adjustments are required to prevent any team from playing two matches within a 48-hour window.

Organisers also have to ensure that the subsequent midweek fixture in the third tier is shifted to Wednesday.



To complicate matters further, Fulham and Chelsea are not typically permitted to host matches on the same day due to their stadiums being in close proximity and the need to avoid overstretching local public services.

However, both Chelsea vs Luton and Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon will kick-off on Thursday, August 27, with only 30 minutes separating their start times.



This scheduling conflict has affected four League One clashes that were originally meant to be played on Tuesday, September 1, which have now been moved to Wednesday, September 2.

These fixtures include: Burton vs Wimbledon, Wigan vs MK Dons, Luton vs Stockport, Reading vs Mansfield.

Additionally, Wimbledon and Luton fixtures against Wigan and Mansfield that were meant to be played on Saturday, August 29 have been moved to Sunday, August 30.

3 Wimbledon have had to change three of their games, not even a month into the season Credit: Getty



Luton Town released a statement confirming the disruptions: "Our Carabao Cup second round tie at Chelsea will take place on Thursday 27th August with a 7:30pm kick-off.

Sports.title: Three Man United stars given huge target to compensate for glaring issue this season
Sports.content:
Three Man United stars given huge target to compensate for glaring issue this season

Matheus Cunha, Benjamin Sesko and Bryan Mbeumo must all contribute more than 15 goals this season, according to talkSPORT's Inside Devils panel.

The Red Devils entered the transfer window aiming to build on a successful campaign in which they secured a return to Champions League football under the guidance of former player Michael Carrick.



3 Kelly wants more than Cunha's ten goals and two assists last season Credit: Getty

So far, United have strengthened their midfield with the arrivals of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

Additionally, recruitment in recent seasons has left their attacking rank well-stocked, bolstered further by the return of Marcus Rashford.

However, defensive options remain light, despite persistent interest in Newcastle United's Lewis Hall and Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.



Carrick will have a core unit of five centre-backs to rotate: Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven, Harry Maguire, Matthijs De Ligt, and Lisandro Martínez.

Nevertheless, the manager may have lingering concerns about the overall depth across his back four.



Speaking on Inside Devils, Angelina Kelly expressed her concerns regarding the squad balance: "The squad is starting to look good, but it’s extremely top-heavy.

"When you look at those forward options, everyone needs to be firing on all cylinders. You look at the likes of Amad and Mbuemo, after AFCON, they did struggle.



"However, you look at those two, you look at Cunha, Sesko, and even Rashford and they need to be top. Especially Cunha, Sesko, and Mbuemo - they all need to be aiming for 15-20 goals at least.

"We are going to struggle defensively because we don’t have all the necessary tools at our disposal. We do have a little bit of squad depth, but we’ve seen Leny Yoro make mistakes. Is Ayden Heaven going to be playing week in, week out? Maybe?

"There are leaks in that defence, and we need our forwards to step up this season, they need to be aiming for 15 goals at least."

3 Maguire and Yoro offer a blend of experience and young talent Credit: Getty



What are the leaks in defence?

Yoro and Heaven are both 20 and 19-years old respectively, and both are still in the early stages of their development.

Yoro has already appeared 66 times since arriving from Lille in July 2024, though his game remains susceptible to the occasional error.

Heaven made just 11 league starts last season and has openly noted that he is still waiting for his main breakthrough opportunity.

At the opposite end of the spectrum, Maguire is at the tail-end of his career at 33 years old, yet he is still expected to start the campaign as the first-choice defender.



Meanwhile, De Ligt's physical condition remains an issue as the 26-year-old has not featured for the Red Devils since November 2025 due to a back injury that was finally operated on in May.

What was United's attacking record last season?

Mbuemo, Sesko, and Cunha all reached double figures last season, but supporters are demanding an even higher output.

3 Nine of Benjamin Sesko's 11 goals last term came in the second half of the season under Carrick's management Credit: Getty

Bruno Fernandes and Casemiro were close behind with nine goals apiece, but the front three will need to absorb an extra goalscoring burden following the Brazilian's departure.



Unlike last term, United will be juggling a congested calendar that includes mid-week European fixtures.

If Carrick's side are to mount a serious challenge for silverware, improving their goal difference will be paramount.

Last season, Premier League champions Arsenal netted 71 times while conceding just 27 goals.

Similarly, Pep Guardiola's Manchester City scored 77 goals across their league fixtures, shipping 35 at the other end.



There was a noticeable drop-off to Carrick's third-placed side, who managed an impressive 69 goals, albeit conceding 50.

Sports.title: Why some Manchester United players will have been denied Champions League wage increase
Sports.content:
Why some Manchester United players will have been denied Champions League wage increase

Qualification for the Champions League has provided financial boosts to the Manchester United squad, but some players have missed out.

Football finance expert Stefan Borson has explained how changes to contracts have prohibited universal wage increases at Old Trafford.



3 United qualified for the Champions League thanks to an excellent second half of the season Credit: Getty

A third-place finish in the Premier League last season granted United a place in the 2026/27 Champions League league phase.

Having won 12 of their 17 league matches under Michael Carrick once he was named as head coach in January, they comfortably finished in the top five.

Many top clubs offer financial incentives to players as part of their deals, which Champions League qualification one example of this.



United will have been no different with their players, but a few will not have benefited from their achievement last season.

How does United's wage increase work?

When discussing wage increases for Champions League qualification on talkSPORT Breakfast, Borson said: "They've got a number of players who will be on a 25 per cent uplift...



"20, 25 per cent, we'll see it in the accounts, we don't know exactly what it is. But apparently what they've done going forward is they've tweaked a lot of, even those contracts.

"If you haven't played in the team that qualified, then you're not automatically entitled to the uplift."



As per the Daily Telegraph, those who played 60 per cent of last season's games will have earned a wage increase from the European qualification.

This criteria is said to have been introduced as they found it difficult to sell players who were on higher wages via the increase.

Marcus Rashford has still earned a recent rise, despite not playing for United amid his loan spell at Barcelona.

3 Although he was at Barcelona, Rashford has still had a wage increase Credit: Getty



However, this is because the contract that he signed in July 2023 was finalised before the club brought in their new requirements.

"Yes, Rashford will be, because he's got one of the older contracts," Borson explained.

"But a player that didn't play very much last season may not be entitled to the uplift."

How do United's wages compare to Premier League rivals?

Earlier on the Breakfast show, United We Stand editor Andy Mitten claimed that the club are 'constrained financially'.



He added: "Long gone are the days, and it's pretty sobering as a Manchester United fan, that they can go to the biggest clubs and take some of their best players."

Although he believes that limited spending may only be temporary, Borson explained why they haven't been as strong in the market in comparison to past seasons.

3 Borson has explained the way structure at United under INEOS Credit: Getty

"You've had a private equity owner in INEOS come in, and they have a different approach.



"They think they can do it in a more conventional private equity manner, where they can beat the market by spending less than the market, they can reduce the wage bill, they can be smarter in the transfer market, we'll see if it works.

"No club has sustained success at the top of the game with a wage bill that's going to be 25, 30 per cent lower than (Manchester) City, Liverpool, Arsenal.

"That's what United are trying to do this season. Can they do it? It's going to be a challenge. They're going to have 60 games, not 40. Is the squad going to be big enough?

"Is the squad going to be a high enough quality? That's going to be their challenge. But I think, for now, what they're trying to do is right size the wage bill that they believe is the right size, which is closer to the sort of Tottenham Hotspur history.



"But it's miles away from where City... City are going to be close to a £500million wage bill going into this season. Liverpool are going to be close to £500million, Arsenal are going to probably be at £425million, £450million, depending on what happens in the transfer market.

"Manchester United are probably going to be around about £325million, £350million, a big difference.

"And that's going to be their big challenge, can they sustain top-four football with just a much lower cost base?"

Sports.title: Ryan Lochte's ex-wife opens up on 'ticking time bomb' marriage to Olympic legend in explosive tell-all interview
Sports.content:
Ryan Lochte's ex-wife opens up on 'ticking time bomb' marriage to Olympic legend in explosive tell-all interview

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ryan Lochte's ex-wife Kayla Reid has broken her silence on the bitter collapse of their eight-year marriage, labeling the relationship as a 'ticking time bomb'.

In an explosive new tell-all interview with PEOPLE following the finalization of their divorce, the 35-year-old former model opened up about the hidden turmoil that ultimately drove her to walk away from the 12-time Olympic medalist.

Reid revealed that despite portraying a united front publicly, she wrote in her personal journal years ago that their marriage was destined to explode, confessing that she now realizes: 'I don't think it was a love anyone deserved.'

'I'm thankful that I'm no longer in that place,' Reid said after settling the split. 'What I was living I thought was good, but there were a lot of things that I didn't know were happening. It's a question that I actually have: What was real? What wasn't?'

The couple first met in early 2016 after Lochte sent Reid a message on Instagram, leading to a whirlwind romance that saw them tie the knot in 2018 shortly after welcoming their first child, Caiden.

However, Reid alleged that the serial infidelity began early on, claiming she was bombarded with photos of Lochte snuggled up to another woman while she was pregnant with their son after he attended a friend's wedding alone.

Ryan Lochte's ex-wife Kayla Reid has broken her silence on the collapse of their marriage

The 35-year-old former model opened up about the hidden turmoil that ultimately drove her to walk away from the 12-time Olympic medalist

View this post on Instagram

'When I confronted him [about whether he cheated], he said, 'Absolutely not, that didn't happen,' she recalls, admitting that she believed his response.

However, she stated that a similar pattern repeated in 2023 while she was pregnant with their daughter Georgia, when she discovered a scantily clad selfie on his phone from a woman at his gym.

'I couldn't believe it,' Reid recalled. 'Here I was again. I felt immense guilt and shame that I wasn't a good wife... So I sat there and sobbed and apologized.'

In addition to infidelity, Reid detailed alleged substance abuse inside their household, claiming she found evidence of Lochte using cocaine in daughter Liv's bedroom and using nitrous oxide - commonly known as whippets - in front of their children.

Lochte has previously admitted to his drug usage but has adamantly denied using substances in front of his children.

The strained relationship escalated following a near-fatal car crash in late 2023 when Lochte smashed his vehicle into a parked garbage truck, leaving him bed-bound with a broken femur while Reid served as the sole caregiver and provider.

The ultimate breaking point arrived in January 2025 when Reid issued an ultimatum with their therapist, demanding Lochte enter a 30-day inpatient rehab facility and complete marriage counseling.

'He screamed, said he wasn't going to rehab, he didn't have a problem,' Reid revealed. 'I called the attorney and filed for divorce.'

Lochte is now engaged to kindergarten teacher Molly Gillihan (pictured) following his divorce

Lochte is seen with new partner, Molly, and his three children

Reid claimed the subsequent 18-month legal battle was brutal, stating Lochte attempted to push her into signing an NDA and accepting a proposed $25,000 buyout in exchange for custody of their three young children.

Responding to the allegations, Lochte issued a statement acknowledging past mistakes while defending his actions during the split.

'Over the past several years, I've taken responsibility for the mistakes I've made and have spoken openly about some of the lowest moments in my life,' Lochte said. 'Looking back, I wasn't ready to be a husband or the man my family deserved at that point in my life. That's on me.'

The 42-year-old swimmer - who has since relocated to Missouri to coach college swimming - insisted that the request for an NDA was solely meant to keep the drama away from their children.

'Any discussion about a confidentiality agreement was never about hiding the truth or protecting my reputation,' Lochte added. 'It was about protecting my children from exactly this kind of situation. I've always believed that my children's privacy should come before headlines.'

Lochte has since moved on and is engaged to new fiancee Molly Gillihan, who also issued a statement pushing back on Reid's claims that she broke up the marriage, stating they only reconnected after the divorce was underway.

Meanwhile, Reid retains primary custody of their children - Caiden, 9, Liv, 7, and Georgia, 3 - and is channeling her energy into real estate and co-hosting a new podcast, The Comeback Era.

'I get to have a second chance at life and love,' Reid concluded, revealing a friend recently gifted her a cake that simply read: 'And she lived happily ever after.'

Sports.title: Inter close in on Djed Spence, Aston Villa line up move for West Ham star and Chelsea sign Marc Cucurella replacement: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Inter close in on Spence

Tottenham and Inter Milan are in the final stages of negotiations over the sale of Djed Spence.

Inter have made an offer worth around £26.9million.

The 26-year-old emerged as a target for the Serie A champions prior to the World Cup but his performances for England convinced Inter further.

They initiated contacts in June for him, teammate Cristian Romero and free agent John Stones.

The latter has already joined and Inter also want to add Liverpool's Curtis Jones.

Talks for Spence advanced this morning and the fee is around £26.9m plus £4m in add-ons and a 10percent sell on.

Spence has agreed to the move and is waiting for permission to travel.

The defender previously enjoyed time in Italy while on loan with Genoa for six months from January 2024.

Inter have also agreed a deal to send Davide Frattesi on loan to Lazio with an obligation to buy at £11m. They hope that deals gives them room to buy Jones from Liverpool but they will have to meet Liverpool's valuation which has been £35m. Their last offer via intermediaries was considerably short of that.

Palace set to sell another youngster

Belgian top-flight side Cercle Brugge are working on a six-figure deal to sign Tayo Adaramola from Crystal Palace.

The 22-year-old Palace academy product is in the final year of his contract, having spent six loan spells away from the club since 2022 and impressed at Sheffield Wednesday in the second half of last season.

Adaramola made his senior international debut this year, starting in the Republic of Ireland’s 5-0 win over Grenada in May.

He is expected to become the third academy player sold this summer, with Mofe Jemide set to join Alverca after Danny Imray joined Wrexham for £5million.

EXCLUSIVE BY BOBBY MANZI

Chelsea sign Marc Cucurella replacement

Chelsea have signed Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria on a five-year deal for a fee of around £16.3m plus add-ons.

The 28-year-old replaces Marc Cucurella, who signed for Real Madrid earlier this summer in a £55.8m deal.

After signing his five-year deal, Chavarria told club media: 'I'm so excited to get started.

'This is a dream for me as Chelsea are one of the biggest clubs in the world. This is one of the best days of my life,' added the 28-year-old.

'It is a big opportunity but I am prepared and will work hard to help the team achieve success.

'There are a lot of people who have helped me get to this moment and I have to thank my family. They have always supported me and today is only possible because of them.'

Chelsea have signed Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria on a five-year deal

Toon press on with Benfica target

Newcastle United are pressing ahead with talks to sign Amar Dedic from Benfica.

The 23-year-old right-back played for new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle at RB Salzburg.

Dedic has been capped 31 times by Bosnia and is valued around £25m.

Newcastle continue to work on a new midfielder too.

Camara never lies

Crystal Palace have held further talks with Monaco over 22-year-old midfielder Lamine Camara.

The clubs have been discussing a £40million deal for the Senegal international who has also been tracked by Chelsea, Newcastle and Manchester United.

Camara impressed in Monaco's friendly against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Monaco are understood to want a fee in excess of £50m for the midfielder who has three years left on his contract.

Palace have also spoken about France international Youssouf Fofana who is available from AC Milan.

Wrexham's Souttar bid

Wrexham are making a £7.5million bid for Leicester City defender Harry Souttar.

The Australia international is also a target for Sheffield United.

The Welsh side also made an offer for Viking Stavanger defender Henrik Falchener which was rejected.

Leicester manager Russell Martin, when asked about Souttar's future, said: 'He captained the team on Saturday. He will captain the team this Saturday. He's been amazing since we've been in.

'Since he came back from the World Cup, he's a proper character. So it wouldn't surprise me that people are interested in him.

'As far as we've had a couple of bids, but they were nowhere near the valuation of the club and what we value him at.

'So that might change. Who knows? But whilst he's here, and I've said this to everyone, we've had other people who have had interest from us, other players, and we've had bids and all that sort of stuff, and lots of talk around different players.'

Villa Wan him

Aston Villa are discussing a move for West Ham right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

The 28-year-old is ready to leave West Ham to stay in the top flight and has been considered as a new addition by a number of clubs including Arsenal but Villa are understood to be in pole position.

The Congo international has also been linked with Everton but manager David Moyes is exploring other options.

Aston Villa are discussing a move for West Ham defender Aaron Wan-Bissaka

Villa are in the process of signing Matteo Ruggeri from Atletico Madrid to strengthen their left back options and now Wan-Bissaka looks a strong option for their right-back berth.

They have previously discussed Emerson Royal at Flamengo.

The Eagle has landed... again!

Evann Guessand has rejoined Crystal Palace on a season-long loan from Aston Villa.

Guessand spent the second half of last season on loan at Selhurst Park, playing 14 times as Palace won the UEFA Conference League.

Palace chose not to exercise his option to buy at the end of last season’s loan but remained open to the possibility of Guessand returning on loan. This switch also includes an option to buy.

Palace initially chased the Ivorian on a permanent deal last summer, but he opted to join Aston Villa - where he made just 21 appearances - in a £30million deal from Nice.

Rejoining Palace, Guessand said: ‘I'm so happy to be here. I already have good memories here – but I think it's only the beginning. I hope many more are coming.’

BOBBY MANZI

Spurs youngster heading to Belgium

Tottenham winger Yang Min-Hyeok has joined KVC Westerlo in Belgium on loan for the 2026/27 season.

Yang, 20, signed for Spurs in July 2024 but completed the season in South Korea and moved to London in January 2025. He has been on loan at QPR, Portsmouth and Coventry.

Spurs have a close relationship with Westerlo. Alfie Devine and Luka Vuskovic are among those who have been loaned there.

MATT BARLOW

City land Geronimo

Manchester City have signed goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille for £1.7million.

The 34-year-old Argentina international has signed a two-year deal and provides cover after James Trafford was sold to Leeds for £40m plus £5m in add ons.

Rulli spent the 2016-17 season at City without making a first-team appearance, playing on loan at Real Sociedad.

Manchester City have signed goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille for £1.7million

Till Douath do us part

Hull City have agreed a deal with RB Salzburg to sign midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath in a permanent move worth £3.5m.

The 23-year-old is travelling to Hull for a medical.Sunderland had also shown interest.

The France U21 international has one year left on contract at Salzburg and impressed in the second half of last season with a spell on loan at Le Havre where he was instrumental in them avoiding relegation.

Wolf at the door for Jordan James

Wolves are closing on a £10million deal for Rennes midfielder Jordan James.

The 22-year-old Wales international had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham also.

He impressed on loan at Leicester City last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games.

James first shot to prominence when he started out at neighbouring Birmingham City.

Munoz not Moyes' type

Everton manager David Moyes is an admirer of Crystal Palace’s Daniel Munoz but would prefer a more orthodox right-back rather than a wing-back.

Munoz could become available after Palace moved for 21-year-old winger and wing-back Anan Khalaili from Belgian club Union Saint-Gilloise.

The Israel international completed his medical at the weekend ahead of signing a five-year contract.

Flo no-go for Spurs

Tottenham maintain they are not pursuing a deal for Monaco’s former Arsenal striker Folarin Balogun.

Sports.title: Roger Federer LOSES his billionaire status after share price crash - leaving just eight athletes on list of the world's richest men
Sports.content:
Roger Federer LOSES his billionaire status after share price crash - leaving just eight athletes on list of the world's richest men

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roger Federer is no longer a billionaire after seeing a major price crash in sports brand On.

As detailed last year, Federer joined the 10-figure club with a net worth of $1.1billion (£813million), according to Forbes.

The publication attributed that wealth to his significant minority stake, estimated at three per cent, in Swiss shoe and apparel brand On - who he has been affiliated with since 2019. On's roster of tennis stars includes six-time grand slam winner Iga Swiatek, men's world No 9 Flavio Cobolli and teenage prodigy Joao Fonseca.

On went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021 and as of August 2025 had a market capitalisation of nearly $15billion (£11.1bn), with Federer's equity worth more than $375million (£277.3m).

However, on Tuesday, Federer lost his billionaire status when On's company share price plummeted by over 20 per cent.

Despite record sales, the result did not meet market expectations and On also lowered its revenue forecast.

Roger Federer has lost his billionaire status after seeing a major price crash in sports brand On

On, who sponsor tennis star Iga Swiatek, have seen their share price plummet by over 20%

And as a result, Federer lost $52m (£38.4m) to reduce his net worth to $952m (£704m), details Forbes.

The impact of this fall means there are only eight athletes now who are billionaires.

Fellow former tennis player Ion Tiriac ($2.3bn - £1.5bn) became the first to hit 10-monetary figures in 2007 when he began investing in real estate, car dealerships and financial services.

Basketball icon Michael Jordan followed seven years later with the six-time NBA champion now estimated to be worth $4.3bn (£3.3bn).

His 1992 Olympic gold-medal winning team-mate Magic Johnson is worth an estimated $1.6bn (£1.2bn). Meanwhile LeBron James is another basketballer on the list at $1.4bn (£1bn).

Golfing great Tiger Woods ($1.5bn - £1.1bn) and football icons Cristiano Ronaldo ($1.2bn - £900m), Lionel Messi ($1.1bn - £813m) and David Beckham ($1bn - £740m) complete the list.

James, Woods, Ronaldo and Messi are the only athletes to have joined the billionaire club while still active in their sports.

During his playing days, where he won 103 tournaments over a 24-year career, Federer earned nearly $131m (£97m) in prize money and made around $1bn (£739m) in pre-tax off-court earnings via multiple sponsorship deals.

Ex-tennis player Ion Tiriac became sport's first billionaire and is now worth $2.3billion (£1.5bn)

As a player, the icon earned nearly $131m (£97m) in prize money during a stellar 24-year career

That included $150m (£110m) from Nike over two decades to wear their apparel. He left them in 2018, after 24 years, to sign for Japanese brand Uniqlo in a 10-year deal worth $300m (£228m).

However, Uniqlo don't make footwear, allowing Federer to start his relationship with Zurich-based On.

Aside from his apparel and footwear deals, he has long-standing sponsorships including Lindt, Mercedes-Benz, Rolex and Moet & Chandon.

All of his off-court income allowed him to become the world's highest-paid tennis player for 16 consecutive years. Furthermore, in 2020, he was the highest-earning sportsperson with a then-$106.3m (£78.6m) estimated pre-tax.

Sports.title: New England captain Joe Root makes decision over team curfew - after Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson Chelsea nightclub incident led to questions over the team's alleged drinking culture
Sports.content:
Joe Root has ripped up England’s curfew rules just a month after they were drawn up.

Root, 35, takes charge of the first match of his second spell as Test captain next week and has confirmed the after-hours guidelines put together by director of cricket Rob Key will not be enforced.

Instead, he is telling his players to behave like ‘grown adults’ ahead of the series against Pakistan beginning in Leeds next Wednesday.

‘There's not going to be a curfew. I don't think this needs to be a big deal, to be honest,’ Root told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast.

‘My view on the curfew is that the players are doing their work, and if you want guys to take responsibility on the field, they've got to feel like they can be grown adults and make good, strong decisions off it.

‘That's for us as a team to manage well, and police well for me and Stephen Fleming.

'We should be known for how we play cricket and what we do on the field. We should be on the back page of papers.’

The stance taken by Root and incoming Test coach Fleming is a bold move, just weeks after the ECB hierarchy felt it necessary to spell out exactly what players could and couldn’t do - including a ban on drinking the day before, during and after international matches.

New England Test captain Joe Root has decided to ditch the team curfew

Former skipper Ben Stokes was dropped from the squad for the second Test against New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew following the first Test

Key went to the length of distributing this amongst all senior men’s cricketers following Daily Mail Sport’s story that Root’s predecessor Ben Stokes had no case to answer in the Cricket Regulator’s probe into being in a nightclub in Chelsea post-midnight following a Lord’s Test win over New Zealand because he did not believe a curfew was in place once a match had finished.

Following that, any member of full England squads were to inform management if they intended to be outside of the team hotel by 10pm.

However, Root insisted: ‘Be adults, look after yourselves, look after each other, create a good, strong culture where you know when the right time is to celebrate and enjoy a win or to have a sensible beer, but remember - you've got to play for England.

‘I don't want people to feel like they can't enjoy winning a Test match because they want to have a beer or at the right time let their hair down and then that's absolutely fine. We're human beings at the end of the day.

‘You know what your responsibilities are, you know how you need to prepare for a Test match and what it takes, and the effects that these things can have on you. So be smart, be sensible, and just be an adult.’

An ECB spokesman told Daily Mail Sport: ‘We have a Test captain and coach, who are looking at how they set team standards and culture.

As part of this, the curfew will no longer be in place.

‘We will ensure all players have a clear understanding of expectations when they come together for the upcoming Test series.’

Sports.title: Why 'overloaded' Youri Tielemans believes he can be Man United's marathon man: £35m star speaks for first time on Michael Carrick, beating Lionel Messi's record and Bruno Fernandes link-up
Sports.content:
When Youri Tielemans made his professional debut for Anderlecht against Lokeren, Michael Carrick, now his boss, still had five years left to run on his own playing career at Manchester United. That goes some way to underline Tielemans' longevity at the top.

Tielemans was a phenomenon in Belgium when he made his pro debut in 2013 aged 16. Only Lamine Yamal made double figures Champions League appearances at a younger age than Tielemans, who had achieved that by the time he was 17. At 18, he’d played more than 100 professional matches.

Now, at 29, with 668 career appearances in the legs, Tielemans is facing the very real prospect of surpassing Lionel Messi (701), and possibly Cristiano Ronaldo (720), for the most games played before he turns 30.

A return to the Champions League means United face a minimum 48-game season. The more likely number is somewhere in the mid-50s.

And so by the time a trip to Bournemouth comes on the final weekend of the season, Tielemans could well have cruised past Messi’s record. Deep runs in the cups and Ronaldo may be sweating too.

With that in mind, meet Manchester United’s new marathon man.

Youri Tielemans' longevity at the top since making his debut has been remarkable

The midfielder, still only 29, has made 668 career appearances already

Tielemans cannot stop smiling as he sits down to chat inside United’s five-star team base for this week’s training camp in Ireland.

There is plenty on the agenda: his first phone call with Carrick, his ‘really natural’ link-up with Bruno Fernandes, and also an insight into the role he expects to play for United this season.

But first it’s the issue of minutes, of wear and tear, and whether he can be counted on for what, if all goes to plan, could be a 60-odd game campaign for United.

‘Yes, I am [confident],’ he says defiantly. ‘I feel very good, actually. I had a little issue during the World Cup, which is sorted now, and I feel back 100 per cent fit.

‘Obviously, pre-season is all about building up fitness for the season, but, yeah, I feel great. I feel like I am ready to go, and in 10 days’ time [against Hull] we will be there.’

Tielemans is refreshingly honest. Thirteen years as a professional will do that.

He doesn’t shy away from the fact that he missed 21 games for Aston Villa last season through ankle and calf problems. Nor does he gloss over the fact he clocked up 62 appearances during a gruelling 2024-25 season.

At the World Cup this summer, Tielemans reached a limit that his body could not fight against.

‘It was just that last game,’ he explains. ‘It was just an overload of too many games, too many minutes, and unfortunately my body could not cope with it anymore.’

Tielemans senses a shift in the room as he, plainly, recounted Belgium’s final act in the United States.

But he knows his game, he knows his body, and where others hold reservations, he has trust and belief that, after signing a five-year contract, he’s still got plenty left in the tank.

‘The thing is, at the World Cup, I think we played 120 minutes against Senegal, and from there we had less time in between games,’ he continues.

‘So we played the US I think three or four days later, and then three days later we played against Spain. In the warm-up, my body just switched off for some reason.

Tielemans is part of the United squad on their pre-season tour of Ireland this month

‘Now, I do not think I am a player that I absolutely need a rest. Obviously, there is a lot of games and the manager needs to manage the team, but when I am good, I am good, you know… it does not happen often.’

There is a steeliness in Tielemans eyes that is befitting of someone who plays for a club the size of Manchester United. A club that, had things shaken out differently, he could have turned out for as early as 2019 when he was first approached.

That was when he was leaving Monaco, only for Tielemans end up at Leicester.

United came back in for him again in the summer of 2022, only to end up signing Casemiro and Christian Eriksen in central midfield instead. Tielemans would have been forgiven for thinking the opportunity to head to Old Trafford may have passed him by.

So, now he’s here, replacing the void left by Casemiro, does he feel any sense of pressure at stepping into the Brazilian’s shoes?

‘Not really, because we are all different players,’ Tielemans adds. ‘He has different qualities, he had a different career path than I have. I just try to be myself, to bring my own qualities to the team, and to enjoy my time here. But it does not add any pressure at all for me.’

At £35million, a release clause which we now know had been hiding in plain sight to the rest of the league, he is a bargain that those inside Manchester United believe could prove to be the pound-for-pound the league’s most valuable signing of the summer.

He played a central role in helping Aston Villa - a club he says he ‘owes the world’ for restoring him to his best level - win the Europa League against Freiburg in Istanbul and has the Premier League proven tag that Ineos and United hold in such high regard.

Beyond just the numbers, United have been crying out for a rhythm-setter. A metronome who can help the team control matches. In his own words, it’s the ‘smelling football’ philosophy Carrick is hoping to have Tielemans bring.

‘He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways,’ Tielemans explains, revealing one of his early tactical conversations with Carrick.

‘It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht. So for me, nothing changes.

‘But it just needs to gel together. When you follow those principles, then you can add your offensive qualities, especially in the last third where everything is a bit more about freedom, without obviously overcommitting and keeping the defensive line in place. Then I think we can do good things.’

Having played as a deep-lying defensive No 6, a box-to-box No 8 and more advanced as a No 10, what does Tielemans see as his best role to help take United back to the top?

The midfielder signed this summer from Aston Villa - a club he says he 'owes the world' to for helping to reignite his career

‘I just try and play forward as much as I can,’ he says, ‘either to Bruno [Fernandes] or the front line, to try and put them in positions that they can attack with freedom and that they can create and use their qualities.

‘I have played different roles in my career. So yeah, I am not just glued to one system or one role. I try and do a bit of everything.

‘Being that link between the defence and the attack, I think that suits me the best.’

He will be a key mentor in a young group, too, alongside the likes of Tyler Fletcher (19), Kobbie Mainoo (21) and fellow new signing Andrey Santos (22).

‘I just try to be myself, and it all comes in a natural way,’ Tielemans concludes.

‘I do not try to boss anyone around because no one likes that anyway. So I just try to be myself, be natural, and then obviously with good performances it helps others to follow.’

Leading by example at the very top level is all Tielemans has known for the past 13 years. It’s why Messi, Ronaldo, a place in the record books, and the game’s biggest prizes, are all in his sights now he’s finally here at Manchester United.

Sports.title: The winners, losers and likely bolters for England's 2027 World Cup campaign from new EPS squad - and why this team badly needs an injection of fresh blood, writes ALEX BYWATER
Sports.content:
Once the management speak had been waded through, a clear picture emerged from England's 25-man list of enhanced Elite Player Squad (EPS) contracts for the upcoming season of who Steve Borthwick trusts for the 2027 World Cup.

The winners? Alex Coles, Seb Atkinson and Guy Pepper. The losers? Ollie Lawrence, Tom Roebuck and Elliot Daly. Tom Willis is also now absent after the No 8 decided to rule himself out of England contention by signing for Bordeaux.

Borthwick has not made wholesale changes to the core squad, who each receive in the region of £150,000 from the RFU and are managed more closely by the head coach and his staff. And an EPS contract is no guarantee of Test selection. But it does provide a clue as to what Borthwick is thinking.

Coles’ addition is the most noteworthy, after the Northampton lock’s impressive international progression in the past year. He’s been involved in all of England’s past 12 Tests and went well at lock in the summer’s Nations Championship matches while captain Maro Itoje was rested.

Coles’ development, the return to fitness of the hard-hitting George Martin and Ollie Chessum’s new position on the blindside flank means Borthwick is not short of lineout forwards. Like Chessum, Coles can also play in the back-row and such versatility can be invaluable at World Cups.

Itoje certainly has a job on his hands to return to the starting team, even if the most likely lock combination for the autumn will be him alongside Martin in the second row, with Chessum wearing No6.

Alex Coles’ addition is the most noteworthy, after the Northampton lock’s impressive international progression in the past year

Guy Pepper, who now has 15 caps, has been rewarded for his progress with an EPS contract

ENGLAND'S EPS CONTRACTS, 2026-27 Seb Atkinson (Gloucester), Fin Baxter (Harlequins), Ollie Chessum (Leicester Tigers), Alex Coles (Northampton Saints), Luke Cowan-Dickie (Sale Sharks), Tom Curry (Sale Sharks), Ben Earl (Saracens), Immanuel Feyi-Waboso (Exeter Chiefs), George Ford (Sale Sharks), Tommy Freeman (Northampton Saints), George Furbank (Harlequins), Ellis Genge (Bristol Bears), Jamie George (Saracens), Joe Heyes (Leicester Tigers), Maro Itoje (Saracens), George Martin (Saracens), Alex Mitchell (Northampton Saints), Asher Opoku-Fordjour (Sale Sharks), Guy Pepper (Bath), Henry Pollock (Northampton Saints), Henry Slade (Exeter Chiefs), Fin Smith (Northampton Saints), Marcus Smith (Harlequins), Will Stuart (Bath), Jack van Poortvliet (Leicester Tigers).

Coles, however, will certainly not give up his starting shirt without a fight. His ability to do the nasty, unseen work combined with the ball-playing ability he has honed winning two PREM Rugby titles with the Saints gives him a point of difference.

Alongside Coles, Gloucester centre Atkinson, Bath flanker Pepper, Leicester scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet and Sale prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour are all new faces on the EPS list.

Atkinson’s replacing of Lawrence as one of the centre options is also significant and a blow for the latter, though it may just provide the kick up the backside he needs to return to his best.

A year out from the World Cup, one of the biggest problems England have is that their midfield pairing is still as clear as mud. A fully firing Lawrence has to be in the mix.

On the whole, England’s squad is ripe for a bolter or two to come in and shake-up the established order – perhaps Northampton duo George Hendy and Archie McParland, or Harlequins' 20-year-old scrum-half Lucas Friday.

Noah Caluori and Benhard Janse van Rensburg could upset the apple cart and add an injection of fresh blood into the squad

Of the latest 25-man party, 20 were also named this time last year and the team then went on to produce the worst Six Nations in England’s history, losing four of the five matches.

Some have argued EPS contracts breed a degree of comfort in selection which should always be absent at international level. Borthwick clearly feels differently. He knows the ones he trusts and has kept the faith. Noah Caluori and Benhard Janse van Rensburg could upset the apple cart.

You get the feeling England would certainly benefit from an injection of fresh blood after a disappointing 2026. That needs to change because right now, it is hard to make a case for Borthwick’s men being genuine World Cup contenders.

Sports.title: What's really going on with Myles Lewis-Skelly: Why Arsenal may be forced to sell 19-year-old England star - and why £45m would be nowhere near enough
Sports.content:
What's really going on with Myles Lewis-Skelly: Why Arsenal may be forced to sell 19-year-old England star - and why £45m would be nowhere near enough

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Myles Lewis-Skelly's Arsenal future depends on key factors including compliance with UEFA spending rules and the ability to further strengthen the Premier League champions' squad, Daily Mail Sport understands.

Gunners fans were left stunned yesterday when it was reported that the club had invited offers for the 19-year-old academy product from Chelsea and Manchester United.

Arsenal have insisted that was not the case, however, an intermediary is believed to have told both clubs that the player would be available at the right price.

Sources have also disclosed that one of the main drivers behind the situation is UEFA’s rules on spending, which operate by the calendar year rather than season by season. That means that the summer window is the last opportunity to bring transfer revenue in, should it be needed. It is also the last chance to ship players out should you need to do so to facilitate more new arrivals.

A potential fee of £45million has been touted for Lewis-Skelly, who started in the Champions League final, however those with knowledge of the situation believe that the price would need to be considerably higher to convince Arsenal to sell.

Because Lewis-Skelly is a product of the club’s academy, any money received would be seen as ‘pure profit’ and come as a significant boost to the balance sheet. That element of the rules has seen other clubs reluctantly sell some of their prized, homegrown assets, to ensure compliance, such as Newcastle’s offloading of Elliot Anderson to Nottingham Forest in July 2024 (although that was to comply with Premier League rather than UEFA rules).

Arsenal fans were left stunned yesterday when it was reported that the club had invited offers for Myles Lewis-Skelly from Chelsea and Manchester United

United are in the market for a left back and are monitoring the situation

Arsenal have options. There are a number of players who are viewed as unlikely to play this season and, in a perfect world, they would depart ahead of Lewis-Skelly, who is liked by both Mikel Arteta and the club’s fans. It would not be a surprise to see Reiss Nelson and Gabriel Jesus, for example, leave the club this month.

However, the closer Arsenal get to deadline day on September 1 without others leaving, the more the likelihood of Lewis-Skelly departing increases.

As for interested parties, United are in the market for a left back and are monitoring the situation. Chelsea have completed a £16million deal for Spanish left back Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano but Lewis-Skelly may well be an intriguing prospect.

Earlier this month, Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for a fee of around £75million. In June, they also took the option to turn Piero Hincapie’s loan move from Bayer Leverkusen into a permanent transfer at a cost of £34.5million. They also paid £34million for Club Bruges forward Christos Tzolis, while last summer they spent around £250million on eight new players.

A spike in commercial activity and prize money from the Premier League title and run to last season’s Champions League final will have helped their position, although player bonuses have taken a sizeable chunk out of the coffers.

With regards to outgoings, the Premier League winners have brought in around £41million from the departures of Leandro Trossard, Jakub Kiwior and Christian Norgaard.
