Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: WBC Threatens Noel Mikaelian’s Title Over Jai Opetaia Fight
Sports.content:
King and Benavidez promoter Sampson Lewkowicz reached an agreement for Mikaelian to defend his WBC cruiserweight title against Benavidez in December in Glendale, Arizona. Zuffa Boxing subsequently announced Mikaelian against Opetaia for September 12 in Las Vegas on the Ryan Garcia-Conor Benn card.

Mikaelian is already training for Opetaia, Pugmire reports, giving the WBC reason to seek an answer in the coming weeks on which fight he intends to take.

Benavidez may already have an alternate route. He teased an announcement Tuesday, and Pugmire reports his next bout will likely be against WBC interim cruiserweight champion Michal Cieslak for the title.

The promotional situation remains unusual. King and Lewkowicz had already struck their agreement when Zuffa announced Mikaelian as Opetaia’s opponent. Mikaelian then began preparing for the September fight despite remaining WBC champion, with Benavidez positioned as his mandatory challenger.

If Mikaelian proceeds with Opetaia, the WBC can remove him and leave Benavidez and Cieslak to fight for the championship. That would give Mikaelian the Zuffa fight he is training for, but without the WBC belt.

Sports.title: Hearn Targets Brandon Moore Next For Teremoana
Sports.content:
“I think we might fight him next, Brandon Moore,” Hearn said after the fight. “We have really got to find someone. It’s so frustrating in Australia because no one wants to fight him.”

A fight with Moore (19-1, 10 KOs) would provide an obvious measuring stick. He defeated Savage by a 10-round unanimous decision last September, dropping him in the seventh. His lone defeat came against Richard Torrez Jr., who knocked him out in five rounds in 2024.

Hearn felt Savage became frightened once he experienced Teremoana’s power.

“I was disappointed Savage didn’t get [further]. I don’t blame him, but it was just the fear. His eyes were popping out of his head as soon as he felt the power.”

Teremoana hardly pressed the accelerator in the opening round, throwing only a handful of punches before hurting Savage with a right hand late. Hearn liked the patience he showed rather than immediately going for the finish.

“I saw a guy that was a little bit more experienced tonight. Sort of took his time. I mean, he could have really done it in 30 seconds.”

Getting meaningful rounds has become increasingly difficult. Hearn conceded that fans will question the quality of Teremoana’s opposition and said Matchroom has reached the point where the competition must increase.

“There’ll be a lot of the public that will say, ‘Well, who’s he fighting?’ And I get that as well. We’ve got to step up,” Hearn said. “We do really, really need rounds.”

Hearn wants Teremoana to fight twice more this year and believes another four or five bouts are needed before he challenges for a world heavyweight title. His target is the back end of 2027, when Teremoana will be 29.

“He needs someone that can take him five or six rounds,” Hearn said. “Sooner or later there’s going to be a 10-round, 12-round war in there, and he’ll be ready.”

Anthony Joshua has also taken notice of Teremoana.

“AJ said to me a few times, ‘What’s this Teremoana?’ I’m like, ‘He’s a fucking monster.’”

Hearn expects a different type of fight once Teremoana encounters heavyweights willing and capable of attacking him rather than simply trying to survive.

Sports.title: Teremoana Teremoana Crushes DeAndre Savage in Two
Sports.content:
Teremoana dictated the opening round, forcing Savage onto the defensive while patiently looking for an opening.

In the co-main event, Michael “Pretty Boy” Zerafa stopped Alejandro “El Venado” Ortiz after nine rounds of their scheduled 10-round middleweight bout.

Zerafa established his jab over the opening two rounds before Ortiz found more success in the third, landing several left hooks to the chin. Zerafa countered effectively and produced a strong fourth round.

Ortiz landed a hard right hand midway through the fifth, but Zerafa regained control in the sixth by increasing his output. The Australian broke through in the ninth, hurting Ortiz and overwhelming him with punches. Ortiz struggled back to his corner after the bell, and his team stopped the fight before the 10th round.

Jasmine Parr defeated Jemma Peart by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout.

Parr controlled much of the opening three rounds by outlanding Peart, who had greater success with her jab in the fourth. Parr occasionally switched to southpaw in the fifth and sixth while maintaining the higher work rate.

The seventh was the most competitive round before Parr closed strongly in the eighth. All three judges scored the bout 80-72.

At super middleweight, Jack Bowen stopped Dalielibieke at 2:15 of the seventh round.

Bowen used an effective jab early and rocked Dalielibieke with an uppercut in the second. Both connected with hard right hands late in the third before the exchanges became heavier in the fourth.

Another right uppercut from Bowen hurt Dalielibieke midway through the fifth. Dalielibieke responded with one of his better rounds in the sixth, but Bowen regained control in the seventh. A sustained combination prompted referee Paul Tapley to stop the contest.

Lekaysha Woodbridge defeated Sothia Sitthichai over five two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout. Referee Paul Tapley scored the fight 50-45 for Woodbridge.

Light heavyweight Omar El-Abdallah stopped Jordan Towns after three rounds of their scheduled five-round bout. The two were competitive through the opening three rounds, but Towns was unable to answer the bell for the fourth.

In welterweight action, Reube Thornberry stopped Lachlan Harrington at 1:40 of the second round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Sports.title: Jake Paul’s MVP Signs IBF Champion Elif Turhan
Sports.content:
Turhan gives Jake Paul’s promotion another major piece at 135 pounds. Caroline Dubois holds the WBC and WBO championships, while Stephanie Han owns the WBA belt.

That leaves MVP working with fighters who control all four major lightweight titles.

Turhan punched her way into that company last December in Monte Carlo. She broke down Brazilian Olympic gold medalist Beatriz Ferreira and forced a fifth-round stoppage to seize the IBF crown, registering the defining victory of her professional career.

She has since strengthened her position with wins over Taylah Gentzen in January and Gabriella Tellez in June.

Turhan brings pressure and finishing instinct to a division loaded with potential championship fights. She likes to close the distance, force exchanges and punish opponents once her combinations begin finding the target.

The Istanbul fighter becomes the first Turkish boxer to join MVP and follows Nicolson as the second addition produced by the promotion’s agreement with Matchroom.

Turhan believes the partnership can push her toward more championship opportunities.

“I am incredibly excited to be part of this powerful collaboration. This marks a major signal of the exciting initiatives we will undertake for women’s boxing globally, and I am deeply honored to be involved in this journey with all my strength and energy.”

Her next opponent has yet to be confirmed, but her ambitions reach beyond defending the IBF belt.

“I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major World Titles.”

That pursuit creates an obvious pressure point at lightweight. Dubois controls two belts, Han holds another and Turhan carries the IBF championship.

If MVP eventually matches its lightweight champions, Turhan will have to establish her pressure against fighters capable of controlling distance, countering her entries and punishing her on the way inside.

Sports.title: Teremoana vs. DeAndre Savage Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana improved to 12-0 with a second-round knockout of DeAndre Savage after another destructive heavyweight finish. Savage survived the opening round despite absorbing several heavy shots as Teremoana began finding his distance and opening up. That resistance ended quickly in the second. Teremoana cracked Savage with a big punch that buckled the American’s legs but left him standing. The Australian kept hunting the finish, dropped Savage moments later, and watched as he failed to beat the referee’s count. Savage became only the third opponent to take Teremoana beyond the opening round, but the extra three minutes merely delayed another knockout for the Australian heavyweight.

Michael Zerafa broke down Alejandro Ortiz for a stoppage victory on the Gold Coast after taking command in the later rounds. Zerafa began forcing Ortiz onto the back foot, then cracked him with a heavy shot in the seventh as the pressure increased. His corner demanded he keep letting his hands go while staying smart, telling him Ortiz was hurt whenever he opened up. Zerafa responded by pressing harder and keeping Ortiz under fire. The breakthrough came when Zerafa dropped Ortiz and immediately looked to close the show. Ortiz climbed off the canvas but remained hurt, and the fight was stopped soon afterward when he had taken enough. The victory gave Zerafa the result he needed after entering the fight under pressure and facing questions over his recent form.

Sports.title: Jack Dempsey’s Harry Wills Problem Never Went Away
Sports.content:
Following Jack Johnson’s 1910 victory over Jim Jeffries, racial violence erupted across the United States. The possibility of another Black heavyweight challenging a white champion encountered resistance from promoters, regulators, and others concerned about another interracial title fight.

Wills paid heavily for that environment.

A Dempsey-Wills fight nearly materialized in 1922 when promoter Tex Rickard selected a date and had tickets printed for a proposed bout in New Jersey. The promotion collapsed when the financing needed to meet Dempsey’s guarantee failed.

Another attempt ran into opposition in New York, where athletic commission chairman William Muldoon resisted an interracial heavyweight championship fight over concerns about racial unrest.

Dempsey also gave his critics ammunition. He drew the color line early in his championship reign before later changing his public position. His long stretches of inactivity intensified criticism that Wills was being denied an opportunity he had earned. Yet Wills himself resisted blaming Dempsey.

“My only regret in life is that I never got a shot at Dempsey, [and] I’m sure I could have beaten him,” Wills later said. “It wasn’t Jack’s fault. He wasn’t scared of anyone. He was a great fighter.”

Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship to Gene Tunney in 1926. Wills never fought for the world title.

The missing fight should count when Dempsey’s championship reign is evaluated. Wills was precisely the type of challenger a champion needed to defeat to remove questions about his dominance.

Placing the entire responsibility on Dempsey, however, ignores the racial barriers, regulators, promoters and failed financing that repeatedly interfered with the fight.

More than a century later, nobody knows what would have happened if Jack Dempsey and Harry Wills had finally met. That unanswered question is why Wills remains an unavoidable part of Dempsey’s legacy.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Dismisses Shakur Stevenson’s Vacant-Belt Championships
Sports.content:
“This fight is about Teofimo Lopez trying to get the world title again, become a real three-division world champion. No vacant belts,” Lopez Sr. said to Fighthype. “Shakur got like two vacant belts, right? So, to me, he’s not a real three-division world champion. My son is going to do it the right way. We’re going to go straight to the champion. No vacant belt.”

Stevenson has actually won world titles across four divisions. His first came against Joet Gonzalez for the vacant WBO featherweight belt in 2019. He then stopped reigning WBO junior lightweight champion Jamel Herring in 2021 before defeating Edwin De Los Santos for the vacant WBC lightweight title in November 2023.

The fourth belt is difficult for Lopez Sr. to dismiss under his own standard. Shakur took the WBO light welterweight title from Teofimo in January, giving him two divisional championships won by defeating reigning titleholders.

Lopez Sr. also criticized Shakur’s fighting style and questioned how much further Stevenson can climb through the weight classes.

“I would love to fight him again. Let’s hope that we can get him before we move up too high,” Lopez Sr. said. “I don’t think Shakur can go up in the weight divisions. He’s too chinny. He doesn’t like to get hit. He’s a boring fighter.”

He believes Teofimo fought the wrong fight against Shakur. In his view, Teofimo should have boxed from the back foot instead of following the southpaw to his right all night.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Answers Devin Haney’s IBF Call
Sports.content:
“Have the WBO.. I want the IBF,” Devin said on X.

Haney seems to have signaled his preferred opponent without directly naming him. The choice makes sense. Paro brings a large following in Australia and the potential for a PPV event built around two welterweight champions.

That separates Paro from Jack Catterall, another opponent who has been discussed for Haney. Catterall presents a difficult fight with his movement, defense, timing and awkward southpaw style.

Paro is a southpaw as well, but he’s much more willing to engage and turn fights into physical exchanges. Haney has generally performed well against aggressive fighters who come forward, giving him opportunities to box from range, counter, and tie up when they get inside.

Catterall offers a different challenge. He’s unlikely to chase Haney recklessly or provide the type of pressure that allows Haney to settle into his preferred rhythm. Taking that fight would mean accepting considerable stylistic difficulty without getting another world title in return.

Paro gives Haney the opportunity to unify the division while bringing an established Australian audience to the promotion. From Haney’s perspective, that combination makes the matchup easier to understand commercially.

Nothing has been finalized, but the exchange leaves little mystery about their interest. Both champions have publicly opened the door to putting the IBF and WBO titles together.

Ghana News.title: Abeiku Santana launches Tourism Destination Africa podcast to promote African tourism
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey Santana, has launched a new podcast aimed at amplifying African voices and reshaping global perceptions of the continent’s tourism industry.

The podcast, titled Tourism Destination Africa, is designed as an informative, educational and entertaining platform focusing on tourism, travel and hospitality in Ghana and across the continent.

Mr Santana, who was recently named among the 2026 Top 100 Most Influential People in Tourism and Hospitality in Africa, said the initiative would provide a platform to explore Africa’s tourism opportunities, cultures and experiences.

According to figures released by UN Tourism, Africa welcomed nearly 81 million international visitors in 2025, up from 75.4 million in 2024.

The growth made Africa the fastest-growing tourism region globally during the period, ahead of Europe, Asia and the Americas.

Despite the growth, Mr Santana said global perceptions of Africa as a tourism destination had not kept pace with the continent’s performance.

He cited Ghana’s Year of Return and Beyond the Return initiatives as examples of the country’s ability to attract members of the African diaspora, but stressed the need for sustained storytelling to maintain that momentum.

“For as long as many of us can remember, the story of Africa has been told by everyone except Africans,” he said.

Mr Santana said Africa’s story had often been framed around colonialism, conflict and hardship, with comparatively less attention given to its achievements, innovation, cultural diversity and tourism potential.

He explained that each episode of Tourism Destination Africa would explore a destination, culture, experience or idea deserving of wider recognition.

“While some episodes will spotlight lesser-known attractions and communities in Ghana, others will examine tourism developments across the continent and lessons African countries can learn from one another,” he said.

The podcast is expected to target tourism professionals, travellers, hospitality stakeholders and audiences interested in how Africa is perceived and represented globally.

Mr Santana said the platform would contribute to changing the narrative by giving Africans greater control over how their destinations, cultures and experiences are presented to the world.

He encouraged the public to follow the podcast and participate in conversations about the future of tourism on the continent.

The initiative comes as African destinations seek to build on recent growth in international arrivals by strengthening destination marketing, cultural storytelling and tourism experiences.

Ghana News.title: Sedina case: There’s nothing to appeal – Amaliba on AG’s decision to withdraw stay application
Ghana News.content:
Former Director of Legal Affairs of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Abraham Amaliba, has suggested that the Attorney-General may have withdrawn the application seeking to keep former MASLOC Chief Executive Sedina Tamakloe-Attionu in custody after concluding that there was little basis to pursue the matter.

According to him, the Attorney-General may have reviewed the Court of Appeal’s judgment and determined that an appeal to the Supreme Court was unlikely to succeed.

Mr Amaliba was commenting on the decision by the Attorney-General to withdraw the stay of execution application following the Court of Appeal’s acquittal and discharge of Ms Tamakloe-Attionu.

The Court of Appeal on July 30, 2026, unanimously overturned her conviction and 10-year prison sentence, holding that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

Speaking on Joy FM's Top Story on August 12, Mr Amaliba said the withdrawal could be explained by the Attorney-General’s approach to prosecutions, which he said is based on the availability and strength of evidence.

“I can only hazard a guess,” he said when asked why the Attorney-General withdrew the stay of application processes filed.

“Don’t forget that the appeal was filed at the time when the judgment was not before the Attorney-General. You remember he said that in his press conference. He said that this morning, that was when he was speaking, that he has a soft copy; he has not read it yet, but he has ordered the DPP.

“I’m sure after reading it, he comes to the firm conclusion that there’s nothing to appeal, and that when you appeal, you will lose.”

Mr Amaliba noted that the Attorney-General has previously maintained that prosecutions should only be pursued where there is sufficient evidence to support them.

He said it was therefore possible that a review of the appellate court’s judgment influenced the decision to withdraw the stay application.

The Attorney-General had initially directed the Director of Public Prosecutions to file a notice of appeal at the Supreme Court and an application for a stay of execution of the Court of Appeal’s judgment.

The State had argued that the Court of Appeal’s decision contained errors of law and fact and that there were substantial grounds for the Supreme Court to overturn it. It also expressed concern that Ms Tamakloe-Attionu could leave the jurisdiction before the Supreme Court determined the appeal.

However, following the withdrawal of the stay application, a judge signed the release warrant for Ms Tamakloe-Attionu, paving the way for her release from custody.

Mr Amaliba also rejected suggestions from the opposition NPP that the development vindicated its earlier claims that the government intended to shield Ms Tamakloe-Attionu.

He argued that such claims ignored the independence of the judiciary and the effect of the Court of Appeal’s ruling.

Ghana News.title: Major Russian grain export terminal hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
Ghana News.content:
A "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia's port city of Novorossiysk has damaged grain export terminals and hit the last major Russian naval base on the Black Sea.

Three people, including an eight-year-old child, were killed and 24 people were injured in the Wednesday nighttime attack.

Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Ukraine had launched rocket and underwater drones in a "unique operation" to strike the Russian naval base at Novorossiysk, although he did not mention grain terminals being hit.

"The occupying fleet and all the infrastructure that supports it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues," Zelensky said.

Most of Russia's Black Sea fleet is docked in Novorossiysk - one of the largest ports in Russia - after it was forced to vacate its former home base of Sevastopol, in the Russia-occupied Crimean peninsula, which was too exposed to Ukrainian attacks.

A major grain trading company confirmed to Russia's TASS news agency that its terminal had been hit, while another told Reuters and Russian outlet RBK the same.

The Russian agriculture ministry announced on Wednesday that it was working to redirect cargo flows to ports in the Baltic and Caspian Seas as well as land routes. It did not make any reference to Ukraine's attacks but said it was "taking into account current logistical constraints".

Repeated explosions reportedly rang out over Novorossiysk throughout the night as air defences shot down aerial objects.

An emergency situation was declared in the city on Wednesday, after the barrage of drones struck areas around the port and damaged pipelines, suspending water supply for the city.

Elsewhere in the region a man was killed by drone debris, Regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said. Several locations in the surrounding Krasnodar region were also struck by "several hundred drones" overnight, Kondratyev added, with dozens of buildings damaged, including homes.

For its part, Moscow launched aerial strikes which killed at least 11 civilians overnight between Tuesday and Wednesday. The majority were killed when Russia hit the city of Zaporizhzhia with ballistic missiles and glide bombs.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

After a period of relative calm in the Black Sea, over the course of this summer Kyiv and Moscow resumed striking one another's ports and shipping.

The last remaining sea route out of Ukraine has been badly affected by several deadly Russian strikes on cargo ships and the port of Odesa, through which Moscow seeks to put off foreign companies from trading with Ukraine. In July, the Ukrainian Agribusiness Club (UCAB) reported a 23% decrease in exports.

Meanwhile, Ukraine has grown increasingly adept at carrying out long-range strikes on Russian territory. Its recent attacks on vessels in the eastern Black Sea have disrupted Russia's grain shipments, too.

Russia is the world's largest wheat exporter - but according to a Moscow-based analytics company, exports for August could fall by more than half compared to the same month over the last five years due to the disruption in the Black and Azov seas.

On Wednesday, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of carrying out strikes on Russian grain and agricultural infrastructure, resulting in a hike in global food prices and growing grain shortages.

But Zakharova also said that for its part Russia would continue striking "facilities that [Ukraine's armed forces] use on the Black Sea to destabilise the navigation situation" until "the full elimination of threats to security projected to the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea".

Concerns over how the war in Ukraine would affect global food supplies have been persistent since Moscow invaded in 2022.

Together, Russia and Ukraine account for a significant share of global grain trade, particularly for buyers in North Africa, the Middle East and parts of Asia.

The 2022 Black Sea Grain Initiative, under which Russia agreed to lift its blockade on Ukraine's agricultural exports, did not last after Moscow resumed attacks on vessels using the maritime corridors to Odesa the following year.

Ghana News.title: LA Lakers to be sold in record $12.5bn deal
Ghana News.content:
The Los Angeles Lakers are to be sold for a reported record-breaking $12.5bn, external (£9.3bn) - less than a year after Mark Walter took a majority stake in the NBA franchise.

Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger are buying the controlling interest in one of the world's most iconic sports teams.

Walter bought his share, reportedly worth an estimated $10bn (£7.45bn) - a previous record - from the Buss family in a deal that was unanimously approved by the NBA Board of Governors in October 2025.

Kushner and Iger said in a statement: "As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honoured for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world.

"We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss.

"Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles."

Jerry Buss bought the Lakers in a $67.5m deal (£50m) in 1979 that included the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and a Los Angeles arena, known as the Kia Forum.

After he died in 2013, ownership was passed to his six children in a Trust before a deal was completed with Walter, who also owns a stake in the LA Dodgers with Todd Boehly.

"Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honors of my life," said Walter.

"It has been an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family.

"I am grateful to Jeanie Buss, the Buss family, the players, and the staff for welcoming me into this chapter. The Lakers belong to Los Angeles, and I have every confidence the best is still ahead."

The LA Lakers have 17 NBA titles - one less than the record of 18 held by the Boston Celtics.

The deal involving Kushner comes after he was part of the recent controversy surrounding Fifa president Gianni Infantino and an aborted plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors.

Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Kushner, was expected to lead the proposed investor group for the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

Ghana News.title: Sixteen inmates injured after lightning strikes US prison
Ghana News.content:
Lightning struck an Ohio prison during severe weather in the state on Tuesday, injuring 16 inmates, one of which had to be airlifted to hospital.

The prisoners were outside during the storm, moving between buildings after an evening meal.

Nine of the inmates have since returned to the correctional institution, while seven remain in hospital, including one in serious condition, the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction said.

Severe weather and flash flooding has ravaged parts of the US Midwest in recent days, generating tornadoes, strong winds and causing widespread power outages.

No staff were injured in the strike, the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction said in a Wednesday morning update on social media.

The nature of injuries to the inmate who was airlifted from the scene has not been disclosed. BBC News has contacted the institution for comment.

The lightning strike hit amid severe weather conditions across the Midwest region. The National Weather Service (NWS) has issued flash flooding warnings across Ohio and Indiana, and confirmed that three tornadoes touched down in Chicago's south suburbs on Tuesday.

Footage from across the region shows homes with damaged roofs and trees that have been downed as a result of the storms.

At least three deaths have been confirmed, including that of a four-year-old boy whose family's mobile home in Indiana was struck by a tree.

An Indiana woman was killed in a home explosion during a period of powerful winds of more than 100 miles (160km) per hour, according to CBS news, the BBC's US partner.

First response efforts were delayed as a result of the road conditions, said police captain Rob Maynard. He said that although they believe the storm played a role in the woman's death, they are unable to draw final conclusions right now.

There were also several gas leaks as a result of the storm, which can be caused when large trees fall and disrupt underground infrastructure, Maynard added.

In Ohio, another individual died when first responders were unable to quickly reach them during a flooding emergency, said Ohio Governor Mike DeWine.

"This is a very dangerous weather situation," DeWine said on Tuesday, while warning people to keep an eye on the news and use "common sense".

The storms have caused extensive power outages across the region.

More than 295,000 customers are without power in Indiana, as well as more than 185,000 in Ohio and 145,000 in Illinois, according to a power tracker webpage on Wednesday.

"Now is the time to plan for severe weather and flooding!" the NWS said, while warning of severe wind gusts strong enough to knock down trees, branches and power lines.

The Federal Aviation Administration issued ground stops at major airports in the area due to thunderstorms, including Chicago's O'Hare and Midway airports, which continue into Wednesday afternoon.

Ghana News.title: Bawumia, Dumelo, Afenyo-Markin, Bola Ray, others to headline Empower Vault Summit on October 14
Ghana News.content:
The annual Empower Vault Summit is set to take place on Friday, August 14, at the Great Hall of the University of Ghana.

This is a high-impact leadership and mentorship platform aimed at equipping young people with the skills, values, and mindset needed to succeed.

The summit is being organised by Stables and Horses in partnership with the Office of the University of Ghana SRC Vice President.

The initiative is designed to provide young people across Ghana with clarity of purpose, strong personal values and practical tools for leadership, entrepreneurship and personal development.

Former Vice President, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, is expected to attend as Guest of Honour, while a distinguished line-up of public officials, business leaders and industry personalities will engage participants throughout the event.

Among the speakers are Osman Abdulai Ayariga, Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority; John Dumelo; Alexander Afenyo-Markin, Minority Leader and MP for Effutu; and George Opare Addo, Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment.

Other speakers include Dr. Dora Oforiwaa Hall, CEO of Zoe Dental; Bayo Adedeji; Bola Ray, CEO of EIB Network; Ewura Karim Adams; and Prof. Rosina Kyerematen, Dean of Student Affairs at the University of Ghana.

The summit will also feature breakout sessions designed to give participants more intimate and practical engagement with influential voices and young personalities. These sessions will feature Endurance Grand, Nyamewaa, Willie Chembez and Asiedu Mends.

A major attraction of the summit will be an entrepreneurship challenge, giving students the opportunity to pitch their businesses, present innovative ideas and compete for a GH¢10,000 cash prize.

The challenge is expected to provide a platform for emerging entrepreneurs to gain visibility, receive feedback and demonstrate how their ideas can address real-world challenges.

Some scholarship opportunities are also in the offing for some brilliant but needy students as part of the event.

Senior Project Manager and Brand Strategist for the Empower Vault Summit, Joey Joseph Nii Ayi Otokunor, is leading the project management and strategic direction of the initiative.

“We believe young people do not lack potential; what they often need is the right platform, guidance and opportunity to unlock it. Empower Vault is designed to provide exactly that—connecting young people with leaders, mentors and opportunities that can shape their next chapter,” he said.

The Empower Vault Summit is expected to bring together students, young entrepreneurs, aspiring leaders, creatives and other young people seeking guidance and opportunities to accelerate their personal and professional development.

The organisers say the summit forms part of a broader effort to empower young people to take ownership of their futures, develop strong leadership values and translate their ideas into tangible opportunities.

Ghana News.title: Sekyedumase Community Bank sues Asokore Mampong Assembly over demolition for 24-hour economy market
Ghana News.content:
A legal dispute is brewing between the Sekyedumase Community Bank and the Asokore Mampong Municipal Assembly in the Ashanti Region following an alleged unlawful demolition of the bank’s building for the construction of a 24-hour economy market.

The bank’s management claims the Assembly acted unlawfully by demolishing the facility while applications concerning the property were still pending before the courts in Kumasi.

The bank, which has operated in the Aboabo community for decades, is now conducting its operations from a makeshift stall after its building was pulled down along with other shops and homes in the area.

The demolition was carried out on Monday by a security taskforce from the Asokore Mampong Assembly as part of preparations for the municipality’s 24-hour economy market project.

Management of the bank says it had engaged the Assembly for several months over the proposed redevelopment of the area and possible relocation or integration of the bank into the project.

However, the bank says its concerns were not addressed, forcing it to seek legal redress over the land it claims ownership of.

Counsel for the Sekyedumase Community Bank, Dr Dickson Osei Assibey, said the bank had occupied the land for more than three decades and had constructed the building with its own resources.

He said the bank was prepared to engage the Assembly but believed its proposal to integrate the existing facility into the 24-hour economy project was not given fair consideration.

“The bank has been there over 33 years. And from the documents that are on the land, it shows that the community gave the land to the bank to develop it as a bank to serve them. So the bank put up the building by themselves. It's not the community. It's not the municipal assembly. It is for the bank. And then the bank has been there for the past 33 years.”

Dr Assibey said the bank had been willing to explore an amicable solution, including having its facility incorporated into the new market development.

“So even if you want them to move, it's a matter of talking with each other, which they started. But the position of the bank was that either you integrate our building into the 24-hour economy project, which to me it is possible. They have not been fair. They have trespassed, and we think that the court have to take that matter up.”

Chief Executive Officer of the bank, Afriyie Michael Kwabena, said the demolition had resulted in the destruction of physical assets worth millions of Ghanaian cedis.

He said while the bank’s customer database had been preserved through its digital systems, equipment and other physical assets inside the building were lost.

“We have inventory of all the assets that is in the building. And the customer database is intact because due to technology and the existence of the bank for the past 46 years, we have managed to have the data of the customers intact. So for customer data, it's not lost. But the physical items of the bank are lost, running into millions of Ghanaian cedis.”

Mr Afriyie also disputed claims that the bank had been formally evicted before the demolition.

“We are not served any eviction notice. In fact, we have for the past five months been cooperating with the Assembly. We have not been served any eviction notice.”

The Asokore Mampong Municipal Assembly is yet to comment on the allegations by the bank.

In the meantime, management says it is working with ARB Apex Bank and the Bank of Ghana to secure an alternative location from which the bank can continue its operations.

The legal dispute is expected to continue in court, with the two applications filed by the opposing sides expected to be heard in October.

Ghana News.title: “I’m partially single” – Tima Kumkum finally breaks silence on divorce rumours
Ghana News.content:
Media personality Cynthia Tima Yeboah, popularly known as Tima Kumkum, has confirmed that she is separated from her husband, Dominic Duodu, and that their divorce is currently before the court.

Speaking to Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime’s Changes show, Tima Kumkum said the couple have not lived together since 1 April 2025 and that she considers herself ‘partially single’ because she is not yet divorced.

“I said I was not going to talk about it. People have been forcing me to say it. I’m separated. Not yet divorced but will be divorced soon. I didn’t want to talk about it but let’s call a spade a spade; we don’t live together since 1st April, 2025. So, I’m partially single because I’m not fully divorced yet but it’s in court so we don’t really want to talk about it,” she revealed.

The media personality had previously been at the centre of speculation after she was seen without her wedding ring for several months, prompting some social media users to suggest that she had divorced her husband.

Tima later addressed the rumours in a post on her social media platforms, debunking the claims and explaining why she had stopped wearing her wedding ring.

During the interview, the question about the whereabouts of her ‘supposed’ current husband came up after Tima revealed that she had been solely responsible for taking care of her children without support from any man.

She added that people in the area where she lives are aware of the situation, so it is not news to them. However, she is not willing to disclose the reason for the breakup, even after the divorce process is successfully completed in court.

Tima Kumkum said she never thought such an incident would happen again, especially since it was her second marriage. However, the couple lived together for one year and nine months before eventually separating.

She also commended her ex-husband, Dominic Duodu, for being a responsible father and taking care of their child since their separation.

“He’s a very responsible man. I’ll give him his flowers for that. He takes care of his child and pays his school fees. That’s fine and I’m okay with that. So, custody is okay,” Tima further said.

For now, she said she has no plans to marry again, adding that marriage is currently the last thing on her mind.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: White House construction project to cost almost $1bn
World.content:
The Trump administration has responded to controversy over construction and expansion projects at the White House by saying the work was “long-overdue and necessary” and “inextricably tied to the security of the President, the White House grounds and the certain security infrastructure assets”.

US President Donald Trump’s administration has long insisted construction is being funded by private donors and is necessary for security reasons. But on Wednesday, The Washington Post cited documents it obtained that showed the administration was planning to spend nearly $1bn on the construction work, which includes a large new ballroom to replace much of the White House’s East Wing.

White House spokesman Davis Ingle, in a statement to Al Jazeera, cited recent security incidents, including attempted attacks on the president and events around the 250th anniversary of US independence, as reasons for the work.

Ingle said the work was being done in coordination with the Secret Service and White House Military Office. He also said approximately $400m in funding for the new ballroom was coming from “President Trump and generous American patriots”.

About $875m has been put into the White House Repair and Restoration account, which typically has only several million dollars and is used for routine maintenance and upkeep. Some $500m of that money came from the Secret Service and the White House Military Office, tasked with securing the president and his family, as well as top US officials. Another $305m, according to The Post, came from private donations, while the provenance of another $70m was not indicated.



The White House reconstruction project has faced scrutiny from lawmakers, as well as courts, over concerns that vested interests, including private businesses seeking government contracts, are paying for the work in exchange for government favours. A federal judge in Washington, DC, last week ordered a halt to work specifically for the ballroom, saying it needed Congressional approval under existing law. In June, the advocacy group Public Citizen said it found corporate donors to the project had received more than $50bn in government contracts during the previous six months.

Record-low water levels on the Danube near Prahovo, Serbia, have exposed the wrecks of dozens of Nazi-era vessels sunk by German forces during their 1944 retreat from advancing Soviet troops. The discovery comes as Europe endures an intense heatwave and historic drought.

World.title: Trump remarks on diminishing impact of pro-Israel groups in Congress
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump took a jab at the dwindling power of pro-Israel lobbying groups in Congress and across Washington’s political spectrum in a pre-taped exclusive recording with the hyper-partisan show America Speaks on the MAGA-friendly network “Real America’s Voice” (RAV).

When asked by host Wayne Allyn Root in the interview that aired on Tuesday about the “problem,” of the “communist colour revolution”, taking over “the biggest cities in America”, Trump replied that the biggest change he had observed over the last decade is “what’s happened to Israel and Jewish people”, adding that if, “you go back 20, 25 years ago, they had the most powerful lobby in Washington. Now, everyone is … if you look at the House … you look at the Democrats in the House … it’s pretty amazing actually. I’ve never seen anything like it.”

The comments come after a recent survey by The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs revealed a dramatic erosion of support for the US ally, with burgeoning opposition from Democrats and signs of polarisation among the Republican base.

This was not the first time the president had conceded Israel’s declining support in US politics. In September 2025, an interview with White House correspondent Reagan Reese of the Daily Caller, a right-wing website founded by former Fox News personality Tucker Carlson, saw Trump acknowledging that he was aware of slumping support for Israel among young Republicans, later explaining to the Caller that Israel’s ironclad endorsement in Congress is now a thing of the past.



In the 42-minute audio clip with RAV, Trump went on to slight Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, the highest-ranking Jewish official in US history and a reliably pro-Israel voice, “Look at Schumer. He’s become virtually a Palestinian,” he told the Caller.

Trump made similar comments in 2025, as well. During a March 2025 Oval Office meeting, Trump told reporters that “Schumer is a Palestinian, as far as I’m concerned,” and reiterated the comment at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in July. He berated the Democrat whom he claims was once “one hundred percent for Israel”.

At the time, Trump’s derogatory proclamations met with widespread disapproval and drew condemnation from Jewish and Muslim groups over what many saw as a xenophobic slur, regarding the president’s attempts to frame “Palestinian” as a political insult directed at Schumer.

In March 2024, the Senate minority leader had called for a leadership shake-up in Israel, after describing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as “too willing to tolerate the civilian toll in Gaza”.

That was the Jewish-American Democrat’s most vociferous critique of Israel since its genocidal war in Gaza first began in October 2023, having also expressed support for a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The veteran senator is usually a staunch defender of Israel.

More recently, Schumer reprimanded the president over his handling of the US-Israel war on Iran, noting that his “rinse and repeat approach … isn’t a strategy”, but a “recipe for utter disaster”, adding, “we keep moving backward … it’s incredible what a fiasco this war is.”
