SRINAGAR: Sarvanand Kaul Premi was a poet. Sarla Bhat was a nurse. Both were Kashmiri Pandits who stayed behind when militancy erupted and were killed in 1990. More than three decades later, J&K policeâs SIA revived unresolved cases from the Valleyâs darkest years. The agency searched Wednesday nine locations in its probe into the abduction-murder of Premi and his younger son, weeks after filing a chargesheet in Bhatâs killing.Premi, 66, a poet, teacher and Gandhian, and Verinder were abducted from their village, Soaf Shali near Kokernag, on Apr 30, 1990. They were shot dead the next day. Five days later, the grief-stricken Kaul family left Kashmir, never to return.State Investigation Agencyâs searches were linked to FIR No. 45/1990 registered at Dooru police station in Anantnag. SIA is pursuing militancy-era cases that had lain cold for decades.On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat, 27, a staff nurse in the neonatology ward at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences in Srinagar. She was allegedly abducted by JKLF from SKIMS Habba Khatoon Hostel on Apr 18, 1990, and taken to Illahibagh-Lal Bazar, tortured and shot dead.Her bullet-riddled body was found the next day at Omer Colony Malabagh in downtown Srinagar.Born in Soaf Shali in 1924, Premi joined Khadi Bhandar after completing his education and became associated with Mahatma Gandhiâs Swadeshi movement. His association with Kashmiri poet Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor inspired his literary career. He translated Rabindranath Tagoreâs âGitanjaliâ into Kashmiri and the Bhagavad Gita and Ramayana into Kashmiri and Urdu, and advocated secularism and interfaith harmony.J&K govt under then-CM Farooq Abdullah posthumously awarded Premi a gold medal in 1997 for his contribution to Kashmiri literature and communal harmony.The killings from Kashmirâs violent spring of 1990 were part of a wider wave of hostility against Kashmiri Pandits after militancy erupted, driving a mass exodus of the community from the Valley. In 2010, J&K govt under then-CM Omar Abdullah told the assembly that 209 Kashmiri Pandits had been murdered since 1990.

World.title: Assam floods: Toll rises to 103; 87,000 remain affected in four districts
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The flood situation in

showed signs of improvement on Wednesday, with the number of people affected falling to around 87,000 across four districts. However, the death toll from this year's floods rose to 103 after two more people died in the past 24 hours.

The latest figures from the Assam State Disaster Management Authority showed that one person drowned in Sivasagar and another in Karbi Anglong.

Around 86,800 people are still affected by the floods in Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Sivasagar. Golaghat remains the worst-hit district, with more than 42,000 people affected. Nagaon has around 20,000 affected residents, while Sivasagar has about 15,000.

The situation has nevertheless improved compared with Tuesday, when nearly 1.13 lakh people were affected across the four districts.

Authorities are continuing relief operations in the affected areas. A total of 79 relief camps and distribution centres are currently operating across five districts, providing assistance to 13,011 people.

Over the past 24 hours, relief agencies distributed nearly 96.55 quintals of rice, 18.26 quintals of dal, 5.41 quintals of salt and more than 204 litres of mustard oil among flood-affected families.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Despite the improvement, the floods continue to damage homes, farmland and infrastructure.





According to ASDMA, 433 villages remain underwater, while more than 10,884 hectares of crop land have been damaged across the state.

Floodwaters have also damaged embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure in several districts.

The Dhansiri River at Numaligarh continues to flow above the danger mark, adding to concerns in the affected areas.

The floods have also affected livestock. More than 32,900 domestic animals and poultry have been impacted across Assam.

While the overall number of people affected has declined, the rising death toll and continuing damage to villages, farmland and infrastructure show that the flood crisis is far from over.

World.title: China says India border 'generally stable' amid tensions in Arunachal
World.content:
China said the India-China border remains âgenerally stableâ while sidestepping reports of increased Chinese military activity near Arunachal Pradesh.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

China said Wednesday that the situation along the India-China border was âgenerally stable at the momentâ, while declining to confirm reports of increased Chinese military activity in disputed areas near Arunachal Pradesh.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing in Beijing in response to questions about videos circulating on Indian social media that purportedly showed heightened Chinese military activity along the border.Guo said China and India had held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on Border Affairs the previous week. He said both sides had agreed to maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels and work together to preserve peace and tranquillity along the border.The comments came a day after India reiterated that its border with China remained a matter of serious concern and that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control was essential to the broader relationship between the two countries.The Chinese response also came amid reports of heightened military activity by Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradeshâs Upper Subansiri region. Beijing claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of what it calls âSouth Tibetâ, a claim consistently rejected by New Delhi.India had separately pushed back against Chinaâs objections to New Delhi formally identifying 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard Indian names. The Ministry of External Affairs said the state was an âinalienable and integralâ part of India and that nothing could change that reality.The latest exchanges come as India and China continue efforts to stabilise ties that deteriorated sharply after the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes and a prolonged military standoff along the border.The two countries reached a disengagement agreement covering the remaining friction points at Depsang and Demchok in October 2024.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping subsequently held talks in Kazan, followed by further diplomatic efforts aimed at improving bilateral relations.

World.title: ‘Delete posts, apologise’: Bengal CM Adhikari orders action over derogatory posts about Netaji
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday ordered action against social media posts making unsavoury comment against

.

While talking to reporters, Suvendu said, "Those making derogatory remarks against Netaji on social media should immediately delete posts and issue apology,"

"I have asked police to arrest those making unsavoury comments on Netaji.

Law will be equal for MLAs, MPs, and government officials," he added.

Adhikari also directed all MLAs to set up public service centres in their respective constituencies and name them after Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

The chief minister's direction to the police came days after BJP MP Nagendranath Roy, popularly known as Ananta Maharaj, described Netaji as a âwar criminalâ and questioned his leadership and the role of the Azad Hind Fauj in Indiaâs freedom struggle.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Adhikari further said the state will assist Rs 30,000 per month to run the centres, subject to certain conditions.

The centres will have to bear Netaji's name and display a portrait of Bose in traditional dhoti and kurta, which will be supplied by the state Information and Cultural Affairs Department, the chief minister said.

"Earlier, MLAs in our state used to work from government offices. Now almost every MLA has their own office. Every constituency must have a service centre run by the MLA. Through these centres, they will provide services to the people of their areas. Everyone will receive services, whether they voted for them or not. These service centres will be called Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Seva Kendra," Adhikari said.

World.title: Delhi Police’s ‘Kuchu Puchu’ Gen-Z twist to warn Delhiites about Chinese manjha
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has found a rather unusual way to join the viral âkuchu-puchuâ Gen Z trend, using internet humour to deliver a serious warning about kite-flying strings.

In a recent social media post, the police urged residents to enjoy kite flying but stay away from banned Chinese manjha and plastic-coated strings, which can cause serious injuries to people and animals.

âDear Kuchu Puchu, Patang Udao but Say NO to Chinese Manjha, Samjhe?â the police wrote, giving its usual safety messaging a more playful, social media-friendly tone.

The message comes as authorities step up action against the banned string in Delhi. The Crime Branch recently seized more than 1,300 rolls of Chinese manjha during an enforcement operation. In a separate action, Central Delhi Police recovered around 120 rolls.

The post quickly drew reactions online, with some users poking fun at the police for adopting the language of Gen Z.

âGen-Z mode of Delhi Policeâ, âThey are updatingâ, some comments read. Behind the light-hearted presentation, however, is a serious safety concern.

Chinese manjha is generally made using synthetic or plastic material and can be coated with abrasive substances. Because of its sharpness, it can cause deep cuts and injuries.





It can also become particularly dangerous for birds, which can get caught in the string while flying. There have already been fatal consequences in Delhi.

Recently, a 32-year-old man travelling to Mundka for business suffered a cut to his neck after coming into contact with Chinese manjha in southwest Delhi's Uttam Nagar.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In another tragic incident in 2023, a seven-year-old girl died after being injured by Chinese manjha while travelling with her father on a scooter in west Delhi's Paschim Vihar.

The police's latest post therefore carries a straightforward message beneath all the social media humour. People can continue flying kites and enjoying the activity, but using banned synthetic strings can put lives at risk.

The campaign also reflects a broader change in the way police departments communicate with the public, with serious safety warnings increasingly being delivered through the language, trends and humour that dominate social media.

World.title: Cybersecurity at nuclear installations accorded highest priority; AERB, external govt agencies assess security at plants: Centre
World.content:
Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Chennai: The Union govt on Wednesday informed Lok Sabha that security assessments are conducted periodically at all nuclear power plant sites by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) and âexternal govt agencies. âIn a written reply to Congress MP Manickam Tagore, minister of state in the Prime Ministerâs Office Jitendra Singh said the plants also conduct internal security assessments. âThe observations made are reviewed, monitored and necessary upgrades are carried out for compliance,â he said.Tagore had sought details of third-party security audits at nuclear plants, including Kudankulam, and measures to counter threats from drones, cyberattacks and sabotage. He asked whether any foreign or suspected state-sponsored cyberattack attempts had been detected during the past three years.The National Alliance of Anti-nuclear Movements urged the Union govt recently to constitute a commission of inquiry to investigate the alleged leak of files related to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant. The statement comes in the wake of a ransomware group reportedly publishing hundreds of files linked to the Kudankulam plant which are said to be highly sensitive.The govt did not directly disclose whether any such foreign or state-sponsored attempts had been detected. It said cybersecurity at nuclear installations was accorded the âhighest priorityâ, with continuous monitoring and surveillance mechanisms in place. Preventive measures include access controls, regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, incident-response mechanisms and capacity-building programmes. It cited CERT-inâs (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) role in issuing alerts and advisories, coordinating responses to cyber incidents and operating the National Cyber Coordination Centre.On physical security, Singh said nuclear power plants were equipped with perimeter intrusion-detection systems, access controls, CCTV surveillance and X-ray baggage inspection facilities. The AERB conducts regulatory inspections covering nuclear security.Singh said regulatory-approved emergency preparedness plans were in place at every nuclear power plant, including Kudankulam. Exercises involving local administration, security agencies and plant authorities are conducted periodically, and feedback is used to revise and strengthen preparedness plans.Tabletop, Integrated Command, Control and Response (ICCR) exercises are held once every two years. Mock exercises are organised according to the National Disaster Management Authorityâs schedule. An ICCR exercise was conducted at the Kudankulam nuclear power plant on April 15, 2025.The govt said all other nuclear power plant sites had conducted their latest ICCR exercises since Sept 2024. At Kalpakkam, an off-site emergency exercise involving the district administration, was conducted on July 17, 2026, with an initiating event from the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor.

World.title: 'Got firebombed by Indians on net': Trump aide Navarro recalls backlash after Russian oil, tariff remarks
World.content:
PM Modi and Trump to work on tariff deal

NEW DELHI: US senior counsellor for trade and manufacturing Peter Navarro has said President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have a âvery good working relationshipâ and will resolve differences over the US tariff issue linked to Indiaâs imports of Russian oil.Responding to an ANI question, Navarro recalled the backlash he faced in India after writing an op-ed on the India-Russia oil trade.âDuring the Ukraine-Russia war, 6-8 months ago, I think I wrote an op-ed, which absolutely factually correctly pointed out that prior to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, India was not involved in the oil trade with Russia, but afterwards it got heavily involved and was selling a lot of refined products on behalf of Russia, which helped feed the war machine,â Navarro said.âAnd that issue has been resolved. Maybe I had a little bit to do with that with that op-ed, but I can tell you, I got actually firebombed by the Indian continent on the internet. All I would say to you, don't do that,â he added.Navarro, however, said the issue would ultimately be handled by Trump and Modi themselves.âThat's not how we resolve problems here in America. With respect to your question, the President and your Prime Minister have a very good working relationship.They are going to work that out amongst themselves, and it's not for me or any gaggle to get between that,â he said.His remarks come amid renewed concerns in India over possible US trade measures targeting countries that continue to purchase Russian energy.Earlier on August 7, the US Senate passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by an 86-11 vote. The bipartisan legislation would give the US president discretionary authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from countries that are among the top five buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas.India and China remain among the largest buyers of Russian crude.

World.title: ED arrests ex-treasurer of Cong's Chhattisgarh unit in Rs 3,000 cr liquor scam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate has arrested Ramgopal Agarwal, former treasurer of the Congress in Chhattisgarh, in an ongoing money laundering investigation in the Rs 3,000 crore liquor scam in the state.

The agency said a substantial part of the proceeds of crime, generated in cash, was delivered to Agrawal in his capacity as the then Treasurer of the Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committee.

Agrawal, who was lodged as an undertrial in the Central Jail, Raipur, was arrested on Tuesday and has been remanded to ED custody for seven days. He is accused of criminal conspiracy, cheating, forgery and corruption in the excise administration of Chhattisgarh during 2019 to 2023.

âInvestigation revealed that a syndicate comprising Anil Tuteja (retd IAS), Anwar Dhebar and Arun Pati Tripathi (an Indian Telecom Service officer) orchestrated a large-scale scam in the stateâs liquor trade and generated proceeds of crime of Rs 3,000 crore through illegal commission on liquor sales, unaccounted country liquor sale, commission collected from distillers and from foreign liquor companies and against the grant of FL-10A licences,â ED said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





The agency further said that âstatements recorded of the persons who handled and moved the cash have revealed that the cash was delivered, at the instance of Ramgopal Agrawal and through handlers of the syndicate, at Rajiv Bhawan, Raipur, the then office of the Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committeeâ.

Agarwal was summoned for questioning earlier, and in his statement subsequently recorded, he gave evasive replies, the agency said.

World.title: Messi event row: govt. may order probe
World.content:
The State government is likely to order a probe into the alleged irregularities and procedural lapses in the previous LDF government’s efforts to bring football legend Lionel Messi and the Argentina team to the State.

Indicating the possibility of an investigation, Sports Minister O.J. Janeesh on Wednesday rejected former minister V. Abdurahiman’s defence of the proposal and alleged that government machinery was misused to facilitate financial gains for a private individual.

Mr. Janeesh said there was no substance in Mr. Abdurahiman’s claim that the government had not suffered any financial loss in connection with the proposed event. He alleged that official procedures were not followed from the beginning and that there was a lack of transparency in selecting the sponsor and dealing with the proposal.

The government machinery was misused for a private event management company. From the Chief Secretary to the District Collector, police and Greater Cochin Development Authority, the administrative machinery was used for a private individual, Mr. Janeesh alleged, while speaking to reporters here.

He said such actions created an opportunity for a private party to make substantial financial gains and, therefore, it was meaningless to argue that the government had suffered no loss.

World.title: NIA arrests an accused in Tronglaobi IED attack case
World.content:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested an accused in connection with the Improvised Explosive Device (IED) attack at a residential house in Tronglaobi Awang Leikai in Manipur’s Moirang on April 7.

S. Palal Thadou allegedly handled finances for UKNA, a Kuki insurgent group that is not engaged in peace talks with the government. He was first arrested on July 23 by the Assam Rifles and the Churachandpur police.

Two minor children were killed and another person was injured in the Moirang incident when unknown militants launched an explosive device from a hillside towards Tronglaobi Awang Leikai. The case was initially registered at the Moirang police station in Bishnupur district.

“The explosion struck the residential wall of a house, causing serious injuries to three family members, including two minor children who later succumbed to their injuries. An unexploded improvised RPG (rocket-propelled grenade) was also recovered near the site,” the NIA said.

The investigation was subsequently taken over by the NIA, which re-registered the case on April 23. “During the course of the investigation, the involvement of accused S. Palal Thadou has surfaced in the commission of the offence,” the agency said.

The agency said Thadou was initially arrested by the Churachandpur police in one case, following which Bishnupur police also arrested him in another case.

The NIA has secured 10-day custody of the accused from a special court in Imphal to probe “the larger conspiracy behind the terror act”, making him the first accused to be arrested in the case.

World.title: Free tanker supply to continue for another week: GVMC Chief
World.content:
Amid the ongoing drinking water supply crisis, Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) Commissioner Ketan Garg conducted a surprise inspection of the Town Service Reservoir (TSR) and reviewed water storage levels, tanker filling points and the overall supply system, on Wednesday. He enquired about the number of tankers supplied free of cost so far and the areas to which they had been deployed.

Mr. Garg directed officials to continue intensive field-level monitoring until the situation returns completely to normal. He specifically instructed that free water supply through GVMC tankers be continued for another week in water-stressed areas to ensure that residents do not face any inconvenience.

During the inspection, Mr Garg thoroughly examined records relating to tanker requests received through the ‘Dial-A-Tanker’ service and the GVMC website, including completed deliveries and pending bookings. To personally verify the service delivery mechanism, the Commissioner spoke over the phone with a consumer named Ramu and expressed satisfaction. He directed officials to ensure the tanker distribution is carried out in a transparent manner.

Mr. Garg said that the water supply situation in the city was gradually easing following the special action plan implemented by the corporation.

He added that water levels in the Yeleru, Godavari, Thatipudi, Raiwada, Mehadri Gedda, Mudasarlova and Gambheeram reservoirs, as well as the Gosthani and Sarada river sources, were satisfactory. At present, these sources are supplying a total of 84.44 MGD (383.86 MLD) of water to GVMC.

He further stated that upon completion of the desilting works related to the Raiwada water supply system, there is scope to augment the city’s water supply by approximately 3 MGD.

The Commissioner said that the situation had improved significantly over the past few days due to coordinated measures.

Superintending Engineer (Water Supply) Pallamraju, Executive Engineer Muralikrishna and other officials were present.

Meanwhile, in view of the construction of two new railway tracks by the Railway Department within Visakhapatnam city limits, the GVMC will be systematically shifting the corporation’s water supply pipelines falling within the railway track expansion areas ensuring that neither the railway works nor water supply to the public is affected.

Mr. Ketan Garg said that that GVMC water supply pipelines, including bulk and domestic water connection pipelines, have been identified at 29 points across eight locations falling within the railway track expansion areas. Of these, four pipelines are located at Ramamurthy Panthulupeta, 12 near NAD New Road, four at Marripalem and two in the Gajuwaka area. GVMC will prepare necessary technical plans for shifting the pipelines and expedite the works in coordination with the Railways.

World.title: Woman dies after falling into crater; villagers launch flash protest seeking action against PWD officers
World.content:
Residents protested after a woman fell into a huge pit dug for bridge repairs in Hosur in Bailhongal taluk in Belagavi district on Wednesday.

Mallavva Suresh Viveki, 44, had gone for a walk when she accidentally fell into the crater. It was a deep reed dug for the construction of a column at the site of the bridge on the Bailahongal-Munavalli main road.

She drowned in the water below. Protestors took the dead body to the main road and blocked it for over an hour. They alleged that deep embankments were left open during construction, and water had accumulated in them. No barricades, barriers, warning signs, and night-visible safety systems were installed to warn commuters, they said.

They said they had warned the contractor several times, but no action was taken to close the dangerous embankments or prevent the public from going near it. They sought action against the contractor and the PWD officers in charge of the project.

Later, the police intervened in the matter. They called the PWD officers to the police station and made them assure action against those found guilty. The villagers dispersed after the assurance.

Somalingappa Mellikeri, Fakiragouda Siddanagouda, Gurupada Kalli, Madivalappa Chalakoppa, Shanmukha Shirennavar, Basavaraj Viveki, and others were present at the protest site.

World.title: Jagan asks party leaders to expose govt.’s failures
World.content:
YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has asked party legislators to raise issues of public interest during the ensuing Legislative Assembly session, while highlighting the failures of the government.

Addressing the YSRCP Legislative Party members here on Wednesday, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy alleged that the government was unwilling to accord Leader of Opposition status to the YSRCP, the principal opposition party, with an intention to gag its voice.

The former Chief Minister said he would raise the issues through the media to present the other side of the story to the people. He asked the legislators to use the party’s strength in the Legislative Council to act as the voice of the people.

On the DSC issue, he said the party had staged 10 forms of protests over the past 74 days and placed “evidence” to substantiate its allegations. He said the party had also exposed the alleged leakage and outsourcing scandals and irregularities in the sports quota, demanded a CBI inquiry, and questioned the alleged involvement of HRD Minister Nara Lokesh.

Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy asked the legislators to raise the issues of fee reimbursement and Vasathi Deevena, alleging that students were being severely affected by pending bills. He said dues had accumulated for 13 quarters to more than ₹9,100 crore under fee reimbursement and ₹3,300 crore under Vasathi Deevena, while the government had released only ₹2,900 crore. He asked the legislators to pursue the issue in the House and insist on a discussion.

On farmers’ issues, he asked the party legislators to raise their voice over lack of MSP for crops, inadequate availability of water and suspension of free crop insurance, which, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said, had pushed farmers into distress.

He also criticised the provision of viability gap funding (VGF) for public-private partnership projects and other concessions to private players, saying they would ultimately burden the people. The government's alleged plans to privatise public services should be strongly questioned, he said.

The YSRCP chief asked the legislators to raise the repeal of the Disha Bill and cases filed against BCs. He alleged that cases were being filed unjustly and vindictively against those questioning the government, and described the cases against leaders such as Chintada Ravi and Mustafa as fabricated.

The legislators should also highlight the junior doctors' strike, dissatisfaction among employees and the grievances of women, youth, the unemployed and other sections of society, he said.

Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy asked the legislators to attend the the Assembly sessions fully prepared with relevant data and effectively expose the government's failures.

World.title: APGDA says 3% annual stipend hike for junior doctors an insult to medical fraternity
World.content:
The State government has to increase the stipend of junior doctors by 15% once every two years, and because it is overdue for more than seven months, the junior doctors have spilled on to the streets, says D. Jayadheer Babu, A.P. Government Doctors’ Association (APGDA) State president.

Announcing the APGDA’s support for the A.P. Junior Doctors’ Association’s (APJUDA) demands, Dr. Jayadheer Babu said the government was trying to project the protesting doctors in a bad light. Moreover, the Health Department had insulted the whole medical fraternity by proposing an annual hike of 3%, he said, while participating in a protest in Visakhapatnam.

“The junior doctors’ demands for rising the biannual stipend hike from 15% to 30% is genuine and valid. They have been waiting since January this year for the hike. Instead of timely increments, the State government is instead offering a token increase of 3% annually. How is this justified?” he asked, demanding Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s response and Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav’s decision on the matter.

Junior doctors said in 2024, too, they had to stage protests for implementation of the hike. “Inflation is rising, rents are increasing and so is the workload. The inflation rate in A.P. is higher than that of the country,” said Ranjeet Dhabable, APJUDA treasurer. He also added that whenever they were on night shifts, they had to work continuously for 36 hours.

In response to the Health Department’s claim that they did not receive any official representation from APJUDA until July 17, Dr. Ranjeet Dhabale said they made multiple representations and all of them were available in the public domain.

On Wednesday, the third day of their strike, non-emergency services were withdrawn completely in the government teaching hospitals as interns, junior residents, super-speciality post-graduates, senior residents participated in the strike. Some of them also held relay hunger strike between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m.

World.title: Man held for impersonation during property transfer
World.content:
Officers from the Market Police Station arrested a 75-year-old man on charges of impersonation and fraud during a property transaction.

Ramachandra Venkatesh Deshpande, 75, of Patil Galli, Kotabagi, Hukkeri taluk, faces charges of claiming to be the owner of the property who died long ago and allegedly trying to sell it.

A case was registered based on the complaint filed by Srishail Dattatrey Guruv, 29, of Topinakatti village.

According to the police, the complainant’s grandfather, Mashanu Jayappa Gurav, and his brothers purchased 7 acres 32 guntas of land in Badala Ankalgi village from Chidambar Sripad Kulkarni and Ramesh Digambar Kulkarni in 1998.

“Several years after the death of the original owner, the accused sold it to another party. The accused went to the Belagavi sub-registrar’s office, took a photo on the office webcam and gave his thumb impressions. He allegedly cheated the complainant by entering into an agreement to sell the property to another person, who is the buyer and other accused in the case,” the police said.

Search for Vinod Deshpande, another of the accused, and others is on.

A team led by inspector J.M. Kamirchi, sub-inspector H.L. Kerur and staff conducted the investigation. Police Commissioner Borase Bhushan Gulabrao and Deputy Commissioners of Police Narayan Baramani and Niranjan Raje Urs have congratulated the team.

World.title: Special flight operations begin at Bhogapuram Airport
World.content:
A special flight carrying Bheemunipatnam MLA Ganta Srinivasa Rao and Anakapalli MP C.M. Ramesh from New Delhi landed at the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport in Bhogapuram on Wednesday, marking the beginning of special flight operations ahead of the scheduled launch of regular services from August 17.

The airport witnessed increased activity as Minister Satya Kumar, MLA Kamineni Srinivas and former MP K.V.P. Ramachandra Rao, who were travelling on another special flight, also happened landed at the airport.

With international-standard facilities being developed for aircraft take-offs and landings, the Bhogapuram airport is expected to emerge as a major growth engine for North Andhra.

World.title: 'We aspire for it to grow': Turkiye's Erdogan eyes expansion of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
World.content:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Wednesday that he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, aimed at stabilising a region wracked by conflict.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Iran war, which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily. “Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Cairo has robust military cooperation with Ankara, but has given no indication it intends to sign up to the new security alliance, which contains a Nato-style clause saying any attack on one would be seen as an attack on all.

The five-month US-Iran war has upended the security architecture in the region and forced a rethink of decades of conventional wisdom rooted in US military supremacy.

Erdogan said the pact emerged out of the “new circumstances” in the Middle East with regional players seeking to assume greater responsibility for their own security and stability.

“Regional issues should be resolved by regional actors, and with this action, we consider that we have taken a first step toward achieving that goal,” he told the Saudi-owned newspaper.

“Resolving regional issues must be carried out away from formulas imposed from the outside. We know very well that solutions imported from abroad only bring disasters.”

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

On Monday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirmed that the defence pact was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

Israel ‘removing Palestine’ from world agenda

Erdogan also accused the Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu of seeking to “remove Palestine” from the world’s agenda.

“The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region,” Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart, Mahmoud Abbas.

“No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people’s hearts as they try to destroy it,” he stressed, vowing Turkiye would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state.

A strong advocate of the Palestinian cause, Erdogan has repeatedly lambasted Netanyahu’s government, accusing the Israeli prime minister of committing “genocide” in Gaza and of pursuing expansionist policies in the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond.

Abbas arrived in Ankara on Tuesday accompanied by his diplomatic adviser Majdi Khalidi, intelligence chief Majed Faraj and senior Palestinian official Ziad Abu Amr.

He met Erdogan on Wednesday with the pair discussing developments in the region in talks the Palestinian leader described as “important and fruitful”.

“I hope the decision to hold legislative and presidential elections in Palestine after a long time will bring good fortune … [and] will advance the reconciliation process,” Erdogan said, in a nod to the historic rivalry between Abbas’ Fatah movement and Gaza’s Hamas rulers.

Abbas also hailed the defence pact between Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad, saying it was “of utmost importance” and expressing hope it would help enhance security and stability in the region.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Re0.94, raises high-speed diesel by Re0.54
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.94 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.54 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs324.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.79 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 13 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: After death of 3 Pakistani sailors, FO says Islamabad will implement maritime coalition 'in full earnest'
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday that Pakistan, as a signatory to the recently announced multinational maritime defence coalition, would implement its commitments “in full earnest”.

The statement comes following the deaths of three Pakistani sailors in Houthi strikes on a Saudi cargo ship on Tuesday.

Last month, Riyadh unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, Turkiye and Egypt, backed the coalition in a joint statement.

Answering questions at a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi elaborated that Pakistan was a signatory of the recent joint statement supporting a multinational maritime defence coalition, led by Saudi Arabia, to protect shipping and energy supply routes.

“Pakistan is a signatory to this maritime coalition communique and we will implement it with full earnest,” Andrabi said, adding that the country was engaged with the Saudi authorities in this regard.

Andrabi further said that on the directions of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Pakistan was ascertaining the details of the agreement.

In his opening statement, the FO also said that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s visit to Iran was aimed at discussing bilateral relations, security-related matters and regional developments, particularly peace and stability in the region.

He said Naqvi — who arrived in Tehran on Tuesday — was holding meetings with senior Iranian officials.

He added that the visit provides the two countries the opportunity to discuss “bilateral relations, security-related matters, and regional development, with a particular focus on efforts to promote peace, stability, and constructive engagement amongst the parties in the region and regional developments”.

Naqvi was received in Tehran by his Iranian counterpart, Eskandar Momeni, and later held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Iranian media reported.

A diplomatic source had told Dawn from Tehran that the principal objective of Naqvi’s visit was to follow up on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and Pakistan’s mediation bet­­w­een Iran and the US.

Speaking further on Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the US and Iran, Andrabi reiterated that Pakistan remained engaged alongside “brotherly states” in “sincere efforts” to work towards a resolution to the crisis.

“Pakistan is making all-out efforts to bring the two parties to the negotiating table and the Islamabad MoU and pave the way for peace and stability in the region,” he said.

He also warned that Pakistan would continue to “offset spoilers using direct and indirect channels” and ensure the continuation of constructive dialogue to resolve outstanding issues.

During the Q&A session, responding to a question regarding the status of the Islamabad MoU, the spokesperson said, “Whenever the rationality for dialogue will overcome the logic of escalation, the template for peace is provided in the Islamabad MoU and Pakistan-Qatar joint statement.”

The current deadline for the 60-day period for US-Iran negotiations under the Islamabad MoU is Aug 17. Andrabi, however, noted that this deadline “can always be extended” if there is the intention to hold dialogue.

“Even then, five days still remain, so we are not closing the chapter,” he added. “But we hope that even if the deadline is not implemented, the extension will take place eventually and the parties will revert to dialogue.”

Asked about the basis for Pakistan’s continued optimism amid the US-Iran conflict, the spokesperson said, “As a mediator and facilitator of talks, we remain optimistic that a solution is in sight.”

He pointed out that during the conflict, the countries had cycled through periods of heightened escalation followed by relative calm and eventual dialogue. He termed this “the natural progression of any armed conflict of international significance”.

“We are not discouraged by escalations, as much as we do not get overly optimistic when there is a period of calm,” he said, while highlighting Pakistan’s sustained engagement with the parties to resolve the conflict.

The country would continue its engagement with optimism “that ought to be there in any credible facilitator and mediator”, he added.

Makkah pact reflects ‘resolve for sharing burden of regional peace’

The FO spokesperson also spoke of the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which he said was “highlight of the week”.

The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

He said the agreement reflected the three nations’ “commitment to further strengthen their collective security, promoting peace security and promoting peace security and stability in the region and beyond”.

He said the agreement reflected the “long-standing brotherly relations” among the three countries and “displays our resolve for sharing the burden of regional peace and security”.

“The agreement is purely defensive in nature and allows unified efforts to confront threats and security challenges to the member states,” Andrabi added, recalling Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s statement congratulating the nation on the agreement on August 10, wherein he held the agreement was defensive in nature and not against any country.

Responding to a question, he noted that while the agreement was open to other countries, he was not “particularly aware” of which specific countries may join it in the future. He also said that he was not aware of any consultations with the US and China regarding the agreement, calling this “a matter of diplomatic exchange”, but noted that channels of communication with both countries remained open.

FO rejects Indian MEA’s ‘baseless’ remarks on AJK

When asked about the Indian Ministry of External Affairs’ recent remarks regarding alleged human rights abuses in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), the FO spokesperson rejected the “baseless” statement. The region has been gripped by unrest since early June as elections are also being held.

“India’s professed concerns for human rights in AJK are disingenuous given its own well-documented record for repression in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, including excessive use of force, arbitrary detention, suppression of political freedom and sweeping powers under the draconian laws enacted there.”

He added that India’s “politicisation” of developments in AJK was “misleading and cannot divert attention from the stark realities in Indian illegally occupied Kashmir”.

“Pakistan remains fully committed to the protection of fundamental rights and the democratic freedom of AJK,” he said.

He added that rather than making such statements over AJK, India would be “well advised to honour commitments made by its founding fathers and uphold the right of the people of Indian illegally occupied Jammu and Kashmir to freely determine their future through a United Nations plebiscite in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions”.

World.title: Met Office forecasts fresh rain spell for upper, central parts of country from Aug 13-15
World.content:
The upper and central parts of the country are set to receive a fresh spell of monsoon rains from August 13 to 15, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said on Wednesday.

In an advisory, the Met Office said monsoon currents were penetrating the upper parts of the country along with a westerly wave.

In Kashmir, it forecast rain accompanied by wind and thundershowers in Neelum Valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur. In Gilgit-Baltistan, the Met Office predicted rain in Diamir, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar.

In upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Malakand, Shangla, Battagram, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Galiyat, Buner, Bajaur, Mohmand, Peshawar, Nowshera, Mardan, Swabi, Haripur, Kurram and Khyber are expected to receive rain.

In northeast Punjab, rainfall was predicted in Murree, Sialkot, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Lahore, Kasur, Sheikhupura and Nankana Sahib from the night of August 12 to August 15, with occasional gaps.

Rain-wind and thundershowers, with a few heavy falls, are also expected in Islamabad, Rawalpindi and the Pothohar region from the night of August 13 to August 15, with occasional gaps.

In Sargodha, Faisalabad, Jhang, Toba Tek Singh, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Noorpur Thal, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Zhob, Barkhan and Musakhel, the Met Office predicted rainfall from August 12 to 15.

Meanwhile, in Sindh, partly cloudy to cloudy weather is expected in the southeastern and coastal areas, with chances of rain-wind/thundershowers in Tharparkar, Umerkot and Sanghar districts on August 12 and 13.

Elsewhere in Sindh, hot and humid weather is expected to persist.

The Met Office warned of urban flooding in low-lying areas of Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Mardan, Swabi, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot and Lahore during the forecast period.

It also indicated the possibility of landslides in vulnerable areas of upper KP, including Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Buner, Battagram, Mansehra, Haripur and Abbottabad, as well as in GB, Murree, Galiyat and Kashmir.

The Met Office advised tourists to exercise caution, while farmers were urged to manage crop activities in accordance with weather conditions.

According to the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), 155 people have lost their lives and 460 have been injured in rain-related incidents in the current monsoon season.

Monsoon rains fall across the region from June to September, offering respite from the summer heat and are crucial to replenishing water supplies.

However, heavy downpours also trigger deadly floods, landslides and displacement, particularly in vulnerable, poorly drained, or densely populated areas.

World.title: AJK polls: Rathore’s LA-17 Haveli victory disputed, local PML-N announces indefinite strike
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: A controversy emerged on Wednesday after the returning officer (RO) issued Form 27 declaring PPP’s Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, the sitting AJK prime minister, the winner from LA-17 (Haveli), despite rival PML-N candidate Engineer Mohsin Aziz being assured that the form would not be issued until the Election Commission took up his complaint.

The development triggered fresh tensions in Haveli district, where PML-N workers announced a complete shutter-down strike and protest from Thursday (August 13) for an indefinite period.

At a meeting in Forward Kahuta, chaired by PML-N Haveli president Syed Abid Bukhari, participants demanded that the Election Commission open all polling bags from LA-17, order a recount and determine the result on the basis of the original results issued by presiding officers at the polling stations.

They warned that the scope of the protest would be expanded if the demand was not accepted.

Polling in the constituency had been held on Monday amid serious allegations and counter-allegations of rigging by all three major contestants — PM Rathore of PPP, PML-N’s Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed.

Late on Monday evening, thousands of Aziz’s supporters gathered at the district courts, claiming that the results provided to polling agents by presiding officers on Form 24 showed their candidate leading Rathore by more than 8,000 votes, but that the RO was subsequently preparing the result in favour of the prime minister.

There were also reports of some people being injured during the demonstration.

The protest ended on Tuesday after Aziz said in a video message that the RO had given him a written undertaking that Form 27 would not be issued until the Election Commission in Muzaffarabad decided his claim.

On Tuesday, Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal had told Dawn that the Commission would take a decision after the polling bags and relevant election records reached its office. He had reportedly given a similar assurance to Aziz over the phone.

The DRO, Waheed Mughal, and RO, Asheer Chughtai, both members of the subordinate judiciary, were evacuated from their offices in Forward Kahuta along with the polling bags with the help of the army’s Quick Response Force (QRF). They reached Muzaffarabad by midnight.

However, the RO subsequently issued Form 27 after midnight, dated August 11, declaring Rathore the winner with 33,872 votes. Aziz secured 32,354 votes, followed by Saeed with 12,538 and IPP candidate Amir Nazir Chaudhry with 5,405.

Hours later, PM Rathore said on X that his “remarkable victory had been officially notified”.

“LA-17 has spoken. I thank the people of Haveli and again pledge to serve them now and forever. I’m grateful to my party leadership, specially, Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Adi Faryal Talpur, for their trust, guidance and unending support amid every challenge we have faced,” he wrote.

The issuance of Form 27, however, failed to settle the dispute, with reports from Haveli suggesting that tensions were rising again.

In a video message recorded in Muzaffarabad, Aziz reiterated his allegation that the Form 24s handed to polling agents of all nine participating candidates contained the genuine results, while different figures were subsequently taken into consideration by the RO.

He offered to have just two polling bags, rather than all of them, opened from areas where he alleged the results had been changed. If his allegation proved to be wrong, he said, he would apologise and congratulate Rathore.

“If Faisal Rathore has won, why is he afraid of opening of polling bags and a subsequent recount?” he asked.

Aziz also claimed that the Election Act, 2020, made it obligatory for the RO to open polling bags following a complaint by any candidate. He said that when they asked Chughtai to take the step, the RO maintained that he was unaware of the provision and did not have a copy of the Act with him.

On Wednesday, senior lawyers Raja Sajjad Ahmed and Chaudhry Ghulam Nabi submitted an application to the chief election commissioner, seeking a recount of votes polled in LA-17 over alleged tampering with the results.

The Election Commission announced that it would take up the matter at 10am on Thursday.

In a post on X, PML-N leader and federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry called for a transparent investigation into the rigging complaint filed by Aziz, saying he hoped the Election Commission would address the allegations regarding the Haveli constituency on merit.

Aziz, however, said he had little hope from the commission after what he described as its failure to prevent the issuance of the “unlawful Form 27”.

“I will take my case to the people’s court apart from the superior judiciary,” he said.

Meanwhile, Saeed also alleged tampering with his results and called for a recount. He claimed that he had won at nine polling stations, but the votes secured by him there had not been included in his tally and had instead been added to that of Rathore.

PPP calls polls ‘rigged and violent’

Against this backdrop, the PPP also criticised the conduct of the AJK elections, with a high-level meeting of the party in Islamabad describing the polls as “rigged and violent” and expressing serious concern over the role of the AJK Election Commission.

The meeting, chaired by PPP Women’s Wing president and AJK affairs in-charge Faryal Talpur, also criticised the phase-wise conduct of the elections and demanded the immediate completion of polling in the remaining two districts of the third phase and seven constituencies of Poonch so that the Legislative Assembly could be fully constituted.

The participants raised questions over the suspension of internet services, shortages of polling material and staff at some polling stations, and alleged inadequate security arrangements.

Talpur said the PPP was the representative party of the people of AJK and had continued to enjoy strong public support despite challenging circumstances.

On the other hand, Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the PML-N had secured a clear lead in the elections and would have 24 general seats, with another six reserved seats, taking its strength to 30.

In his post on X, he said the AJK Assembly session would be convened next week for the swearing-in of members and election of reserved seats, followed by elections for the speaker and prime minister.

Chaudhry described the elections as free, fair and credible, saying there had been “zero tolerance” for misconduct or rigging. He cited the arrest of a candidate in LA-6 (Mirpur) for taking away a ballot box from a polling station as an example of action against electoral misconduct.

World.title: Awaam Pakistan calls ECP delisting ‘unwarranted’, seeks urgent hearing
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Headed by former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi, Awaam Pakistan has challenged the Election Commission of Pakistan’s (ECP) decision to delist the party over its alleged failure to hold intra-party elections, calling the move “arbitrary, unwarranted and unprecedented”.

In a letter to Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja dated August 12, 2026, Abbasi, who is also the party’s president, said Awaam Pakistan had been “taken by surprise” by an ECP notification issued on August 7. The notification cited an ECP order dated Aug 3, 2026, in a case titled “Non-Conduct of intra-party election by Awaam Pakistan”.

Abbasi said the party had conducted intra-party elections for both the National General Council and national office-bearers between March 26 and April 2, 2026. He said the polls were held within the extension granted by the ECP in its decision of January 2026.

“The results of the intra-party election and detailed documentation were submitted to the ECP on April 6, 2026,” the letter said.

He added that 12,846 party members participated in the exercise, which was “democratic, transparent, and in full compliance with the Elections Act, 2017.”

Terming the delisting “in contradiction of the record available with the ECP”, Abbasi said the action was taken “without an opportunity to be heard by the Election Commission”.

“We request an urgent hearing by the commission so that we can clarify our position,” he wrote.

While Article 17 of the Constitution guarantees the right to form political parties, enlistment with the ECP is a legal requirement for obtaining an election symbol to contest polls.

Under Section 202 of the Elections Act, 2017, a party must apply for enlistment within 30 days of formation. The application must include certified results of intra-party elections, a copy of the party constitution, details of funding sources, a membership list of at least 2,000 members with CNICs and thumb impressions, and proof of payment of a Rs200,000 non-refundable fee.

Section 208 empowers the ECP to issue a show-cause notice or impose a fine of up to Rs200,000 on a party that fails to hold intra-party elections within the prescribed timeframe. In case of continued non-compliance, the commission may cancel the party’s enlistment.

Under Section 202(6), a party whose enlistment is refused or cancelled may file an appeal in the Supreme Court within 30 days.

Awaam Pakistan was launched by Abbasi in 2024 after he parted ways with PML-N. The party contested the February 8, 2024, general elections but did not win any National Assembly seat. It has since sought to position itself as an alternative centrist platform.

With the latest notification, Awaam Pakistan stands delisted “accordingly”, according to the ECP order of August 3. The delisting means the party will not be eligible to contest elections under its name and election symbol unless it is re-registered.

World.title: 18 terrorists killed in Balochistan’s Surab district: ISPR
World.content:
At least 18 terrorists were killed in Balochistan’s Surab district, including eight in a premature detonation, the military’s media wing said on Wednesday.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said eight terrorists were killed when an “under preparation” vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated.

“An under preparation vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated while being prepared by terrorists affiliated with Fitna Al Hindustan in Surab district of Balochistan.”

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The military’s media wing added that multiple terrorists were also injured in the explosion.

However, the blast also killed three civilians in the area after a “secondary detonation of other explosives stored there”.

Following the explosion, a contingent of security forces and police reached the incident site and “launched a comprehensive joint clearance operation to track down the perpetrators and facilitators”.

Elaborating further, the military said security forces “proactively detected the movement of fleeing terrorists, effectively engaging and neutralising ten more”.

“In total, 18 terrorists affiliated with Fitna Al Hindustan have been eliminated in these incidents so far,” said the ISPR, adding that during the exchange of fire, two soldiers were injured.

“Sanitisation operations continue in the area to eliminate any remaining terrorists.

“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision ‘Azm e Istehkam’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” concluded the ISPR.

Security forces killed 15 terrorists in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in several areas of Balochistan, state media reported last week.

State-run Pakistan TV, citing sources, reported that the IBOs were carried out in Mastung, Bolan, Washuk, Awaran, Sibi, Khuzdar, Harnai, and Nushki under Operation Raddul Fitna 3, adding that weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the dead terrorists.

“The operations severely damaged the khawarij network and restricted their movement,” Pakistan TV said. Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on July 31, the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan in the country last month.

The overall death toll increased by 241pc in Balochistan, from 109 in June to 372 in July, the report said.

Security personnel deaths in Balochistan increased from six in June to 62 in July, representing a rise of 933pc. Terrorist deaths rose from 75 to 238, while civilian deaths increased by 93pc, from 28 to 54. Eighteen members of peace committees were also killed in the province.

World.title: California Senate unanimously backs stronger Pakistan-US ties
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The California State Senate has unanimously passed a resolution celebrating the “enduring relationship” between Pakistan and the United States and recognising the “significant contributions” of Pakistani-Americans to the state’s economy, culture and social fabric.

The resolution, presented by Senator Melissa Hurtado, highlighted the “pivotal role” played by Pakistani-Americans in California and commended their achievements across diverse fields. It also urged all Californians to join in celebrating the friendly relations between the two countries.

The resolution’s language goes beyond a routine recognition of the Pakistani-American community, placing its contributions alongside California’s relationship with Pakistan and calling for broader public recognition of the friendship between the two countries.

Pakistan’s Ambassador to the United States, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, also visited California during this process and held meetings with state lawmakers to expand political and economic engagement between Pakistan and the state.

The California State Assembly also adopted a resolution supporting stronger relations with Pakistan. It called for promoting the role of Pakistani-American businesses and investors in advancing economic cooperation between Pakistan and California.

Ambassador Sheikh welcomed the Senate resolution and praised Senator Hurtado for her leadership. He said that Pakistan remained committed to “deepening people-to-people ties” and building on what he described as the “current positive trajectory” in Pakistan-US relations.

The ambassador also held talks with Senator Eloise Gomez on expanding trade, investment and economic cooperation between Pakistan and the United States. Gomez praised Pakistan’s role in promoting regional peace and stability, while Sheikh invited her to visit Pakistan.

He later hosted a working lunch for Assembly member Matt Haney and Assemblywoman Sharon Quirk-Silva. The discussions covered bilateral cooperation, with the ambassador inviting both lawmakers to visit Pakistan.

The Council of Pakistan, led by Dr Imran Sharief, also played a role in efforts leading to the passage of the Senate resolution.

The California resolutions come at a time when Pakistan is seeking to strengthen economic and political engagement with the United States while expanding ties with individual US states.

For Pakistan, the California initiative is significant not only because of its explicit celebration of the “enduring relationship” between the two countries, but also because it widens the role of the Pakistani-American community in expanding political and economic ties between Pakistan and the United States.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.
